तस्माच्छ्रुतीनां प्रपञ्चविषयेऽनादरादेव तदुत्पत्तिक्रमस्यैकविधत्वेन वर्णने न यत्नः ।
Therefore, since the Śrutis have no real interest in the phenomenal world, they make no effort to describe the order of its creation in a uniform manner.
तदुत्पत्तिविषये श्रुतीनां विगानदर्शनादेव प्रपञ्चनिषेध एव श्रुतीनां नैर्भर्यं न तदुत्पत्ताविति ज्ञेयम् ।
From the very observation of discrepancies among the Śrutis regarding the creation of the world, it is to be understood that the full weight of the Śrutis lies in negating the world, and not in establishing its creation.
254 · श्रुत्युक्तक्रमेण जगदुत्पत्तिकथने सूत्रकारभाष्यकृतोरभिप्रायः
यदपि सूत्रभाष्यकृतौ द्वितीयाध्याये जगदुत्पत्तिप्रतिपादकश्रुतिवाक्यानां परस्परविरोधं परिहरन्तौ तैत्तिरीयोक्तसृष्टिक्रम एव सर्वौपनिषदामर्थ इति वर्णितवन्तौ, तन्मन्दाधिकारिसमाधानार्थमिति ज्ञेयम् ।
And as for the fact that the author of the Sūtras and the author of the Bhāṣya, while resolving the mutual contradiction among scriptural passages expounding world-creation in the second chapter, described that the order of creation stated in the Taittirīya alone is the sense of all Upaniṣads, that should be understood as intended merely for satisfying aspirants of dull capacity.
पूर्वं वर्णितमुत्पत्तिवाक्यानां वस्तुभूतमभिप्रायमवगन्तुमसमर्था मन्दजिज्ञासवः परस्परविरुद्धानि वाक्यानि दृष्ट्वा भ्रान्ता मा भूवन्निति सूत्रभाष्यकृतौ सर्वोपनिषदामाकाशादिक्रमेणैव जगदुत्पत्तौ तात्पर्यमिति प्रदर्शयामासतुः ।
Lest dull seekers—unable to grasp the real intention behind the creation passages explained earlier—should become confused upon seeing mutually conflicting statements, the Sūtrakāra and the Bhāṣyakāra demonstrated that the purport of all Upaniṣads lies in the world's origin being in the order of space and so forth.
किञ्च वेदान्तविचारेण यथार्थज्ञानमलभमानस्य लयचिन्तनार्थमपि श्रुतीनां वैमत्यपरिहारेण विवक्षितो जगदुत्पत्तिक्रमः सूत्रभाष्यकृद्भ्यां प्रदर्शितः ।1
Furthermore, for one who does not attain true knowledge merely through inquiry into Vedānta, the intended order of cosmic creation was also presented by the Sūtrakāra and the Bhāṣyakāra by resolving the apparent discrepancies among the scriptures, in order to facilitate meditation on cosmic dissolution (*laya-cintana*).
टिप्पणी
1.
सूत्रशब्देन व्यासकृतब्रह्मसूत्रम्, भाष्यशब्देन श्रीशङ्करभगवत्पादभाष्यं च ग्राह्यम् ।
By the word 'sūtra', the *Brahmasūtra* composed by Vyāsa is to be understood, and by the word 'bhāṣya', the commentary of Śrī Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda.
येन क्रमेणोत्पत्तिस्तद्विपरीतक्रमेण जगतो लयश्चिन्तनीयः ।
In whichever order creation occurs, in the reverse of that order the dissolution of the world should be meditated upon.
तथा लयचिन्टनेनाद्वितीये ब्रह्मणि बुद्धिः स्थिरा भवेत् ।
Thus, through meditation on cosmic dissolution, the mind becomes steady in non-dual Brahman.
सोऽयं लयचिन्तनप्रकारः वार्तिककारैः सुरेश्वराचार्यैः पञ्चीकरणाख्यग्रन्थे वर्णितः ।
This method of meditation on cosmic dissolution has been described by the Vārttikakāra Sureśvarācārya in the text named *Pañcīkaraṇa* (i.e. *Pañcīkaraṇa-vārttika*).
अस्य ग्रन्थस्य उत्तमाधिकारिविषयत्वाद्यद्यपि जगदुत्पत्तिलयक्रमवर्णनस्य नात्रावसरस्तथापि सागररूपत्वादस्य ग्रन्थस्य मन्दानुग्रहाय सङ्क्षेपतः स उच्यते ।
Although there is no strict occasion here to describe the sequence of the world's creation and dissolution—since this treatise is meant for the highest class of aspirants—nevertheless, because this work has the nature of an ocean (encompassing all aspects), that sequence is briefly stated out of compassion for dull seekers.
असङ्गत्वादक्रियत्वाच्च शुद्धब्रह्मणः सकाशाज्जगदुत्पत्त्यादिकं न सङ्गच्छते ।
Because pure Brahman is unattached and actionless, the creation and other phenomena of the universe cannot logically proceed directly from It.
किन्तु मायाविशिष्टशबलब्रह्मणः सकाशाज्जगदुत्पद्यते ।
Rather, the world is produced from Brahman qualified by *māyā* (i.e. *śabala-brahman*).
तस्मान्मायेश्वरयोः स्वरूपं प्रतिपाद्यते ।
Therefore, the essential nature of *māyā* and *īśvara* is now expounded.
श्रुत्युक्तोत्पत्तिक्रमनिरूपणम्॥ २५५–२७२ ॥
प्रसङ्गान्मायास्वरूपप्रतिपादनम्॥ २५५–२६० ॥
255 · मायास्वरूपं
जीवेश्वरादिविभागशून्यशुद्धचैतन्याश्रिता माया ।
Māyā rests upon pure consciousness, which is devoid of divisions such as jīva and Īśvara.
इयम् उत्पत्तिरहितत्वात् अनादिः ।
Since it is devoid of origin, it is beginningless.
तस्याः उत्पत्त्यङ्गीकारे पुत्रात् पितुरुत्पत्तिकथनस्य इव मायाकार्यात् प्रपञ्चात् मायोत्पत्तिकथनम् असङ्गतं भवेत् ।
If its origin were admitted, then stating that Māyā arises from the world—which is itself Māyā's effect—would be as absurd as saying that a father is born from his son.
तस्मात् चैतन्यात् मायोत्पत्तिः वक्तव्या ।
Therefore, one would have to say that Māyā originates from consciousness.
तथा सति जीवत्वेश्वरत्वयोः मायाकार्यत्वात् न जीवचेतनात् न वा ईश्वरचेतनात् मायोत्पत्तिः भवेत् ।
That being the case, since jīva-hood and Īśvara-hood are themselves effects of Māyā, Māyā cannot originate either from the jīva-consciousness or from the Īśvara-consciousness.
जीवेश्वरसिद्धौ तत्सकाशान्मायोत्पत्तिः मायासिद्धौ जीवेश्वरसिद्धिरित्यन्योन्याश्रयप्रसङ्गात् ।
For it would lead to mutual dependence: if jīva and Īśvara are established, Māyā originates from them; and if Māyā is established, jīva and Īśvara are established.
शुद्धचैतन्यं तु असङ्गमक्रियम् अविकारि च ।
Pure consciousness, however, is unattached, actionless, and changeless.
तस्मात् मायोत्पत्त्यङ्गीकारे शुद्धचैतन्यं विकारि भवेत् ।
Therefore, if the origin of Māyā were accepted, pure consciousness would become mutable.
किञ्च यदि शुद्धचैतन्यात् मायोत्पत्तिः उच्यते तर्हि मोक्षदशायां शुद्धचैतन्यस्य सत्त्वात् पुनः मायोत्पत्तिप्रसङ्गः स्यात् ।
Furthermore, if the origin of Māyā from pure consciousness is asserted, then since pure consciousness remains in the state of *mokṣa*, there would arise the unwelcome possibility of Māyā being born again.
मोक्षसाधनवैयर्थ्यं च स्यात् ।
And the means to liberation would become futile.
तस्मात् मायोत्पत्तिरहिता ; अत एव च अनादिः ।
Therefore, Māyā is devoid of origin; and for this very reason, it is beginningless.
सा च एका एव ।
And it is only one.
ज्ञाननाश्यत्वात् सान्ता च ।
And because it is destructible by knowledge, it has an end.
सा इयं माया सदसद्विलक्षणा ।
This Māyā is distinct from both the real (*sat*) and the unreal (*asat*).
त्रिकालाबाध्यं यत् तत् सद् इति उच्यते ।
That which is unsublated across the three divisions of time is called real (*sat*).
त्रिकालाबाध्यत्वात् चैतन्यम् एव सत् ।
Due to being unsublated in all three times, consciousness alone is real (*sat*).
माया तु ज्ञानबाध्यत्वात् सद्विलक्षणा ।
Māyā, on the other hand, is distinct from the real (*sat*) because it is sublated by knowledge.
कालत्रये अपि अप्रतीयमानं शशश‍ृङ्गवन्ध्यासुताकाशपद्मादिकम् असत् इति उच्यते ।
That which is never perceived in any of the three periods of time, such as a hare's horn, a barren woman's son, a sky-lotus, and the like, is called unreal (*asat*).
ज्ञानात् पूर्वं माया तत्कार्यं च प्रतीयते ।
Prior to knowledge, Māyā and its effects are experienced.
तथा हि, जाग्रत्काले अहम् अज्ञः ब्रह्म न1,2
To explain: in the waking state [the experience is] 'I am ignorant, I do not [know] Brahman...'
टिप्पणी
1.
दृष्टिसृष्टिवादैकसत्तावादैकजीववादेषु दृढतरसंस्कारवान् उत्तमाधिकारी ।
One who has strong impressions in Dṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-vāda, Eka-sattā-vāda, and Eka-jīva-vāda is the foremost qualified aspirant (*uttamādhikārin*).
2.
जगद्विवर्तोपादानभूतमधिष्ठानं मायोपहितचैतन्यमेव, न तु मायाविशिष्टम् ।
The substrate that is the material cause (*vivartopādāna*) of the world's illusory appearance is consciousness conditioned by *māyā* alone, not consciousness qualified (*viśiṣṭa*) by *māyā*.
तथापि मायाविशिष्टस्य उपादानत्वं ततः जगदुत्पत्तिः च अविवेकिदृष्ट्या उच्यते ।
Even so, the material causality of consciousness qualified by *māyā* and the creation of the world from it are spoken of only from the standpoint of the undiscriminating.
विवेकिदृष्ट्या तु जगतः परिणाम्युपादानं वा विवर्तोपादानं वा न मायाविशिष्टचैतन्यम् ।
From the perspective of the discriminating, however, consciousness qualified by *māyā* is neither the transformative cause (*pariṇāmy-upādāna*) nor the transfigurative cause (*vivartopādāna*) of the world.
किन्तु जगतः परिणाम्युपादानं केवला माया ।
Rather, the transformative material cause of the world is *māyā* alone.
विवर्तोपादानं मायोपहितचैतन्यम् ।
And the transfigurative material cause is consciousness conditioned by *māyā*.
अविवेकिनः तु उभयविधम् उपादानत्वं मायाविशिष्टचैतन्ये भ्रान्त्या प्रतीयते ।
To the undiscriminating, however, both kinds of material causality appear mistakenly in consciousness qualified by *māyā*.
तस्मात् शास्त्रकारैः अविवेकिनां दृष्टिः अनूद्यते केवलम्, न तु तात्पर्येण उच्यते इति ज्ञेयम् ।
Therefore, it should be understood that the scriptural authors merely restate the perspective of the undiscriminating, but do not propound it as the primary purport.
जानामि इति अनुभूयते माया ।
[... 'I do not know Brahman']—in this way, Māyā is experienced.
स्वप्नकाले प्रतीयमानसर्वपदार्थानाम् उपादानकारणतया माया एव विभाति ।
In the dream state, *māyā* alone shines forth as the material cause of all perceived objects.
सुप्तोत्थितस्य सुखम् अहम् अस्वाप्सं न किञ्चित् अवेदिषम् इति परामर्शः (स्मृतिः) भवति ।
For one awakened from deep sleep, there is the reflective recollection (memory): 'I slept happily; I knew nothing.'
सा च स्मृतिः अननुभूते अर्थे न सम्भवेत् ।
And that memory would not be possible regarding an object that had not been experienced.
तस्मात् सुषुप्तौ अज्ञानानुभवः अस्ति ।
Therefore, in deep sleep there is the experience of ignorance (*avidyā*).
अज्ञानं माया इति च एकम् एव वस्तु उच्यते ।
And *ajñāna* and *māyā* designate the very same entity.
इत्थम् अवस्थात्रये अपि माया प्रतीयते ।
Thus, Māyā is experienced in all three states of consciousness.
अतः सा असद्विलक्षणा ।
Hence it is distinct from the unreal (*asat*).
सदसद्विलक्षणमायाकार्यं जगत् अपि सदसद्विलक्षणम् एव ।
The world, being the effect of Māyā which is distinct from the real and the unreal, is itself also distinct from the real and the unreal.
अद्वैतमते सदसद्विलक्षणम् एव वस्तु मिथ्या इति, अनिर्वचनीयम् इति च कथ्यते ।
In the Advaita tradition, only an entity that is distinct from the real and the unreal is called *mithyā* (illusory) and *anirvacanīya* (inexpressible).
तस्मात् मायातत्कार्याभ्यां न द्वैतं सिद्ध्येत् ।
Therefore, duality cannot be established through Māyā and its effects.
मायातत्कार्ययोः सदसद्विलक्षणत्वात् मिथ्यात्वम् एव ।
Because Māyā and its effect are distinct from both the real and the unreal, they are only illusory (*mithyā*).
न हि मिथ्यापदार्थेन द्वैतसिद्धिः भवति, स्वप्ने दृष्टपदार्थेन यथा न द्वैतसिद्धिः तथा मिथ्यामायातत्कार्याभ्यां न ब्रह्मणः सद्वितीयत्वसिद्धिः ।
For duality is never established by an illusory object; just as duality is not established by an object seen in a dream, so too the possession of a second by Brahman is not established by illusory *māyā* and its effect.
256 · अज्ञानस्य स्वाश्रयविषयकत्वं
जीवेश्वरविभागशून्यशुद्धब्रह्माश्रिता माया शुद्धं ब्रह्मैवावृणोति, गृहाश्रितं तमो यथा गृहमेवावृणोति, तद्वत् ।
Just as darkness resting in a house veils the very house itself, likewise māyā, resting upon pure Brahman which is devoid of the distinction between jīva and īśvara, veils pure Brahman alone.
अयमेव स्वाश्रयस्वविषयकत्वपक्ष इत्युच्यते ।
This very position is called the doctrine that avidyā has itself (Brahman) as its locus and its object (svāśraya-svaviṣayakatva-pakṣa).
स्वशब्देन शुद्धं ब्रह्मोच्यते ।
By the word 'sva' (itself), pure Brahman is meant.
तदेव ब्रह्माज्ञानस्याश्रयो भवति, तदेव ब्रह्माज्ञानेनाव्रियते च ।
That very Brahman is the locus of avidyā, and that very Brahman is veiled by avidyā.
तस्मादज्ञानं स्वाश्रयस्वविषयकं इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, avidyā is said to be that which has itself as locus and itself as object.
विषयत्वं = आवृतत्वम् ।
Being the object means being veiled.
सङ्क्षेपशारीरकविवरणवेदान्तमुक्तावल्यद्वैतसिद्ध्यद्वैतदीपिकादिग्रन्थेषु अज्ञानं स्वाश्रय- विषयकं इति वर्णितम् ।
In treatises such as Saṅkṣepaśārīraka, Vivaraṇa, Vedāntamuktāvalī, Advaitasiddhi, Advaitadīpikā, etc., avidyā is described as having itself as both locus and object.
257 · उक्तार्थे वाचस्पतिमतं
अज्ञानं जीवमाश्रित्य स्थित्वा ब्रह्म विषयीकरोति ।
Avidyā, residing in the jīva as its locus, makes Brahman its object.
अहमज्ञो ब्रह्म न जानामि इत्यनुभवे अहम् इति शब्दार्थो जीवः अज्ञः इत्यज्ञानाश्रयत्वेन प्रतीयते ।
In the experience 'I am ignorant, I do not know Brahman', the jīva, which is the referent of the word 'I', is cognised through 'ignorant' as the locus of avidyā.
तस्माज्जीवस्याज्ञानाश्रयत्वं व्यक्तीभवति ।
Therefore, the jīva's being the locus of avidyā becomes clearly evident.
ब्रह्म न जानामि इति शब्दैरज्ञानस्य विषयो ब्रह्मेति सिद्ध्यति ।
By the words 'I do not know Brahman', it is established that Brahman is the object of avidyā.
तथा चाज्ञानं जीवाश्रितं सद्ब्रह्म विषयीकरोति = आवृणोतीति सिद्धम् ।
And thus it is established that avidyā, residing in the jīva, makes Brahman its object, i.e., veils Brahman.
तच्चाज्ञानं नैकम्, किन्तु नाना ।
And that avidyā is not one, but manifold.
अज्ञानस्यैकत्वे एकस्य ज्ञानोदयेनाज्ञाने नष्टे इतरेषामप्यज्ञानं तत्कार्यसंसारो वा न प्रतीयेत; प्रतीयते तु ।
If avidyā were single, then upon the rise of knowledge in one person and the consequent destruction of avidyā, neither avidyā nor saṃsāra (its effect) would be experienced by others; however, it is experienced.
अद्यावधि न कस्यचिदपि ज्ञानं नोदितमित्यभ्युपगमे इतः परमपि न कस्यचिदपि ज्ञानं जायेत ।
If it be assumed that till today knowledge has not arisen for anyone, then even hereafter knowledge would never arise for anyone.
श्रवणादिसाधनानामानर्थक्यप्रसङ्गश्च स्यात् ।
And there would also be the contingency of the futility of spiritual disciplines such as hearing (śravaṇa) and the rest.
तस्मादनन्तजीवाश्रितान्यज्ञानान्यनन्तानि ।
Therefore, avidyās resting in infinite jīvas are infinite in number.
अनन्तजीवानामनन्ताज्ञानैः कल्पिता ईश्वरा अपि अनन्ताः ।
The īśvaras projected by the infinite avidyās of the infinite jīvas are also infinite.
तथा ब्रह्माण्डान्यप्यनन्तानि ।
Likewise, the universes (brahmāṇḍas) are also infinite.
यस्य जीवस्य ज्ञानमुदेति तस्याज्ञानं तदज्ञानकल्पितेश्वरब्रह्माण्डानि च नश्यन्ति ।
For whichever jīva knowledge arises, his avidyā, as well as the īśvara and universes projected by his avidyā, perish.
यस्य ज्ञानं नोदितं तस्य बन्धोऽनुवर्तत एव ।
For whom knowledge has not arisen, his bondage simply continues.
258
वाचस्पतिमतासाङ्गत्यम्; अज्ञानैकत्वं च
The incongruity of Vācaspati's doctrine, and the oneness of avidyā:
ईश्वरो जीवाज्ञानकल्पित इत्युक्तिः श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणविरुद्धा ।
The statement that īśvara is projected by the jīva's avidyā is contradicted by śruti, smṛti, and the purāṇas.
ईश्वरा अनन्ताः, प्रतिजीवं सृष्टिर्भिन्ना इत्यपि प्रमाणविरुद्धम् ।
The proposition that 'There are infinite īśvaras, and creation is distinct for each jīva' is also contrary to all pramāṇas.
तस्मादज्ञानस्य नानात्वमाश्रित्य ईश्वरस्य सृष्टेश्चै ऐकत्वाभ्युपगमोऽपि न सङ्गच्छते ।
Therefore, even accepting the multiplicity of avidyā while trying to uphold the oneness of īśvara and creation is not logically tenable.
तथा हि, जीवेश्वरप्रपञ्चा अज्ञानकल्पिताः ।
To explain: jīva, īśvara, and the universe are projected by avidyā.
अज्ञानस्य नानात्वे एकैकाज्ञानकल्पितजीववदीश्वरप्रपञ्चानामप्यानन्त्यं प्रसज्येतैव ।
If avidyā is manifold, then just like the jīvas projected by each individual avidyā, the infinitude of īśvaras and universes would inevitably follow.
अत एव वाचस्पतिमिश्रैरनन्तेश्वरानन्तसृष्टय उक्ताः ।
That is precisely why Vācaspati Miśra asserted infinite īśvaras and infinite creations.
तस्मादज्ञानमेकमिति मतमेव ज्यायः ।
Therefore, the doctrine that avidyā is one alone is the superior (and correct) view.
259 · अज्ञानस्य स्वाश्रयस्वविषयकत्वपक्षाङ्गीकारः
तदिदमेकमज्ञानं न जीवाश्रितम्, किन्तु शुद्धब्रह्माश्रितमेव ।
Therefore, this single avidyā is not supported by the jīva, but is dependent solely upon pure Brahman.
जीवभावश्चाज्ञानकार्यम् ।
And the condition of being a jīva is an effect of avidyā.
तच्चाज्ञानं न कदाचिदपि स्वतन्त्रं तिष्ठति ।
And that avidyā never exists independently (without a locus).
तस्मान्निराश्रयाज्ञानेन न जीवभावः सिद्ध्येत् ।
Therefore, by an avidyā that is without any locus, the state of being a jīva could not be established.
यद्यज्ञानं प्रथमं यत्किञ्चिदाश्रयमाश्रित्य तिष्ठेत्तदा तत्कार्यजीवभावः सिद्ध्येत् ।
Only if avidyā first abides in some locus can the state of being a jīva, which is its effect, be established.
जीवभाव इवेश्वरभावोऽप्यज्ञानकार्यमेव ।
Just like the state of being a jīva, the state of being Īśvara is also an effect of avidyā alone.
तस्मादज्ञानं नेश्वराश्रितमपि ।
Therefore, avidyā is not located in Īśvara either.
परिशेषादिदमनाद्यज्ञानं शुद्धब्रह्माश्रितं भवति ।
By residual elimination, this beginningless avidyā is located in pure Brahman.
अनादिचैतन्याज्ञानयोः सम्बन्धः (कालः) अप्यनादिरेव ।
The relation between beginningless Consciousness and avidyā (as well as time) is also beginningless indeed.
चैतन्याज्ञानयोरनादिसम्बन्धाधीनजीवेश्वरभावोऽप्यनादिरेव ।
The state of being jīva and Īśvara, which depends on the beginningless relation between Consciousness and avidyā, is also beginningless indeed.
परन्तु जीवेश्वरभावयोरज्ञानाधीनत्वात् जीवेश्वरयोः अज्ञानकार्यत्वव्यपदेशः ।
However, because the conditions of jīva and Īśvara are dependent upon avidyā, jīva and Īśvara are designated as 'effects of avidyā'.
अहमज्ञः इति जीवाश्रितत्वेन यद्यप्यज्ञानमापाततः प्रतीयते, तथापि शुद्धब्रह्माश्रितेऽज्ञाने जीवस्य योऽभिमानः स एवार्थोऽनेन वाक्येनाभिलप्यते इति परमार्थः ।
Although avidyā appears superficially to reside in the jīva through the experience 'I am ignorant', nevertheless the ultimate truth is that this sentence only expresses the jīva's ego-identification with avidyā which is actually located in pure Brahman.
अज्ञानकार्यत्वाज्जीवस्य न तस्याज्ञानाधिष्ठानत्वरूपमाश्रयत्वं युज्यते ।
Because the jīva is an effect of avidyā, its having the status of a locus in the form of being the substratum of avidyā is not tenable.
किन्तु शुद्धब्रह्मैवाज्ञानस्य अधिष्ठानरूपाश्रयः ।
Rather, pure Brahman alone is the locus of avidyā in the sense of being its substratum (adhiṣṭhāna).
अहमज्ञः इति तु प्रतीतिर्जीवस्याज्ञानाभिमानित्वरूपमाश्रयत्वं विषयीकरोति ।
On the other hand, the cognition 'I am ignorant' has as its content the jīva's locus-status in the sense of identification with avidyā (as its experiencer/claimant).
शुद्धब्रह्मरूपाधिष्ठानाश्रितमज्ञानं स्वाश्रयं ब्रह्मैवावृणोति ।
Avidyā, resting upon the substratum that is pure Brahman, veils Brahman alone, its own locus.
तदनन्तरं जीवः अहमज्ञोऽस्मि इत्येवमज्ञानस्य अभिमानिरूपाश्रयो भवति ।
Thereafter, thinking 'I am ignorant', the jīva becomes the locus of avidyā as its claiming experiencer (abhimānī).
अनेन प्रकारेणाज्ञानं स्वाश्रयविषयकमिति सिद्धम् ।1
In this manner it is established that avidyā has its own locus as its object (svāśraya-svaviṣayaka).
टिप्पणी
1.
अहमज्ञः इत्यनुभवबलादज्ञानस्याश्रयो जीव इति वाचस्पतिमिश्रा आहुः ।
On the strength of the experience 'I am ignorant', Vācaspati Miśra asserts that the jīva is the locus of avidyā.
अयं पक्षो मुमुक्षुबुद्धौ सुखं प्रविशेदिति तैस्तथा वर्णितम् ।
He described it that way so that this position might be easily grasped by the intellect of a seeker of liberation.
वस्तुतस्तेषामेवमाशयः अहंशब्दस्य वाच्यार्थोऽन्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यरूपो जीवः ।
In reality, his purport is this: the expressed meaning (vācyārtha) of the word 'I' is the jīva, which is Consciousness qualified by the mind (antaḥkaraṇa).
तत्र विशेष्यांशभूतसाक्षिचैतन्यमेव ब्रह्म ।
Therein, the Witness-Consciousness constituting the substantive element (viśeṣyāṁśa) is Brahman itself.
तच्च ब्रह्माज्ञानस्याश्रयः ।
And that Brahman is the locus of avidyā.
विशेष्यधर्मस्य विशिष्टे व्यवहार इति न्यायेन जीवस्याज्ञानाश्रयत्वव्यपदेशः कृतः ।
According to the maxim that 'the attribute of the substantive is ascribed to the qualified entity' (viśeṣya-dharmasya viśiṣṭe vyavahāraḥ), the designation that the jīva is the locus of avidyā was made.
260 · एकाज्ञानपक्षे बन्धमोक्षव्यवस्था; एकाज्ञानपक्षस्य ज्यायस्तवम्; नामभेदेन मायास्वरूपं च
तच्चाज्ञानमेकमेव ।
And that *ajñāna* is indeed one only.
ज्ञानेन तदज्ञानं निवर्त्यते ।
By knowledge, that *ajñāna* is removed.
परन्तु यस्मिन् अन्तःकरणे ज्ञानमुदेति तादृशान्तःकरणावच्छिन्नचैतन्यनिष्ठाज्ञानांशस्तेन ज्ञानेन निवर्त्यते ।
However, in whichever *antaḥkaraṇa* knowledge arises, the part of *ajñāna* residing in the Consciousness delimited by that *antaḥkaraṇa* is removed by that knowledge.
स एव मुक्तो भवति ।
He alone becomes liberated.
यस्मिन् अन्तःकरणे ज्ञानं नोदेति तत्राज्ञानांशो बन्धश्च तथैवावतिष्ठते ।
In the *antaḥkaraṇa* where knowledge does not arise, there the portion of *ajñāna* and bondage remain just as before.
अनेन प्रकारेणाज्ञानस्य एकत्वपक्षे बन्धमोक्षव्यवहारसिद्धिः ।
In this manner, even in the doctrine of a single *ajñāna*, the empirical operation of bondage and liberation is established.
यदि वाचस्पतिमिश्रमतानुसारेण केषाञ्चिन्नानाज्ञानपक्षो मनसि प्रविशति तदा सोऽपि पक्षोऽद्वैतज्ञानोपाय एव ।
If, following the view of Vācaspati Miśra, the doctrine of multiple *ajñānas* appeals to someone's mind, then even that view is merely a means to the knowledge of Advaita.
न तन्मतखण्डने आग्रहः कार्यः ।
One should not insist on refuting that view.
यया प्रक्रियया जिज्ञासोरद्वैतबोधो भवति तस्यां प्रक्रियायां तस्य बुद्धिः स्थिरीकर्तव्या ।
By whichever methodology the seeker attains realization of non-duality, his intellect should be anchored in that very methodology.
शुद्धब्रह्माश्रितां मायां अविद्येति अज्ञानमिति चाहुः ।
*Māyā*, which is supported by pure Brahman, is called *avidyā* and *ajñāna* as well.
अचिन्त्यानन्तशक्तिमत्त्वाद्युक्तीनामविषयत्वाच्च मायेति व्यपदेशः ।
Because it possesses inconceivable and infinite power, and because it is beyond the scope of logical arguments, it is designated as *māyā*.
विद्यानाश्यत्वादविद्येति वर्ण्यते ।
Because it is destructible by knowledge (*vidyā*), it is described as *avidyā*.
स्वरूपावारकत्वाद् अज्ञानमिति च भण्यते ।
And because it conceals one's true nature (*svarūpa*), it is called *ajñāna*.
मायाया आश्रयभूतं चैतन्यं सामान्यचैतन्यम् ।
The Consciousness that serves as the locus of *māyā* is general Consciousness (*sāmānya-caitanya*).
न तन्मायाया विरोधि, किन्तु साधकम् ।
That is not opposed to *māyā*, but is rather its revealer.
मायायाः सत्ताप्रदं स्फुरणप्रदं च ।
It gives existence and manifestation to *māyā*.
वृत्त्यारूढं चैतन्यमथवा चैतन्यसहितां वृत्तिं मायाया विरोधितया जानीयात् ।
One should know Consciousness reflected in the mental mode (*vṛtti-ārūḍha-caitanya*), or the *vṛtti* endowed with Consciousness, to be the adversary of *māyā*.
अत्र सूर्यकान्तशिलारूढसूर्यप्रभा दृष्टान्तत्वेनावगन्तव्या ।
Here, sunlight focused through a sunstone (*sūryakānta-śilā*) should be understood as an illustration.
इत्थमेका अनादिः सान्ता सदसद्विलक्षणानिर्वचनीया अविद्याज्ञानादिशब्दव्यपदेश्या सामान्यचैतन्यमाश्रिता वृत्त्यारूढचैतन्यविनाश्या च माया वर्णिता ।1,2
Thus *māyā* has been described as one, beginningless, having an end, indescribable as being distinct from real and unreal, designated by words like *avidyā* and *ajñāna*, supported by general Consciousness, and destroyed by Consciousness reflected in a mental modification.
टिप्पणी
1.
अत्रायमभिप्रायः - अंशिरूपान्धकारस्यैकत्वेऽपि अंशभूता नानान्धकाराः प्रतिगृहं वर्तन्ते ।
Here this is the purport: even though darkness as an organic whole is one, individual darknesses exist as parts in every house.
यस्मिन् गेहे दीपोऽस्ति तत्रस्थोंऽशभूतोऽन्धकारो विनश्यति ।
In the house where a lamp is lit, the portion of darkness situated there is destroyed.
न गेहान्तरस्थान्धकारांशस्य नाशः ।
There is no destruction of the portion of darkness situated in another house.
एवमेवांशिभूतमज्ञानमेकमेव ।
In the very same way, *ajñāna* as the total whole is just one.
तस्यांशभूतनानाज्ञानानि नानान्तःकरणप्रदेशस्थसाक्षिचैतन्यमाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्ति ।
Its various component portions of *ajñāna* exist by taking support of the *sākṣin* Consciousness located in different regions of the *antaḥkaraṇas*.
यस्मिन्नन्तःकरणप्रदेशे वृत्तिज्ञानमुदेति तादृशान्तःकरणप्रदेशस्थाज्ञानांशो विनश्यति ।
In whichever locus of an *antaḥkaraṇa* the *vṛtti-jñāna* arises, the portion of *ajñāna* located in that region of the *antaḥkaraṇa* is destroyed.
स एव मुक्तो भवति, नेतरे ।
He alone becomes liberated, not others.
तस्मादेकस्य ज्ञानोदये सति सर्वेषामप्यज्ञानतत्कार्यनाशद्वारा मुक्त्यापत्तिर्न कार्या ।
Therefore, when one person attains knowledge, the undesirable contingency of everyone becoming liberated through the destruction of *ajñāna* and its effects need not be raised.
इत्थमेकाज्ञानाङ्गीकारपक्षे बन्धमोक्षव्यवस्थासिद्धिः ।
Thus, in the position accepting a single *ajñāna*, the proper distinction of bondage and liberation is established.
किञ्च जीवाज्ञानकल्पित ईश्वरोऽनन्तः, जीवभेदेन सृष्टिरपि नाना इति श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणादिविरुद्धपक्षो न युक्तः ।
Moreover, the view that 'Īśvara is manifold, imagined by each *jīva's* *ajñāna*, and creation too is manifold according to the difference of *jīvas*' is contrary to Śruti, Smṛti, and the Purāṇas, and is untenable.
अत एकाज्ञानपक्षो ज्यायान् ।
Therefore, the doctrine of a single *ajñāna* (*eka-ajñāna-vāda*) is superior.
2.
यया यया भवेत्पुंसां व्युत्पत्तिः प्रत्यगात्मनि । सा सैव प्रक्रियेह स्यात् साध्वी सा चानवस्थिता ॥ (बृ. भा. वा. १.४.४०२) इति नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिकारा आहुः ।
'By whichever method people gain understanding of the inner Self, that very methodology is valid here; and it is not rigidly fixed' (बृ. भा. वा. १.४.४०२) — so say the authors of Naiṣkarmyasiddhi.
प्रसङ्गादीश्वरस्वरूपवर्णनम्॥ २६१–२६२ ॥
261 · ईश्वरस्वरूपम्; द्विविधकारणलक्षणं च
शुद्धसत्त्वगुणसहिता माया, मायाधिष्ठानं चैतन्यम्, मायाप्रतिफलितचैतन्याभास इति त्रयं मिलित्वा ईश्वर इत्यभिधीयते ।
The triad consisting of māyā endowed with pure sattva-guṇa, the pure Consciousness which is the substratum of māyā, and the reflection of Consciousness reflected in māyā, together is designated as Īśvara.
सोऽयमीश्वरः सर्वज्ञः ।
This very Īśvara is omniscient.
स एव जगतः कारणम् ।
He alone is the cause of the universe.
कारणं द्विविधं - उपादानकारणम्, निमित्तकारणं चेति ।
Cause is of two kinds: the material cause (upādāna-kāraṇa) and the efficient cause (nimitta-kāraṇa).
यत् कार्यस्वरूपे प्रविशति, यद्विना कार्यस्य स्थितिर्नास्ति, तदुपादानकारणं उच्यते ।
That which enters into the very nature of the effect, and without which the effect cannot subsist, is called the material cause.
यथा मृद्घटस्योपादानकारणम् ।1
Just as clay is the material cause of a pot.
घटस्वरूपे मृदः प्रवेशोऽस्ति, मृदं विना घटो न स्थितिं लभते च ।
Clay is immanent in the nature of the pot, and without clay the pot does not obtain existence.
यत् कार्यस्वरूपे न प्रविशति, किन्तु कार्यात्पृथक् स्थितं सत्कार्यमुत्पादयति, यस्य नाशेन कार्यं न नश्यति तन्निमित्तकारणं इत्यभिधीयते ।
That which does not enter into the nature of the effect, but, remaining distinct from the effect, produces it, and upon whose destruction the effect does not perish, is designated as the efficient cause.
यथा घटस्य कुलालो दण्डचक्रादयश्च निमित्तकारणानि ।
Just as for a pot, the potter, the stick, the wheel, etc., are efficient causes.
न कुलालादयो घटस्वरूपे प्रविशन्ति; घटात्पृथग्भूता घटमुत्पादयन्ति; घटो2
The potter and others do not enter into the nature of the pot; being distinct from the pot, they produce the pot; the pot...
टिप्पणी
1.
कार्योत्पत्तिस्थितिलयकारणत्वमुपादानकारणस्य लक्षणम् ।
Being the cause of the origin, sustenance, and dissolution of an effect is the definition of a material cause.
जगदुत्पत्तिविषये आरम्भपरिणामविवर्तवादानां मध्ये विवर्तवाद एव श्रेयानिति विचारतः सिद्ध्यति ।
Regarding the origin of the world, it is established through inquiry that among the doctrines of ārambhavāda (creationism), pariṇāmavāda (transformation), and vivartavāda (illusory appearance), vivartavāda alone is superior.
तथा हि- (१) सावयवैरनेकैः कारणद्रव्यैः संयोगसचिवैरेकमवयवि कार्यमुत्पद्यत इत्यारम्भवादः ।
To explain: (1) Ārambhavāda is the doctrine that a single composite whole effect arises from multiple cause-substances possessing parts, aided by conjunction.
यथा अनेकैस्तन्तुभिः संयोगसचिवैरेकं पटरूपकार्यमुत्पद्यत इत्यारम्भवादः ।
As [in the example where] from many threads joined together, a single cloth-effect is newly generated: this is ārambhavāda.
अत्र मते कार्यकारणयोरत्यन्तभेदोऽभ्युपगम्यते ।
In this doctrine, an absolute difference between cause and effect is accepted.
जगदुत्पत्तिविषये आरम्भवादो न सम्भवति ।
Ārambhavāda is not possible regarding the origin of the world.
अद्वितीयब्रह्मणोऽपरिच्छिन्नत्वेन निरवयवत्वान्न ततः सावयवं जगत्पृथग्जायेत ।
Because non-dual Brahman is unconditioned and devoid of parts, a separate world with parts cannot be born from It.
(२) परिणामवादोऽपि न प्रपञ्चोत्पत्तिविषये युज्यते ।
(2) Pariṇāmavāda (transformation doctrine) too is not tenable regarding the creation of the cosmos.
कारणवस्तुनः प्राक्सिद्धकारणावस्थापरित्यागपूर्वकावस्थान्तरप्राप्तिः परिणामः ।
Pariṇāma is the causal substance's attainment of a different state through the abandonment of its previously established causal state.
यथा मृत्परिणामो घट इति प्रधानपरिणामो जगदिति च साङ्ख्या वदन्ति ।
Just as a pot is a modification of clay, the Sāṅkhyas claim that the world is a transformation of pradhāna.
ब्रह्मपरिणामो जगदिति केचनोपासका मन्यन्ते ।
Certain upāsakas hold that the world is a transformation of Brahman.
तदुभयं सूत्रभाष्यकारादिभिः खण्डितम् ।
Both of these views have been refuted by the authors of the Sūtras, Bhāṣya, etc.
चैतन्यस्याकाशादपि सूक्ष्मत्वेन निरवयवत्वादेवोपासकमतमत्यन्तमसङ्गतमेव ।
Because Consciousness is subtler than even space and is partless, the view of the upāsakas is utterly untenable.
इत्थं परिणामवादोऽपि न युज्यतेऽत्र ।
Thus, pariṇāmavāda also is not valid here.
(३) विवर्तवादे तु पूर्वोक्तदोषलेशोऽपि न सम्भवति ।
(3) But in vivartavāda, not even a trace of the aforementioned defects can arise.
कारणवस्तुनो नित्यसिद्धस्वस्वरूपापरित्यागेनैवान्यथा भानमात्रं विवर्त इति श्रुतियुक्त्यनुभवसिद्धम् ।
That vivarta is the mere appearance as something else without the causal reality giving up its eternally established true nature, is established by scripture, reasoning, and experience.
यथा शुक्त्यादौ रजतावभासः ।
Just as the appearance of silver in mother-of-pearl.
अयमेव पक्षो वेदान्ताभिमतः ।
This alone is the position accepted in Vedānta.
अत्र जगद्विवर्तोपादानरूपाधिष्ठानं मायोपहितचैतन्यमेव ।
Here, the substratum functioning as the illusory material cause (vivartopādāna) of the universe is Consciousness conditioned by māyā (māyopahita-caitanya) alone.
न मायाविशिष्टम् ।
Not Consciousness qualified by māyā (māyā-viśiṣṭa).
अविवेकिनस्तथा कथयन्ति ।
The non-discriminating say so.
परिणाम्युपादानं माया, विवर्तोपादानमुपहितचैतन्यमिति विवेके सिद्धेऽपि तदुभयं मायाविशिष्टचैतन्यमिति वदन्ति विवेचनाकुशलाः ।
Even when the distinction is established that māyā is the transformative material cause (pariṇāmy-upādāna) and conditioned Consciousness is the transfigurative material cause (vivartopādāna), those unskillful in discernment say that both together are Consciousness qualified by māyā.
2.
कार्योत्पत्तिमात्रकारणत्वं निमित्तकारणस्य लक्षणम् ।
Being the cause merely of the origination of an effect is the definition of an efficient cause (nimitta-kāraṇa).
तच्च निमित्तकारणमनेकविधम् ।
And that efficient cause is of manifold kinds.
त्पत्त्यनन्तरं कुलालादीनां नाशेऽपि घटो न नश्यति ।
Even upon the destruction of the potter and the like after the production [of the pot], the pot is not destroyed.
इत्थं उपादानं निमित्तं इति च कारणं द्विविधम् ।
Thus, cause is twofold, namely the material cause (upādāna) and the efficient cause (nimitta).
262 · ईश्वर एव प्रपञ्चस्योपादानकारणं नीमत्तकारणं च
ईश्वर एव जगत उपादानकारणं निमित्तकारणं च भवति ।
Īśvara alone is both the material cause and the efficient cause of the world.
यथैक एव लूताकीटस्तन्तुरूपकार्यं प्रत्युपादानकारणं निमित्तकारणं च भवति ।
Just as the spider alone is both the material cause and the efficient cause with respect to the effect in the form of the thread (web),
तद्वदेवेश्वरः प्रपञ्चं प्रत्युपादानं निमित्तं च ।
similarly Īśvara alone is both the material and efficient cause with respect to the phenomenal universe.
तत्र लूताकीटस्य जडं शरीरं तन्तोरुपादानकारणम्, तच्छरीरस्थमन्तःकरणसहितचैतन्यं निमित्तकारणम् ।
There, the insentient body of the spider is the material cause of the thread, while the consciousness situated in that body endowed with the internal organ is the efficient cause.
एवमेवेश्वरशरीरभूतजडमाया जगत उपादानम्, चेतनभागो निमित्तकारणम् ।
In the very same way, insentient māyā, which constitutes the body of Īśvara, is the material cause of the world, and the conscious aspect is the efficient cause.
इत्थमेकस्यैवेश्वरस्य प्रपञ्चं प्रत्युपादाननिमित्तोभयकारणत्वे लूताकीटो दृष्टान्तः ।
Thus, regarding the single Īśvara being both the material and efficient cause with respect to the universe, the spider serves as an illustration.
मुख्यदृष्टान्तस्तु स्वप्न एव ।
However, the primary illustration is the dream alone.
यदा पुनरीश्वरो जीवानां कर्मफलदानाय न सम्मुखो भवति तदा जगतः प्रलयः, यदा च स ईश्वरो जीवानां कर्मफलदानायाभिमुखो भवति तदा जगतः सृष्टिश्च भवति ।
When Īśvara is not inclined towards dispensing the fruits of karma of the jīvas, then dissolution of the world occurs; and when that Īśvara becomes inclined to dispense the fruits of karma of the jīvas, then creation of the world takes place.
इत्थं जगत्सृष्टेर्जीवकर्माधीनत्वाज्जीवस्वरूपमिदानीं निरूप्यते ।1,2
In this way, since the creation of the world depends upon the karma of the jīvas, the essential nature of the jīva is now delineated.
टिप्पणी
1.
न्यायमते घटेनेश्वरस्य संयोगे ईश्वरस्याभिन्ननिमित्तोपादानत्वमुक्तम् ।
In the Nyāya doctrine, regarding the conjunction of Īśvara with a pot, Īśvara is stated to be the non-different efficient and material cause (as the substrate of the conjunction and its agent).
तथा जीवाश्रितज्ञानसुखादिगुणानां जीवस्याभिन्ननिमित्तोपादानत्वमभिमतम् ।
Likewise, regarding the qualities like knowledge, pleasure, etc., residing in the jīva, the jīva's being the non-different efficient and material (inherence) cause is admitted.
किञ्च यथास्मन्मते जीवस्य स्वप्नप्रपञ्चं प्रत्यभिन्ननिमित्तोपादानत्वमिष्टं तथेश्वरस्य जाग्रत्प्रपञ्चं प्रत्यभिन्ननिमित्तोपादानत्वं भवति ।
Furthermore, just as in our system the jīva is accepted as the non-different material and efficient cause with respect to the dream world, so too Īśvara is the non-different material and efficient cause with respect to the waking world.
2.
शिष्यःननु दुःखतत्साधनपरिहारे वा सुखतत्साधनसम्पादने वेच्छा दृष्टा ।
[Objection:] Desire is observed either for the removal of suffering and its causes, or for the acquisition of happiness and its causes.
शिष्यःईश्वरस्य तु दुःखतत्साधनयोरभावान्न तन्निवृत्तीच्छासम्भवः ।
Since suffering and its causes are absent in Īśvara, there is no possibility of a desire for their removal.
शिष्यःपर्याप्तकामत्वादीश्वरस्य नापि सुखतत्साधनसम्पादनेच्छा ।
Nor can Īśvara have a desire for acquiring happiness and its causes, because He is already fully satisfied (paryāptakāma).
शिष्यःअत ईश्वरस्येच्छा न कुत्रचिदपि युज्यते ।
Therefore, no desire whatsoever is tenable in Īśvara.
शिष्यःबालानामकस्मादेव क्रीडायामिच्छावदीश्वरस्यापि जगत्सृष्टिरूपविनोदेच्छा निमित्तं विनैव भवतीत्यपि न ।
Nor can it be said that just as children have a spontaneous desire for play, so too Īśvara has a desire for the sport of world-creation without any motive at all.
गुरुःयथा बालानां चित्ते आह्लादरूपसुखप्राप्तिनिमित्तकेच्छा भवति तथा पूर्णकामस्येश्वरस्याह्लादरूपसुखप्राप्तीच्छा न सम्भवतीति चेन्न ।
For just as children have in their mind a desire motivated by gaining the joy of pleasure, in the case of Īśvara, whose desires are already fulfilled, such a desire to gain joy is impossible — if this is argued, we reply: No.
गुरुःयथा कल्पवृक्षादिः स्वाश्रितपुरुषसङ्कल्परूपनिमित्तेन स्वस्वभावादेवाश्रितपुरुषमनोरथं पूरयति, तथेश्वरोऽपि प्राणिनां फलदानोन्मुखो यदा भवति तदा जीवादृष्टरूपनिमित्तेनैव स्वस्वभावादेव जगत्सृष्ट्यादिविषयक- ज्ञानेच्छाप्रयत्नादिकं करोति ।
Just as the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa) etc. fulfills the desire of a person who has taken refuge in it purely out of its own nature, through the instrumental cause of that person's resolve, so too, when Īśvara becomes inclined to bestow fruit upon living beings, He manifests knowledge, desire, effort, etc., regarding the creation of the world, purely by His own nature through the cause of the unseen merit/demerit (adṛṣṭa) of the jīvas.
गुरुःईश्वरीयेच्छाज्ञानप्रयत्नमध्ये एकैकापि व्यक्तिः सृष्ट्यारम्भकाले उत्पन्ना प्रलयपर्यन्तं तिष्ठति ।
Among the desire, knowledge, and effort belonging to Īśvara, each single instance that arises at the inception of creation endures right up to dissolution.
गुरुःतस्मादीश्वरेच्छाप्रयत्ना नित्या उच्यन्ते ।
Therefore, the desire and effort of Īśvara are spoken of as eternal (lasting throughout creation).
गुरुःकिञ्चेश्वरीयेच्छादयो भूतभविष्यद्वर्तमानकालगतसकलपदार्थान् विषयीकरोति ।
Moreover, Īśvara's desire and so forth take as their object all entities belonging to the past, future, and present times.
गुरुःअत एव सदा सृष्टिः प्रलयो वा, सदा शैत्यमौष्णं वा, सदा वृष्टिरवग्रहो वा न सम्भवति ।
For this very reason, creation or dissolution does not occur perpetually, nor does cold or heat last perpetually, nor do rain or drought prevail continuously.
गुरुःकिन्तु समयानुसारेणैव भवन्ति ।
Rather, they occur strictly in accordance with their designated time.
263 · जीवस्वरूपवर्णनम्
रजस्तमसी अभिभूय उद्भूतो यः सत्त्वगुणः स शुद्धसत्त्वगुण इत्यभिधीयते ।
That sattva-guṇa which manifests having overpowered rajas and tamas is called pure sattva-guṇa (śuddha-sattva).
रजस्तमोभ्यामभिभूतो यः सत्त्वगुणः स मलिनसत्त्वगुण इति कीर्त्यते ।
That sattva-guṇa which is overpowered by rajas and tamas is declared to be impure sattva-guṇa (malina-sattva).
ईदृशमलिनसत्त्वगुणसहिताज्ञानांशप्रतिफलितचिदाभासः, अज्ञानं, अज्ञानाधिष्ठानकूटस्थचैतन्यं चेति त्रयं मिलित्वा जीव इति वर्ण्यते ।
These three together — the reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa) reflected in that portion of avidyā which contains such impure sattva-guṇa, avidyā itself, and the immutable Consciousness (kūṭastha-caitanya) which is the substratum of avidyā — are described as the jīva.
सोऽयं जीवः कर्म करोति ।
This very jīva performs actions,
तत्फलं चेच्छति ।
and desires their fruits.
जगत्सृष्टिवर्णनम्॥ २६४–२७२ ॥
264 · ईश्वरस्य वैषम्यनैर्घृण्याभावः
जीवस्य स्वकर्मानुसारेण उच्चावचभोगानुभवाय ईश्वरः प्राणिनां पुण्यपापानुरूपां सृष्टिं करोति ।
In order that the jīva may experience diverse higher and lower enjoyments in accordance with its own past karma, Īśvara brings about a creation conforming to the merits and demerits of living beings.
तस्मादीश्वरस्य न वैषम्यनैर्घृण्ये स्तः ।
Therefore, partiality and cruelty do not exist in Īśvara.
नन्वाद्यसर्गात्पूर्वं न कर्मास्ति ।
[Objection:] But prior to the very first creation, there was no karma.
प्रथमसर्गे चेश्वरः प्राणिनामुच्चनीचशरीराणि उच्चावचभोगांश्च सृजति ।
And in the first creation, Īśvara creates high and low bodies and unequal enjoyments for living beings.
तस्मादीश्वरो विषमदृष्टिरेवाकस्माद्विषमसृष्टिकरणादिति चेन्न ।
Therefore, Īśvara is indeed partial, because He brings about an unequal creation arbitrarily without prior cause — if this is argued, it is not so.
संसारोऽनादिः ।
Saṃsāra is beginningless.
तस्मादुत्तरोत्तरसृष्टेः पूर्वपूर्वसृष्टौ तत्तत्प्राणिकृतं कर्मैव कारणम् ।
Therefore, for each subsequent creation, the karma performed by each respective living being in each preceding creation is itself the cause.
सृष्टेरिदम्प्रथमत्वासम्भवान्नेश्वरे दोषः ।
Since an absolute first beginning of creation is impossible, there is no fault in Īśvara.
265 · जीवभोगार्थमीश्वरस्य जगत्सिसृक्षा
जीवकर्मफलप्रदानाद्यदेश्वरो विमुखो भवति तदा जगत्प्रलयो भवति ।
When Īśvara turns away from dispensing the fruits of the jīvas' karmas, then the dissolution (pralaya) of the world occurs.
प्रलये सर्वपदार्थसंस्कारा मायायां लीना भवन्ति ।
In dissolution, the latent impressions (saṃskāras) of all entities become merged in māyā.
तस्माज्जीवानां कर्मशेषोऽपि सूक्ष्मरूपेण मायायां निलीनो भवति ।
Therefore, the unexhausted residue of the jīvas' karma also remains absorbed in subtle form within māyā.
यदा प्राणिनां कर्मफलदानाभिमुखो भवतीश्वरस्तदा जीवानां भोगार्थमहं जगत् सृजे इतीश्वरस्येच्छा जायते ।
When Īśvara turns toward dispensing the fruits of karma to living beings, the desire arises in Īśvara: 'Let Me create the world for the experience of the jīvas.'
सूक्ष्मसृष्टिनिरूपणम्॥ २६६–२७० ॥
266 · सूक्ष्मपञ्चभूतानां तद्गुणानां चोत्पत्तिः
एतादृशेश्वरेच्छावशात् माया तमोगुणप्रधाना भवति तादृशतमोगुणप्रधानमायासकाशात् आकाशवायुतेजोजलपृथिव्यात्मकपञ्चभूतान्युत्पद्यन्ते ।
By the power of such will of Īśvara, māyā becomes predominated by the quality of tamas; from such tamas-predominated māyā, the five elements consisting of space, air, fire, water, and earth are born.
तेषु भूतेषु क्रमेण1
In those elements, successively...
टिप्पणी
1.
यथा पुत्रार्थिनी जाया पत्या सङ्गता शुक्ररूपं बीजम्, ततः क्रमेण पुत्ररूपेण परिणतं गर्भं च वहन्ती प्रसवात्पूर्वं सन्ततिलाभनिमित्तेन सदा प्रसन्ना सत्त्वगुणप्रधानेव भवति ।
Just as a wife desiring a child, united with her husband, receives the seed in the form of semen and bearing the womb that gradually develops into the form of a child, remains always joyful prior to delivery due to the anticipation of gaining progeny, as though predominated by sattva-guṇa;
पश्चात्प्रसवकाले वेदनानिमित्तेन प्रसन्नतायाः तिरोधाने सति शून्यचित्ता तमोगुणप्रधानेव भवति;
Later, at the time of childbirth, due to labor pain, upon the disappearance of her cheerfulness, she becomes blank-minded and as though predominated by tamas;
यथा वा पूर्वं श्वेतवर्णो मेघो वर्षाकाले श्यामो भवति;
Or just as a cloud that was previously white becomes dark during the rainy season;
तथा सृष्टेः पूर्वं ब्रह्मप्रतिबिम्बरूपजगद्बीजधारिणी अविद्योपाधिकानन्तजीवसहितप्रपञ्चरूपगर्भधारिणी च शुद्धसत्त्वप्रधाना माया (ईश्वरस्योपाधिः) भवति ।
Similarly, before creation, māyā (the upādhi of Īśvara), bearing the seed of the world which is the reflection of Brahman, and bearing the womb of the universe together with infinite jīvas conditioned by avidyā, is predominated by pure sattva.
पश्चात्सृष्ट्यारम्भकाले सा माया शुद्धसत्त्वस्वरूपतिरोधानेन सृष्टियोग्यतमोगुणप्रधानप्रकृतिरूपा भवति ।
Later, at the time of the commencement of creation, that māyā, by the concealment of its pure-sattva nature, assumes the form of prakṛti predominated by tamas suitable for creation.
शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धाख्यपञ्चगुणा वर्तन्ते ।
There exist five qualities known as sound, touch, form, taste, and smell.
मायायाः सकाशाच्छब्दसहित आकाश उत्पन्नः ।
From māyā, ether endowed with sound was born.
आकाशाद्वायुः ।
From space, air was produced.
वायोराकाशकार्यत्वात्कारणगुणेन शब्देन स्वासाधारणगुणस्पर्शेन च द्विगुणो वायुः ।
Because air is an effect of space, it possesses two qualities: the causal quality, sound, and its own unique quality, touch.
वायोरग्निः सम्भूतः ।
From air, fire arose.
कारणाकाशवायुगुणाभ्यां शब्दस्पर्शाभ्यां स्वासाधारणरूपगुणेन च त्रिगुणोऽग्निः ।
Fire has three qualities: the qualities of its causes (space and air), namely sound and touch, and its own unique quality, form.
अग्नेरापः सम्भूताः ।
From fire, waters arose.
कारणाकाशवाय्वग्निगुणैः शब्दस्पर्शरूपैः स्वासाधारणरसगुणेन च चतुर्गुणा आपः ।
Water possesses four qualities: the qualities of its causes (space, air, and fire), sound, touch, and form, and its own unique quality, taste.
अद्भ्यः पृथिवी सम्भुता ।
From waters, earth arose.
कारणाकाशवाय्वग्न्यब्गुणैः शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसैः स्वासाधारणगन्धगुणेन च पञ्चगुणा पृथिवी ।
Earth has five qualities: the qualities of its causes (space, air, fire, and water)—sound, touch, form, and taste—and its own unique quality, smell.
आकाशे प्रतिध्वनिरूपशब्दो वर्तते ।
In ether, there is sound in the form of echo.
वायौ बीसीतिशब्दः, शीतोष्णकठिनानां विलक्षणस्पर्शश्च वर्तते ।
In air, there is the rustling sound 'bīs' and a touch distinct from cold, hot, and hard (i.e. neither hot nor cold).
अग्नौ भुग्भुग्शब्दः, उष्णस्पर्शः, प्रकाशाख्यरूपं च वर्तते ।
In fire, there is the roaring sound 'bhug-bhug', hot touch, and the visible form known as light.
जले चिलिचिलिशब्दः, शीतस्पर्शः, शुक्लरूपम्, मधुररसश्च वर्तते ।
In water, there is the splashing sound 'chili-chili', cold touch, non-luminous white color, and sweet taste.
लवणतिक्ततादिरसास्तु पृथिवीसम्बन्धादेव जले विभान्ति ।
Tastes like salty, bitter, etc., however, appear in water only due to contact with earth.
माधुर्यमेव स्वाभाविकरसो जलस्य ।
Sweetness alone is the natural taste of water.
स च हरीतक्यामलकादिभक्षणसंस्कृतरसनया जलपानेऽभिव्यज्यते ।
And that sweetness is clearly manifested when drinking water after the tongue has been cleansed/sensitized by chewing harītakī, āmalaka, etc.
पृथिव्यां कडकडाशब्दः, अनुष्णाशीतस्पर्शः, शुक्लकृष्णपीतरक्तहरितादिरूपम्, मधुराम्ललवणकटुकषायतिक्ताख्यषड्रसाः, सुगन्धदुर्गन्धरूपद्विविधगन्धश्च वर्तते ।
In earth, there is the cracking sound 'kaḍakaḍā', neither-hot-nor-cold touch, diverse colors such as white, black, yellow, red, green, etc., the six tastes known as sweet, sour, salty, pungent, astringent, and bitter, and the twofold smell of fragrance and foul odor.
इत्थमाकाशे एको गुणः ।
Thus in ether there is one quality.
वायौ द्वौ ।
In air, there are two.
अग्नौ त्रयः ।
In fire, there are three.
जले चत्वारः ।
In water, there are four.
पृथिव्यां पञ्चगुणाः ।
In earth, there are five qualities.
तत्रापि प्रतिभूतं प्रातिस्विकगुणस्त्वेक एव ।
Even there, for each respective element, the intrinsic, unique quality is only one.
तदितरगुणाः कारणादनुगताः ।
The other qualities are inherited from the respective causes.
सर्वस्य मूलकारणमीश्वरः ।
The root cause of everything is Īśvara.
ईश्वरे चांशद्वयमस्ति ।
And in Īśvara, there are two aspects:
चैतन्यांशो मायांशश्चेति ।
namely, the consciousness-aspect and the māyā-aspect.
सर्वेषु भूतेषु विद्यमानो नामरूपात्मकमिथ्यांशो मायायाः, सत्तास्फुर्तिरूपांशस्तु चैतन्यस्येति ज्ञेयम् ।
It should be understood that the illusory aspect of name and form present in all elements belongs to māyā, whereas the aspect of existence and illumination belongs to consciousness (*caitanya*).
267 · चतुर्विधभेदसहितान्तःकरणोत्पत्तिः
अपञ्चीकृतपञ्चभूतानां सत्त्वगुणांशसमष्टिः सत्त्वं इत्यभिधीयमानमन्तःकरणमुत्पादयति ।
The totality (samaṣṭi) of the sattva-guṇa portions of the unquintuplicated five subtle elements produces the inner instrument (antaḥkaraṇa), which is also termed 'sattva'.
अन्तःकरणं ज्ञानोत्पत्तिहेतुः ।
The inner instrument is the cause of the arising of knowledge.
ज्ञानोत्पत्तिः सत्त्वगुणादित्यङ्गीकृतम् ।
It is accepted that the arising of knowledge is from *sattva-guṇa*.
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानम् (भ. गी. १४.१७) इति ।
As the scripture says: 'From *sattva* arises knowledge' (Bhagavad Gītā 14.17).
तस्मादन्तःकरणं भूतानां सत्त्वगुणकार्यम् ।
Therefore, the inner instrument is the product of the *sattva-guṇa* of the elements.
तच्चान्तःकरणमपञ्चीकृतपञ्चभूतव्यष्टिसत्त्वगुणकार्यपञ्चज्ञानेन्द्रियाणां स्वस्वविषयग्रहणे सहकारि ।
Moreover, that inner instrument is an auxiliary cause for the five sense organs—which are the products of the individual (*vyaṣṭi*) *sattva* aspects of the unquintuplicated five elements—in apprehending their respective objects.
तस्मादपि पञ्चभूतसमष्टिसत्त्वगुणकार्यमेवान्तःकरणम् ।
For this reason as well, the inner instrument is indeed the product of the collective (*samaṣṭi*) *sattva-guṇa* of the five elements.
न वैशेषिकादीनामिवान्तःकरणं नित्यम् ।
The inner instrument is not eternal, as held by the Vaiśeṣikas and others.
अन्तः = देहस्यान्तः स्थित्वा, करणं = ज्ञानसाधनं इत्यन्तःकरणं उच्यते ।
Because it acts inside the body (antaḥ) as an instrument (karaṇa) of knowledge, it is called the 'antaḥkaraṇa' (inner instrument).
पञ्चभूतसमष्टिसत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वेनान्तःकरणं सत्त्वं इत्यपि कीर्त्यते ।
Because it is the product of the collective *sattva-guṇa* of the five elements, the inner instrument is also designated as 'sattva'.
अन्तःकरणपरिणामस्य वृत्तिरिति संज्ञा ।
The transformation (pariṇāma) of the inner instrument receives the designation 'vṛtti'.
अन्तःकरणस्य वृत्तयश्चतस्रः ।
The *vṛtti*s of the inner instrument are fourfold.
तत्र पदार्थस्य स्वरूपनिश्चयात्मिका वृत्तिर्बुद्धिः ।
Among these, the *vṛtti* that is of the nature of determinate ascertainment regarding the nature of an object is *buddhi* (intellect).
सङ्कल्पात्मिका वृत्तिर्मनः ।
The *vṛtti* that is of the nature of deliberation (saṅkalpa and vikalpa) is *manas* (mind).
चिन्तनात्मिका वृत्तिश्चित्तम् ।
The *vṛtti* that is of the nature of contemplation/recollection (*cintana*) is *citta*.
अहम् इत्यभिमानात्मिका वृत्तिरहङ्कारः ।
The *vṛtti* that has the nature of 'I'-identification (abhimāna) is *ahaṅkāra* (ego).
268 · पञ्चभेदसहितप्राणोत्पत्तिः
अपञ्चीकृतपञ्चभूतसमष्टिरजोगुणांशात् पञ्चवृत्तिप्राणः सम्भूतः ।
From the collective (*samaṣṭi*) *rajas-guṇa* portion of the unquintuplicated five subtle elements arose *prāṇa* having five modes (functions).
स प्राणः क्रियाभेदात् स्थानभेदाच्च पञ्चविधः ।
That *prāṇa* is fivefold due to differences in function and differences in location.
यस्य हृदयं स्थानम्, क्षुत्पिपासे क्रिया स प्राणः ।
That whose location is the heart and whose function is hunger and thirst is *prāṇa*.
यस्य गुदः स्थानम्, मूत्रपुरीषयोरधोनयनं क्रिया स अपानः ।
That whose location is the anus and whose function is the downward evacuation of urine and feces is *apāna*.
यस्य नाभिः स्थानम्, भुक्तपीतयोरन्नपानयोः पाचनयोग्यसमीकरणं क्रिया स समानः ।
That whose location is the navel and whose function is the equal distribution of ingested food and drink suitable for digestion is *samāna*.
यस्य कण्ठः स्थानम्, श्वासः क्रिया स उदानः ।
That whose location is the throat and whose function is respiration (upward movement) is *udāna*.
यस्य सर्वशरीरं स्थानम्, अन्नपानादिरसस्य सर्वनाडीषु प्रवेशनं क्रिया स व्यानः ।
That whose location is the entire body and whose function is conveying the essence of food, drink, etc. into all the channels (*nāḍī*s) is *vyāna*.
क्वचित् नागकूर्मकृकरदेवदत्तधनञ्जयाख्याः पञ्च वायवोऽधिकतया पठ्यन्ते ।
In some texts, five additional vital airs named Nāga, Kūrma, Kṛkara, Devadatta, and Dhanañjaya are additionally enumerated.
तत्रोद्वमनकृत् नागः ।
Among them, Nāga is that which causes belching/vomiting.
उन्मीलनहिक्कादिकृत् कूर्मः ।
Kūrma causes the opening/closing of eyelids, hiccups, and the like.
क्षुतहेतुः कृकरः ।
Kṛkara is the cause of sneezing.
जृम्भणकरो देवदत्तः ।
Devadatta produces yawning.
श्वयथुकरो धनञ्जयः ।
Dhanañjaya causes swelling/nourishment.
एत उपवायवः ।
These are the subsidiary vital airs (upavāyus).
तेषां च पृथिवीजलतेजोवाय्वाकाशानां रजोगुणांशेभ्यः क्रमेणोत्पत्तिः ।
And their origin is stated to be respectively from the *rajas-guṇa* portions of earth, water, fire, air, and space.
तथैवापानसमानप्राणोदानव्यानानामपि क्रमेण पृथिव्यादीनामेकैकस्य रजोगुणांशादुत्पत्तिः ।
Likewise, it is said that the origin of *apāna*, *samāna*, *prāṇa*, *udāna*, and *vyāna* is respectively from the individual *rajas-guṇa* portion of earth and each subsequent element.
सर्वेषां समष्टिरजोगुणांशान्नोत्पत्तिः इति चोक्तं क्वचिद्ग्रन्थेषु ।
And in some texts, it is said that their origin is not from the aggregate (*samaṣṭi*) *rajas-guṇa* portion of all elements.
परन्त्वद्वैतसिद्धान्ते एषा प्रक्रिया नास्ति ।
However, in the Advaita Siddhānta, this method is not accepted.
विद्यारण्यस्वामिभिः, पञ्चीकरणग्रन्थे वार्तिककारैश्च सूक्ष्मशरीरे पञ्चकोशे च नागकूर्मादीनां ग्रहणं न कृतम् ।
Neither by Svāmī Vidyāraṇya nor by the Vārtikakāra in the *Pañcīkaraṇa-vārtika* was any inclusion made of Nāga, Kūrma, etc., in the subtle body (*sūkṣma-śarīra*) or among the five sheaths (*pañca-kośa*).
अपि च तैरपानादिपञ्चप्राणानां पञ्चभूतसमष्टिरजोगुणांशादुत्पत्तिर्वर्णिता ।
Moreover, they described the origin of the five vital airs (beginning with *apāna*) as arising from the collective (*samaṣṭi*) *rajas-guṇa* portion of the five elements.
तस्मादेकैकभूतव्यष्टिरजोगुणांशादपानादीनामुत्पत्तिकथनमयुक्तमेव ।
Therefore, asserting the origin of *apāna* and the others from the individual (*vyaṣṭi*) *rajas-guṇa* portions of each single element is indeed untenable.
तस्मात्सूक्ष्मशरीरे नागकूर्मादीनां ग्रहणमसङ्गतम् ।
Therefore, the inclusion of Nāga, Kūrma, etc. within the subtle body is inappropriate.
पञ्चप्राणानामेव सूक्ष्मशरीरे ग्रहणं युक्तम् ।
The inclusion of only the five *prāṇa*s in the subtle body is appropriate.
किञ्च प्राणो विक्षेपरूपः ।
Furthermore, *prāṇa* is of the nature of activity/motion (*vikṣepa*).
रजोगुणस्य विक्षेपः स्वभावः ।
Activity (*vikṣepa*) is the inherent nature of *rajas-guṇa*.
तस्मात्पञ्चभूतरजोगुणांशात्प्राणोत्पत्तिकथनं युक्तमेव ।
Therefore, describing the origin of *prāṇa* as being from the *rajas-guṇa* portions of the five elements is entirely correct.
269 · ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणां कर्मेन्द्रियाणां चोत्पत्तिः
अपञ्चीकृतैकैकभूतसत्त्वगुणांशात् पञ्चज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि रचितानि ।
From the sattva-guṇa portion of each individual unquintupled element, the five sense-organs of knowledge (jñānendriyas) are fashioned.
एकैकभूतरजोगुणांशादेकैकं कर्मेन्द्रियं रचितम् ।
From the rajo-guṇa portion of each element, each single organ of action (karmendriya) is fashioned.
आकाशस्य सत्त्वगुणात् श्रोत्रम्, वायोः सत्त्वगुणांशात् त्वक्, तेजसः सत्त्वगुणांशात् नेत्रम्, जलस्य सत्त्वगुणांशात् रसना, पृथिव्याः सत्त्वगुणांशात् घ्राणं चाजायत ।
From the sattva-guṇa of space, the ear arose; from the sattva-guṇa portion of air, the skin; from the sattva-guṇa portion of fire, the eye; from the sattva-guṇa portion of water, the tongue; and from the sattva-guṇa portion of earth, the nose arose.
एतानि पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि ज्ञानस्य साधनानि, अतो ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणीत्युच्यन्ते ।
These five sense-organs are instruments of knowledge; therefore, they are called 'organs of knowledge' (jñānendriyas).
ज्ञानं सत्त्वगुणाज्जायते ।
Knowledge is produced from sattva-guṇa.
अतश्चैतानि पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि भूतानां सत्त्वगुणादुत्पन्नत्वेनोच्यन्ते ।
And therefore, these five sense-organs are stated to be born from the sattva-guṇa of the elements.
श्रोत्रेन्द्रियमाकाशस्य गुणं शब्दं गृह्णातीति तदाकाशस्य सत्त्वगुणकार्यम् ।
Because the organ of hearing grasps sound, which is the quality of space, it is an effect of the sattva-guṇa of space.
एवमेव यदिन्द्रियं यस्य भूतस्य गुणं गृह्णाति तत्तस्य भूतस्य सत्त्वगुणकार्यमिति ज्ञेयम् ।
In the same manner, whichever sense-organ perceives the quality of a particular element, it should be understood to be the effect of the sattva-guṇa of that element.
आकाशस्य रजोगुणांशात् वाक्, वायो रजोगुणांशात् पाणिः, अग्ने रजोगुणांशात् पादः, जलस्य रजोगुणांशात् उपस्थः, पृथिव्या रजोगुणांशात् गुदं चोत्पद्यते ।
From the rajo-guṇa portion of space arises speech; from the rajo-guṇa portion of air, the hand; from the rajo-guṇa portion of fire, the foot; from the rajo-guṇa portion of water, the genital organ; and from the rajo-guṇa portion of earth, the anus is produced.
स्त्रीयोनौ पुरुषलिङ्गे च वर्तमानं विषयानन्दलवसाधनमिन्द्रियं उपस्थ इत्युच्यते ।
The organ residing in the female and male generative organs, which serves as the means for experiencing a small fraction of sensual joy, is called the 'upastha'.
कर्मेति क्रियोच्यते ।
By 'karma', action (kriyā) is meant.
एतानि पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि क्रियासाधनत्वात् कर्मेन्द्रियाणीत्यभिधीयन्ते ।
These five organs, being instruments of action, are designated as 'organs of action' (karmendriyas).
क्रियाया रजोगुणकार्यत्वाद्भूतानां रजोगुणांशात्कर्मेन्द्रियोत्पत्तिर्वर्णिता ।
Because action is an effect of rajo-guṇa, the origin of the organs of action is described as being from the rajo-guṇa portion of the elements.
इत्थं सूक्ष्मसृष्टिर्निरूपिता ।
Thus the subtle creation has been expounded.
270 · सूक्ष्मसृष्टेरुपसंहारः
अपञ्चीकृतभूतानि तत्कार्यभूतान्तःकरणप्राणकर्मेन्द्रियाणि सूक्ष्मसृष्टिरिति कीर्त्यते ।
The unquintupled elements and their effects—the internal organ, the vital airs, and the organs of action (and knowledge)—are celebrated as 'subtle creation'.
सूक्ष्मसृष्टिविषयकं ज्ञानं नेन्द्रियैरुत्पद्यते ।
Knowledge concerning the subtle creation cannot be obtained through the senses.
नेत्रनासिकादिगोलकानि तु यद्यपीन्द्रियविषयाणि तथापि तत्तद्गोलकान्तःस्थेन्द्रियाणि न कस्यचिदपीन्द्रियस्य विषयीभवन्ति ।
Although the physical orifices/sockets such as the eyes and nose are indeed perceivable by the senses, the subtle faculties residing inside those respective physical organs never become the object of any sense-organ.
सूक्ष्मसृष्ट्युत्पत्त्यनन्तरमीश्वरेच्छया स्थूलसृष्टिनिमित्तं भूतानां पञ्चीकरणं निष्पद्यते ।
After the creation of the subtle world, by the will of Īśvara, the quintuplication (pañcīkaraṇa) of the elements takes place for the sake of gross creation.
स्थूलसृष्टिः॥ २७१–२७२ ॥
271 · पञ्चीकरणप्रकारःपञ्चीकरणे द्वौ प्रकारावुक्तौ । प्रथमप्रकारस्त्वेवं
एकैकसूक्ष्मभूतस्य तमोगुणांशं साम्येन द्विधा विभजेत् ।
One should divide the portion of tamas-guṇa of each subtle element equally into two parts.
तत्रैकमर्धं पृथगवस्थापयेत् ।
There, one should set aside one half separately.
ततोऽपरमर्धं साम्येन चतुर्धा विभजेत् ।
Then one should divide the other half equally into four parts.
एवं पुनर्विभागेन निष्पन्नमेकैकभूतस्याष्टममंशं पृथगवस्थापितेन स्वस्वेतरभूतचतुष्टयस्यार्धभागेन योजयेत् ।
Thus, one should combine the one-eighth portion of each element produced by subdivision with the half-portion of the other four elements set aside separately.
एवं पञ्चीकरणं निष्पद्यते ।
In this way, quintuplication (*pañcīkaraṇa*) is accomplished.
तत्रैकैकस्मिन्नपि स्थूलभूते एकमर्धं स्वांशः ।
There, in each gross element, one half is its own share.
अपरमर्धं तु स्वेतरैकैकभूताष्टमांशमेलनेन निष्पन्नम् ।
The other half, however, is formed by combining the one-eighth parts of each of the other elements.
एवमेकैकस्मिन्नपि स्थूलभूते पञ्चानामपि भूतानामंशसत्त्वात् स्थूलभूतानि पञ्चीकृतानीति वर्ण्यन्ते ।
Thus, because parts of all five elements are present in each gross element, the gross elements are described as 'quintupled'.
द्वितीयप्रकारस्त्वेवं - एकैकसूक्ष्मभूतस्य तमोगुणांशं वैषम्येण द्विधा विभजेत् ।
The second method, however, is as follows: one should divide the portion of tamas-guṇa of each subtle element unequally into two parts.
तत्रैको भागश्चतुर्भिरंशैर्निष्पन्नः ।
There, one part consists of four portions (four-fifths).
अपरस्तु भागः पञ्चमांशेन ।
The other part, however, consists of the one-fifth portion.
तत्र1
There—
टिप्पणी
1.
प्रथमप्रकारे प्रतिभूतमर्धभागस्य स्वकीयत्वेऽपीतरार्धभागस्य स्वेतरभूतचतुष्टयांशनिष्पन्नत्वात् तेन भागेन स्वभागस्य तिरोधानं सम्भाव्येत ।
In the first method, although half the portion in each element belongs to itself, since the other half is composed of the portions of the other four elements, the overshadowing of its own share by that portion might be possible.
ततश्चाकाशादीनां भूतानां प्रत्येकं पृथक् पृथग्भानं दुर्घटं स्यादिति मत्वा यथा प्रतिभूतं स्वांशाधिक्यं स्यात्तथा द्वितीयः प्रकार आश्रीयते ।
And considering that the distinct individual perception of elements like space and so forth would then be difficult to explain, the second method is adopted so that there is a preponderance of each element's own share in itself.
चतुरंशनिष्पन्नमधिकपरिमाणकं भागं पृथगवस्थापयेत् ।
One should set aside separately the larger portion consisting of four parts.
पञ्चमांशनिष्पन्नं न्यूनपरिमाणकं भागं पुनः पञ्चधा विभजेत् ।
One should divide the smaller portion (constituting one-fifth) again into five parts.
तत्रैकमेकमंशं पृथगवस्थापिताधिकपरिमाणकपञ्चभागेषु पृथक् पृथग्योजयेत् ।
There, one should add each one of those parts separately into the five set-aside larger portions.
अनेनापि प्रकारेण पञ्चीकरणं सिद्ध्यति ।
By this method also, quintuplication (*pañcīkaraṇa*) is accomplished.
तत्र प्रथमप्रकारे प्रतिभूतमेकमर्धं स्वांशः ।
In the first method, one half in each element is its own share.
अपरमर्धं तु स्वेतरभूतचतुष्टयस्यांशः ।
The other half, however, is the share of the four elements other than itself.
यथा आकाशे एकमर्धं स्वस्यैवांशः ।
For example, in space, one half is its very own share.
द्वितीयमर्धं तु वायोरष्टमांशेन, तेजसोऽष्टमांशेन, जलस्याष्टमांशेन, पृथिव्या अष्टमांशेन च निष्पन्नम् ।
The second half, however, is formed by one-eighth of air, one-eighth of fire, one-eighth of water, and one-eighth of earth.
एवं भूतान्तरेष्वप्यूह्यम् ।
In this way it should be inferred for the other elements as well.
द्वितीयप्रकारे तु प्रतिभूतमेको भागः स्वकीयैरेकविंशत्यंशैर्निष्पन्नः ।
In the second method, however, one part in each element is composed of twenty-one parts of its own.
द्वितीयो भागस्तु स्वेतरभूतानां चतुर्भिरंशैर्निष्पन्नः ।
The second part, however, is formed by four parts from the elements other than itself.
यथा आकाशे एको भागः स्वकीयैकविंशत्यंशात्मकः ।
For example, in space, one part consists of twenty-one parts of its own.
अपरो भागस्तु वायोः पञ्चविंशांशेन, तजसः पञ्चविंशांशेन, जलस्य पञ्चविंशांशेन, पृथिव्याः पञ्चविंशांशेन च निष्पन्नः ।
The other part, however, is formed by one-twenty-fifth of air, one-twenty-fifth of fire, one-twenty-fifth of water, and one-twenty-fifth of earth.
एवं भूतान्तरेष्वप्यूहनीयम् ।
In this way it should be inferred in the case of the other elements as well.
प्रथमप्रकारापेक्षया द्वितीयप्रकारे प्रतिभूतं स्वांशाधिक्याद्विविच्य पृथक् पृथगाकाशादीनां भानं सुघटं भवति ।
Compared to the first method, in the second method, because of the preponderance of its own portion in each element, the distinct perception of space and the other elements separately is easily explained.
272 · स्थूलब्रह्माण्डाद्युत्पत्तिः
एवं पञ्चीकृतभूतेभ्य इन्द्रियगोचरं स्थूलब्रह्माण्डं उत्पद्यते ।
Thus, from the quintuplicated elements, the gross universe perceptible to the senses is produced.
तस्मिन् ब्रह्माण्डे भूर्भुवस्वर्महर्जनस्तपस्सत्य इत्युपरि सप्त लोकाः, अतलसुतलपातालवितलरसातलतलातलमहातला इत्यधः सप्त लोका वर्तन्ते ।
In that universe, there are seven upper worlds, namely Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, Tapaḥ, and Satyam; and seven nether worlds below, namely Atala, Sutala, Pātāla, Vitala, Rasātala, Talātala, and Mahātala.
एषु चतुर्दशसु लोकेषु वसतां जीवानां पृथक्पृथगुपभोगयोग्यान्नपानादिकं, देवमनुष्यपश्वादिरूपाणि भोगायतनानि स्थूलशरीराणि चोत्पद्यन्ते ।
For the jīvas residing in these fourteen worlds, their respective objects of experience such as food and drink, as well as gross bodies in the forms of gods, humans, animals, etc., which serve as the seats of experiencing pleasure and pain, are produced.
इत्थं सङ्क्षेपेण सृष्टिरुक्ता ।
In this way, creation has been described in brief.
मायावैभवस्य विस्तरेण निरूपणं तु कोटिब्रह्मायुषापि न शक्यते ।
However, expounding the magnificence of māyā in full detail is not possible even within the lifespan of crores of Brahmās.
मायासृष्टपदार्थानां नान्तोऽस्तीति वाल्मीकिर्वासिष्ठे नानेतिहासैर्निरूपितवान् ।
Sage Vālmīki has expounded through various stories in the Yogavāsiṣṭha that there is no end to the things created by māyā.
आत्मविवेकः, अथवा पञ्चकोशविवेकः॥ २७३ ॥
273
पञ्चकोशास्तैरात्मन आवरणं च1
The five sheaths (*pañcakośa*) and the concealment of the *ātman* by them.
टिप्पणी
1.
स्थूलशरीरं - स्थूलसूक्ष्मकारणात्मकानि त्रीणि शरीराणि सन्ति ।
Gross body: There are three bodies, consisting of the gross, subtle, and causal.
प्रतिक्षणं शीर्यमाणत्वात् शरीरं इति व्यपदेशः ।
It is designated as 'śarīra' because it continually decays at every moment.
दह्यमानत्वात् देह इति तस्यैव व्यपदेशः ।
It is also designated as 'deha' because it is subject to being consumed by fire.
लोमत्वक्सिरामांसास्थिमज्जानां षण्णां समुदायः स्तम्भादिवत्प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानत्वात् स्थूलदेह इत्युच्यते ।
The aggregate of the six components—hair, skin, blood vessels, flesh, bones, and marrow—is called the gross body because it is directly perceived like a pillar or other objects.
स च देहः पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वात्मकः ।
And that body consists of twenty-five elements.
तानि च तत्त्वानि निम्नदेशे प्रदर्शितपताकया सुखं ज्ञातुं शक्यानि ॥
And those principles can be easily understood from the chart shown below.
मायायां तत्कार्येषु च त्रीणि शरीराणि पञ्च कोशाश्चान्तर्भवन्ति ।
Within *māyā* and its effects, the three bodies and five sheaths are included.
शुद्धसत्त्वगुणप्रधाना मायेश्वरस्य कारणशरीरम् ।
*Māyā*, predominated by pure *sattva*, is the causal body of Īśvara.
मलिनसत्त्वप्रधानाविद्यांशो जीवस्य कारणशरीरम् ।
The portion of *avidyā* predominated by impure *sattva* (*malinasattva*) is the causal body of the *jīva*.
तदंशा एते मुख्यतत्त्वानि पृथिवी आपः तेजः वायुः आकाशः पृथिवी अस्थि मांसं नाड्यः त्वक् लोम आपः रक्तं शुक्रं मूत्रं स्वेदः लाला तेजः आलस्यं कान्तिः क्षुत् पिपासा निद्रा वायुः आकुञ्चनं गमनं स्थितिः धावनं प्रसारणं आकाशः भयं अथवा कटिः मोहः अथवा उदरं क्रोधः अथवा हृदयं कामः अथवा कण्ठः शोकः अथवा शिरः
Their parts are these: the primary elements are Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Space. Under Earth: bone, flesh, nerves, skin, and hair. Under Water: blood, semen, urine, sweat, and saliva. Under Fire: sloth, complexion, hunger, thirst, and sleep. Under Air: contraction, locomotion, standing/stability, running, and expansion. Under Space: fear (or waist), delusion (or belly), anger (or heart), desire (or throat), and grief (or head).
आत्मबोधे पञ्चप्राणमनोबुद्धिदशेन्द्रियसमन्वितम् । अपञ्चीकृतभूतोत्थं सूक्ष्माङ्गं भोगसाधनम् ॥ १३॥ इति ।
In the *Ātmabodha* (13) it is said: Endowed with the five vital airs, the mind, the intellect, and the ten sense-organs, originated from the unquintuplicated elements, is the subtle body, the vehicle of experience.
तत्र प्राणाः पञ्च, कर्मेन्द्रियाणि पञ्च, ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि पञ्च, मन एकम्, बुद्धिश्चैकेति सप्तदशतत्त्वानि मिलित्वा लिङ्गं इत्युच्यते ।
Therein, the five vital airs, five organs of action, five organs of perception, one mind, and one intellect—these seventeen principles combining together are called the subtle body (*liṅga*).
शुभाशुभकर्मकर्तृत्वम्, सुखदुःखादिफलभोक्तृत्वम्, इहलोकपरलोकादिगमनागमने, रागद्वेषादि, शमदमादि, आन्ध्यमान्द्यपटुत्वादि च सर्वं लिङ्गशरीरधर्माः ।
Agency of good and evil deeds, experiencership of fruits such as pleasure and pain, transmigrating to this world and other worlds, attachment and hatred, tranquility and sense-control, blindness, dullness, sharpness of senses, etc.—all these are attributes of the subtle body (*liṅga-śarīra*).
स्थूलशरीरवत्प्रत्यक्षप्रमाणागोचरत्वात्सूक्ष्मशरीरमित्युच्यते ।
Unlike the gross body, because it is beyond the scope of direct sensory perception, it is called the subtle body (*sūkṣma-śarīra*).
शब्दादिविषयोपलब्धिहेतुत्वात्, लक्षणया आत्मावबोधकत्वाच्च लिङ्गदेह इति कीर्त्यते ॥
Because it is the cause of cognition of objects like sound, etc., and because it indicatively points to the *ātman*, it is called the *liṅga-deha* (indicative body).
भूतं यं कमपि पदार्थमात्मत्वेन मन्यमानाः कोशानां साक्षिभूतान्मुख्यात्मस्वरूपाद्विमुखा भवन्ति ।
Considering whatever material entity as the Self, people turn away from the essential nature of the primary *ātman*, which is the witness (*sākṣin*) of the sheaths.
अत एवान्नमयादयः कोशा आत्मस्वरूपाच्छादका इति वर्ण्यन्ते ।
Therefore, the sheaths beginning with *annamaya* are described as coverers/veilers of the essential nature of the *ātman*.
274
केचन पामरा विरोचनसिद्धान्तमनुसरन्तोऽन्नमयकोशमेवात्मेति वदन्ति ।
Some ignorant people, following the doctrine of Virocana, assert that the food-sheath (*annamayakośa*) alone is the Self.
तत्रैवं युक्तीः कथयन्ति ।
In support of this, they state the following arguments:
(१) यत्राहमिति धीरुत्पद्यते, स आत्मा ।
(1) That entity with reference to which the cognition 'I' arises is the Self.
सा चाहन्धीः स्थूलशरीरे भवति ।
And that 'I'-cognition occurs with respect to the gross body.
अहं मनुष्यः अहं ब्राह्मणः इत्यनुभवः सार्वजनीनः ।
Experiences such as 'I am a human' and 'I am a Brāhmaṇa' are universal.
मनुष्यत्वब्राह्मणत्वादिधर्माः स्थूलशरीरस्यैव ।
The attributes such as humanness and Brāhmaṇa-hood belong solely to the gross body.
तस्मादहन्धीविषयः स्थूलदेह एवात्मा ।
Therefore, the gross body alone, which is the object of the 'I'-cognition, is the Self.
अथवा यत्र मुख्या प्रीतिर्भवति स आत्मा ।
Alternatively, that towards which primary love is directed is the Self.
दारापत्यधनपश्वादयो यतोऽस्य स्थूलदेहस्योपकुर्वन्ति ततस्तेषु प्रीतिर्भवति ।
Because wife, children, wealth, cattle, and so on serve this gross body, love is directed towards them.
अज्ञानमेव कारणशरीरमित्युच्यते ।
Ignorance (*avidyā*) alone is called the causal body (*kāraṇa-śarīra*).
स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीरयोः कारणत्वादज्ञानं कारणशरीरमित्युच्यते ।
Because it is the cause of both the gross and subtle bodies, ignorance is designated as the causal body.
अस्य च स्वरूपं प्रागभिहितम् ।
And its essential nature has been explained earlier.
तत्त्वज्ञानदाह्यत्वात् कारणदेह इति चोच्यतेऽज्ञानमेव ।
And because it is burnt up by the knowledge of truth, ignorance alone is called the causal body (*kāraṇa-deha*).
समष्ट्यज्ञानरूपमायेश्वरस्य कारणशरीरम् ।
*Māyā*, in the form of collective ignorance (*samaṣṭy-ajñāna*), is the causal body of *Īśvara*.
सैवेश्वरस्य आनन्दमयकोशः ।
That itself is the bliss-sheath (*ānandamayakośa*) of *Īśvara*.
जीवानां सूक्ष्मशरीरसमष्टिरूपहिरण्यगर्भः ईश्वरस्य सूक्ष्मशरीरम् ।
*Hiraṇyagarbha*, constituting the totality of subtle bodies of the *jīva*s, is the subtle body of *Īśvara*.
अत्रेश्वरस्य विज्ञानमयमनोमयप्राणमयकोशा अन्तर्भवन्ति ।
Within this are included the *vijñānamaya*, *manomaya*, and *prāṇamaya* sheaths of *Īśvara*.
श्रोत्रादिपञ्चज्ञानेन्द्रियाधिष्ठातृदेवतारूपदिक्पालवायुसूर्यवरुणाश्विनीकुमारात्मकानि यानीश्वरस्य पञ्चज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि तानि, समष्टिबुद्धिमयमहत्तत्त्वरूपः, अथवा सर्वबुद्ध्यभिमानिब्रह्मरूपा येश्वरस्य बुद्धिः सा च मिलित्वा ईश्वरस्य विज्ञानमयकोशः ।
The five organs of knowledge of *Īśvara*, which are of the nature of the directional deities, Vāyu, Sūrya, Varuṇa, and the Aśvinīkumāras—who preside over the five sense organs like the ear—combined with *Īśvara*'s intellect (which is in the form of the cosmic *mahat-tattva*, or Brahmā identifying with all intellects), constitute the *vijñānamayakośa* of *Īśvara*.
पूर्वोक्तश्रोत्राद्यधिष्ठातृदेवतारूपाणि यानीश्वरस्य पञ्च ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि तानि, समष्टिमनोमयाहङ्काररूपं वा सर्वमनोऽभिमानिचन्द्ररूपं वा यदीश्वरस्य मनस्तच्च मिलित्वा ईश्वरस्य मनोमयकोशः ।
The aforesaid five organs of knowledge of *Īśvara*, together with the mind of *Īśvara* (which is in the form of cosmic mental ego, or the Moon-god identifying with all minds), constitute the *manomayakośa* of *Īśvara*.
अग्नीन्द्रोपेन्द्रप्रजापतियमात्मकानि यानीश्वरस्य पञ्च कर्मेन्द्रियाणि तानि, समष्टिप्राणो वा वाय्वभिमानिदेवतारूपो वा य ईश्वरस्य प्राणः स च मिलित्वा ईश्वरस्य प्राणमयकोशः ।
The five organs of action of *Īśvara*, which are of the nature of Agni, Indra, Upendra, Prajāpati, and Yama, together with *Īśvara*'s cosmic vital energy (*prāṇa*, or the deity presiding over air), constitute the *prāṇamayakośa* of *Īśvara*.
समष्टिस्थूलसृष्टिरूपो विराडीश्वरस्य स्थूलशरीरम् ।
*Virāj*, embodying the totality of gross creation, is the gross body of *Īśvara*.
स एवेश्वरस्यान्नमयकोशः ।
That itself is the *annamayakośa* of *Īśvara*.
मातापितृभ्यामुपभुक्तान्नरसपरिणामरूपशुक्रशोणितसम्बन्धान्मातुरुदरे उत्पन्नो जननानन्तरमपि क्षीरशाकादिरूपान्नेन वर्धितो मरणानन्तरमप्यन्नरूपपृथिव्यामेव लीयमानो देहोऽन्नमयकोश उच्यते ।
The physical body—conceived in the mother's womb through the union of semen and ovum derived from the essence of food consumed by parents, nourished after birth by food like milk and vegetables, and dissolving after death into the earth that is food—is termed the *annamayakośa*.
प्राणमयकोशस्तु केवलरजोगुणस्यावस्थाविशेषः ।
The *prāṇamayakośa*, on the other hand, is a specific state born solely of the quality of *rajas*.
प्राणादयो वायव आपादमस्तकं स्थूलदेहं व्याप्य, तस्य बलमाधायेन्द्रियाणि स्वस्वव्यापारेषु प्रवर्तयन्ति ।
The vital airs such as *prāṇa*, pervading the physical body from head to foot and imparting strength to it, impel the organs to their respective functions.
कर्मेन्द्रियैर्व्यवहारनिर्वर्तनादिच्छादिरूपरजोगुणवृत्तिसहितत्वाच्च मनोमयकोशः सत्त्वरजोगुणयोरवस्थाविशेषः ।
And because it carries out transactions via the motor organs and is accompanied by rajasic modifications such as desire, the *manomayakośa* is a specific state composed of both *sattva* and *rajas*.
विज्ञानमयकोशस्तु केवलसत्त्वगुणस्यावस्थाविशेषः ।
The *vijñānamayakośa*, on the other hand, is a specific state born purely of the quality of *sattva*.
एवमवस्थाभेदेनैकस्मिन्नेव सूक्ष्मशरीरे त्रयः कोशा वर्ण्यन्ते ।
Thus, by virtue of different states, three sheaths are described within one single subtle body.
आनन्द एवात्मनः स्वरूपम् ।
Bliss alone is the essential nature of the *ātman*.
आत्मस्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बसहिता प्रियमोदप्रमोदरूपवृत्तिलयाविधभूता या अविद्या सैव कारणदेहः ।
That *avidyā*, endowed with the reflection of the bliss of the Self and serving as the terminus of dissolution for the mental states of *priya*, *moda*, and *pramoda*, is itself the causal body (*kāraṇa-deha*).
सैवानन्दमयकोशश्च ।
And that alone is the bliss-sheath (*ānandamayakośa*).
इष्टवस्तुदर्शनजन्या वृत्तिः प्रिय इति, तल्लाभजन्या वृत्तिः प्रमोद इति च कीर्त्यते ।
The mental modification born from merely seeing a cherished object is termed *priya*, while that born from acquiring it is called *pramoda*.
एता वृत्तयो जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोरवस्थयोः पुण्यकर्मफलभूतसुखानुभवकाले उद्भवन्ति ।
These mental modifications arise in the waking and dream states during the experience of joy born of meritorious deeds.
सुषुप्तौ ता वृत्तयः स्वकारणेऽज्ञाने लीयन्ते एतादृशमज्ञानमानन्दमयकोश इत्युच्यते ।
In deep sleep (*suṣupti*), these modifications merge into their cause, ignorance; such ignorance is termed the *ānandamayakośa*.
तत्रान्नमयकोशो भोगस्थानम् ।
Among them, the food-sheath is the locus of experiencing pleasures and pains.
यदि तेऽस्य स्थूलदेहस्य नोपकुर्वन्ति तदा तेषु प्रीतिर्नास्ति ।
If they do not benefit this gross body, then there is no love for them.
यस्य निमित्तेनान्यत्र प्रीतिरुपजायते तस्मिन्नेव स्थूले देहे मुख्या प्रीतिः सर्वेषाम् ।
That for whose sake love arises towards other things—in that very gross body alone lies the primary love of all.
तस्मात् स्थूलदेह एवात्मा ।
Therefore, the gross body alone is the ātman.
तस्माद्वस्त्राभरणान्नपानाद्युपकरणैः स्थूलशरीरस्य समलङ्कृत्य पोषणमेव परमपुरुषार्थ इत्यसुरराजविरोचनस्य सिद्धान्तः ।
Therefore, nicely adorning and nourishing the gross body with accessories such as clothes, ornaments, food, and drink alone is the supreme human goal—this is the doctrine of Virocana, king of the Asuras.
सूक्ष्मशरीरं भोगसाधनम् ।
The subtle body is the instrument of experience.
तत्रापि प्राणमयकोशः क्रियाशक्तिमत्त्वात् कार्यरूपो भवति ।
Therein also, the prāṇamayakośa, having the power of action, is in the nature of an effect (instrument of action).
मनोमयकोशस्तु इच्छाशक्तिमत्त्वात्करणरूपो भवति ।
The manomayakośa, however, having the power of desire, is of the nature of an instrument.
विज्ञानमयकोशस्तु ज्ञानशक्तिमत्त्वात् कर्तृरूपो भवति ।
The vijñānamayakośa, however, having the power of knowledge, is of the nature of the agent (doer).
आनन्दमयकोशस्तु भोक्तृरूपः ।1
And the ānandamayakośa is of the nature of the experiencer (enjoyer).
टिप्पणी
1.
चार्वाकमतानुसारिणो वाय्वादिभूतचतुष्टयसङ्घातरूपं देहमात्मत्वेन प्रतिपन्नास्तत्रैता युक्तीराहुः -
The followers of the Cārvāka view, having accepted the physical body—which is an aggregate of the four elements beginning with air—as the ātman, state these arguments in that regard:
(१) अहन्धीविषयो यः स आत्मा ।
(1) That which is the object of the 'I'-cognition is the ātman.
अहं मनुष्यः अहं स्थूलः अहं कृशः अहं ब्राह्मणः इत्याद्यनुभवेषु मनुष्यत्वादिधर्मविशिष्टः स्थूलदेह एव विषयो भवतीति स देह एवात्मा ।
In experiences such as 'I am human', 'I am stout', 'I am thin', 'I am a Brāhmaṇa', only the gross body qualified by attributes like humanness is the object; therefore, that body alone is the ātman.
(२) अथवा परमप्रेमविषयो यः स आत्मा ।
(2) Alternatively, that which is the object of supreme love is the ātman.
एतत्स्थूलदेहोपकारकत्वनिमित्तं पुरस्कृत्यैव पुत्रमित्रकलत्रादयः प्रिया भवन्ति ।
Only because they are beneficial to this gross body do sons, friends, wives, and so forth become dear.
अतो देह एव परमप्रीतेर्विषयः ।
Therefore, the body alone is the object of supreme love.
एवं परमप्रेमास्पदत्वरूपात्मलक्षणयोगात्स्थूलदेह एवात्मा ।
Thus, due to fitting the definition of the ātman as the object of supreme love, the gross body alone is the ātman.
(३) तस्य देहस्यालङ्करणपोषणादिजन्यभोग एव परमपुरुषार्थः ।
(3) The enjoyment produced by adorning and nourishing that body is alone the supreme goal of human life.
(४) मरणमेव मोक्षः ।
(4) Death alone is mokṣa.
(५) प्रत्यक्षमेकमेव प्रमाणं नान्यत्प्रमाणमस्तीति ।
(5) Direct perception alone is the valid means of knowledge; no other means of knowledge exists—thus they claim.
तदेतच्चार्वाकमतमसङ्गतं - (१) अहं पश्यामि अहं वदामि इत्यादिव्यवहारेष्विन्द्रियस्याप्यहन्धीविषयत्वं दृश्यते ।
This Cārvāka doctrine is untenable: (1) In usages like 'I see' and 'I speak', sense organs too are seen to be the object of the 'I'-cognition.
(२) मम देहः कृशः इत्यादिव्यवहारेषु देहस्य ममताविषयत्वमपि भवति ।
(2) In usages such as 'my body is thin', the body is also an object of the sense of 'mine' (possession).
यो ममताविषयः स अहन्ताविषयो न भवितुमर्हति ।
That which is the object of 'mine' cannot be the object of 'I'.
इत्थं स्थूलदेहे अहन्धीविषयत्वस्य व्यभिचारदर्शनात्स्थूलदेहो नात्मा ।
Thus, since being the object of the 'I'-cognition is inconstant (deviates) regarding the gross body, the gross body is not the ātman.
(३) पुत्रदाराद्यपेक्षया स्थूलदेहेऽधिकप्रीतिदर्शनेऽपि देहादप्यतिशयिता प्रीतिरिन्द्रियेषु दृश्यते ।
(3) Although greater love is seen for the gross body compared to sons, wife, etc., even greater love than for the body is seen towards the senses.
तथा च परप्रेमास्पदत्वस्याप्यभावात् स्थूलदेहो नात्मा ।
And so, since it lacks being the object of supreme love as well, the gross body is not the ātman.
(४) किञ्च चेतन एवात्मा भवितुमर्हति ।
(4) Furthermore, only a conscious principle can be the ātman.
जडानां भूतानां सङ्घातरूपे देहे चैतन्याभावाद्देहो नात्मा ।
Because there is no consciousness in the body which is an aggregate of inert elements, the body is not the ātman.
(५) पूगचूर्णादिसंयुक्तताम्बूलपत्रे रागजननशक्तिवत् भूतसमुदायात्मकदेहे ज्ञानशक्तिरस्तीत्येतन्न युज्यते ।
(5) The claim that just as the capacity to produce red coloration arises in a betel leaf mixed with areca-nut and lime, so too the capacity of knowledge exists in a body composed of elements, is untenable.
जडभूतसमुदायरूपदेहे ज्ञानशक्तिरस्ति चेत्तर्हि भूतसमुदायरूपघटादावपि चैतन्यं प्रसज्येत ।
If the capacity for knowledge were present in the body which is a collection of inert elements, then consciousness would absurdly result in pots and the like as well, which are also aggregates of elements.
न तु घटादौ चैतन्यमस्ति ।
However, consciousness does not exist in a pot and the like.
(६) सुषुप्तिमूर्च्छामरणाद्यवस्थासु घटादिवद्देहोऽपि जडो भवति ।
(6) In states such as deep sleep, fainting, and death, the body too becomes completely inert like a pot.
तस्मान्न जडो देह आत्मा भवति ।
Therefore, the inert body cannot be the ātman.
(७) यदि देह आत्मा भवेत्तदा बालदेहाद्भिन्ने यौवनदेहे सोऽहम् इति प्रत्यभिज्ञा न भवितुमर्हति ।
(7) If the body were the ātman, then in the youthful body—which is distinct from the childhood body—the recognition 'I am that same person' could not occur.
जायते तु तथा प्रत्यभिज्ञा ।
However, such recognition does arise.
अतोऽपि देहो नात्मा ।
For this reason too, the body is not the ātman.
(८) जन्ममरणादियुक्तस्य देहस्य जन्मनः पूर्वं मरणादूर्ध्वं च सत्ता नास्ति ।
(8) The body, which is subject to birth, death, and so forth, has no existence before birth or after death.
आत्मा त्वस्ति ।
The ātman, however, does exist.
अन्यथा कृतनाशाकृताभ्यागमप्रसङ्गः स्यात् ।
Otherwise, the fallacies of the destruction of deeds done (*kṛta-nāśa*) and the accrual of results for deeds not done (*akṛtābhyāgama*) would result.
अतश्च देहो नात्मा ।
And for this reason also, the body is not the ātman.
(९) देहालङ्करणपोषणादिजन्यभोग एव परमपुरुषार्थ इत्यपि न ।
(9) Nor is it true that enjoyment born of adorning and nourishing the body is alone the supreme human goal.
तथा हि, यः इच्छाविषयः स पुरुषार्थ इत्युच्यते ।
To explain: that which is the object of desire is called *puruṣārtha* (human goal).
सा चेच्छा सर्वेषां सुखप्राप्तौ दुःखनिवृत्तौ च भवति ।
And that desire for all living beings is directed towards the attainment of happiness and the cessation of suffering.
अतस्तयोरेव पुरुषार्थत्वमुचितम् ।
Therefore, being a human goal belongs properly only to those two.
तत्रापि सर्वसुखापेक्षया अधिकं यत्सुखम्, आत्यन्तिकी च या दुःखनिवृत्तिस्तयोरेव परमपुरुषार्थत्वं भवति ।
Even there, that happiness which is superior to all pleasures, and that cessation of sorrow which is absolute—only to these two does the status of being the supreme human goal (*parama-puruṣārtha*) belong.
तादृशं निरतिशयं सुखम् ॥
Such unexcelled bliss [is the Self alone].
