275 · इन्द्रियात्मवादः
अपरे केचनैवमाहुः स्थूलशरीरं नात्मा ।
Some others say thus: 'The gross body is not the ātman.'
किन्तु स्थूलशरीरे यत्सद्भावे जीवनव्यवहारो भवति, यदभावे मरणव्यवहारो भवति स आत्मा ।
'Rather, that by whose presence in the gross body the usage of living occurs, and by whose absence the usage of death occurs, that is the ātman.'
स च स्थूलशरीराद्व्यतिरिक्तः ।
'And that is distinct from the gross body.'
जीवनमरणव्यवहाराविन्द्रियाधीनौ भवतः ।
'The conventions of living and dying are dependent upon the sense-organs.'
शरीरे यावत्कालपर्यन्तमिन्द्रियाणि स्वस्वव्यापारक्षमाणि भवन्ति तावत्कालपर्यन्तं अयं जीवति इति व्यवहारो भवति ।
'For as long as the sense-organs in the body remain capable of their respective functions, so long does the usage 'this person is alive' take place.'
यस्य कस्यापीन्द्रियस्य नाशे अयं मृतः इति च व्यवह्रियते ।
'And upon the destruction of any sense-organ whatsoever, it is spoken of as 'this person is dead' (with respect to that function).'
किञ्च अहं पश्यामि अहं वदामि इत्यादिव्यवहारे अहम् इति बुद्धिरिन्द्रिये एव भवति ।
'Furthermore, in everyday expressions such as 'I see' and 'I speak', the cognition 'I' pertains only to the sense-organ.'
तस्मात् अहम् इति बुद्धिविषयेन्द्रियमेवात्मा ।
'Therefore, the sense-organ alone, being the object of the 'I'-cognition, is the ātman.'
276 · हिरण्यगर्भोपासकानां प्राणात्मवादः
हिरण्यगर्भोपासकाः प्राण एवात्मेति वदन्ति ।
The worshippers of Hiraṇyagarbha state that prāṇa alone is the ātman.
आत्यन्तिकी दुःखनिवृत्तिश्च मोक्षे एव स्तः ।
And absolute cessation of sorrow exists only in liberation.
वैषयिकभोगे दोषसत्त्वान्न स परमपुरुषार्थः ।
Sensual enjoyment is not the supreme goal of human life, because of the presence of defects in it.
(१०) देहस्यात्मत्वे मरणानन्तरं देहस्य दाहे मोक्षान्वयिनो देहरूपस्यात्मन एवाभावात् मरणमेव मोक्षः इति शब्दो निरर्थकः ।
(10) If the body were the ātman, then upon the burning of the body after death, since the ātman in the form of the body that would be linked with liberation does not exist at all, the statement 'Death alone is liberation' is meaningless.
(११) भाविभोजनादौ तृप्त्यादिहेतुत्वज्ञानमनुमानप्रमाणेन सिद्ध्यति ।
(11) The knowledge that future food and the like are the causes of satisfaction is established through the means of inference.
देशान्तरे मृतपित्रादिमरणज्ञानमाप्तवाक्यरूपशब्दप्रमाणात् सिद्ध्यति ।
The knowledge of the demise of a father or others who died in another country is established from the instrument of verbal testimony in the form of a statement of a trustworthy person.

टिप्पणी
1.
मनात्मवादखण्डनं - नारदपाञ्चरात्रतन्त्रानुसारिणो मन एवात्मेति वदन्ति ।
Refutation of the doctrine that the mind is the ātman: The followers of the Nārada-Pāñcarātra Tantra assert that the mind alone is the ātman.
तदपि न सम्भवति ।
That too is not possible.
(१) टङ्कवास्यादिवन्मनसः करणत्वान्न मन आत्मा ।
(1) Because the mind is an instrument like a chisel, an adze, etc., the mind is not the ātman.
(२) सूषुप्त्यादौ मसनोऽभावेऽपि सामान्यचैतन्यस्य सत्त्वात्, सति मनसि चैतन्यं तदभावे तदभावः इत्यन्वयव्यतिरेकस्य भङ्गात् न मनश्चेतनम्, किन्तु जडमेव ।
(2) Since general consciousness exists even in the absence of the mind in deep sleep, etc., the rule of positive-and-negative concomitance—'when the mind exists, consciousness exists; in its absence, consciousness is absent'—breaks down; hence the mind is not conscious, but merely insentient.
तस्मान्मनो नात्मा ।
Therefore, the mind is not the ātman.
(३) मम मनोऽन्यत्र गतम्, इदानीं प्रत्यागतम् इति व्यवहारान्मनो ममताया विषयो नाहन्तायाः ।
(3) From the common experience 'My mind had gone elsewhere; now it has returned', the mind is the object of the notion of 'mine', not of 'I'.
तस्मान्मनसः स्थैर्यचाञ्चल्यादिवेत्ता साक्षीभूत आत्मा मनोविलक्षणः सिद्धः ।
Therefore, the ātman, which is the witness and the knower of the mind's steadiness, restlessness, etc., is established as distinct from the mind.
(४) चैतन्याभाससहितमेव मनो भोक्तृ भवति, न स्वतन्त्रं मनः ।
(4) The mind becomes an experiencer only when endowed with the reflection of consciousness (*cidābhāsa*), not independently.
अतोऽभोक्तृत्वादपि मनो नात्मा ।
Hence, also because it is non-experiencing on its own, the mind is not the ātman.
(५) मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः । बन्धाय विषयासक्तं मुक्त्यै निर्विषयं स्मृतम् ॥ इति वचनास्यायमाशयः - विषयवासनावासितं मनो मोक्षसाधनं प्रतिबद्ध्य जगदध्यासास्पदं भूत्वा बन्धकारणं भवति ।
(5) As for the statement: The mind alone is the cause of human beings' bondage and liberation; attached to objects it leads to bondage, free of objects it leads to liberation, this is its import: the mind, when tainted by impressions of sense objects, obstructs the means to liberation, becomes the locus for the superimposition of the world, and thus serves as the cause of bondage.
तदेव च मनो विषयवासनारहितं ज्ञानप्राप्तिद्वारा मनसः स्वरूपं बाधित्वा मोक्षकारणं भवतीति ।
And that very mind, freed from the latent impressions of objects, by subverting its own form through the attainment of knowledge, becomes the cause of *mokṣa*.
न तद्वाक्यं मनस एवात्मतां बोधयति ।
That statement does not teach that the mind itself is the ātman.
किन्तु बन्धसाधनान्निवृत्तिं मोक्षसाधने प्रवृत्तिं तद्वाक्यं बोधयति ।
Rather, that statement teaches turning away from the means of bondage and engaging in the means to liberation.
(६) मनो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् (तै. भृ. ४) इत्यादिना मनोमयकोशस्यात्मत्वबोधकश्रुतेस्तात्पर्यं तु स्थूलारुन्धतीन्यायेनेति प्राक् प्रदर्शितम् ।
(6) As for Śruti passages that seem to teach the *manomaya-kośa* as the ātman, such as He understood mind as Brahman (Taittirīya Upaniṣad, Bhṛguvallī 4), their true purport operates by the *sthūlārundhatī-nyāya* (the method of pointing to a subtle star by first indicating a gross one), as was already shown earlier.
स्थितिः सिद्ध्यति ।
Such a state is established.
तादृशी स्थितिरेव तन्मते मोक्षः ।
Such a state itself is *mokṣa* in their doctrine.
इत्थं विज्ञानवादिनो बुद्धेः क्षणिकतां स्वयम्प्रकाशरूपतां च कल्पयित्वा, सा बुद्धिरेवात्मेति वर्णयन्ति ।
Thus, the Vijñānavādins, hypothesising momentariness and self-luminosity in the intellect (*buddhi*), describe that intellect alone as the ātman.
आनन्दमयकोक्ष एवात्मेति मतम्॥ २७९–२८२ ॥
279 · तत्र भट्टमतं
पूर्वमीमांसावार्तिककारो भट्ट एवमाह - न हि विद्युल्लेखेवात्मा क्षणिकः, किन्तु स्थिरः ।
The author of the Pūrvamīmāṃsā-vārttika, Bhaṭṭa, states thus: 'The ātman is indeed not momentary like a streak of lightning, but is permanent.'
स आत्मा जडरूपः प्रकाशरूपश्चास्ते ।
That ātman is both insentient and luminous in nature.
अयमस्याभिप्रायः - सुषुप्तेरुत्थित एवं वदन्ति एतावन्तं कालमहं जडो निःसंज्ञोऽस्वाप्सम् इति ।
This is his intention: those waking from deep sleep say thus, 'For all this time I slept inert and unconscious.'
तस्मादात्मा जडरूप इति सिद्ध्यति ।
Therefore it is established that the ātman is inert in nature.
किञ्च सुषुप्तादुत्थितस्य स्मृतिरपि भवति ।
Moreover, there is also recollection for one who has awoken from deep sleep.
अननुभूतेऽर्थे न स्मृतिर्भवेत् ।
Recollection cannot occur with regard to an unexperienced object.
सुषुप्तावात्मस्वरूपातिरिक्तं न किञ्चिदपि ज्ञानसाधनमस्ति ।
In deep sleep, there is no instrument of knowledge whatsoever other than the very nature of the ātman.
सुषुप्त्यनन्तरभाविस्मृतेः कारणं सौषुप्तज्ञानमेव वाच्यम् ।
The knowledge during deep sleep alone must be declared as the cause of the recollection arising subsequent to deep sleep.
तच्च सुषुप्तिकालीनं ज्ञानमात्मस्वरूपमेव ।
And that knowledge during deep sleep is the very nature of the ātman.
इत्थमात्मा खद्योतवत्प्रकाशरूपोऽप्रकाशरूपश्च ।
Thus, like a firefly, the ātman is both of the nature of light and of the nature of darkness.
ज्ञानरूपत्वात् प्रकाशरूपः, जडरूपत्वादप्रकाशरूपश्च ।
Because of being knowledge by nature it is luminous, and because of being inert by nature it is non-luminous.
आनन्दमयकोश एव प्रकाशरूपोऽप्रकाशरूपश्चास्ति ।
The ānandamayakośa alone is both luminous and non-luminous.
सुषुप्तौ चैतन्याभाससहिताज्ञानमेवानन्दमयकोश इत्युच्यते ।
In deep sleep, avidyā accompanied by the reflection of consciousness is alone designated as the ānandamayakośa.
तत्र चिदाभासः प्रकाशरूपोऽज्ञानमप्रकाशरूपं च भवति ।
Therein, the reflection of consciousness is luminous and avidyā is non-luminous.
तस्माद्भट्टमते आनन्दमयकोश एवात्मेति सिद्धम् ।1
Therefore, it is established that in Bhaṭṭa's system, the ānandamayakośa alone is held to be the ātman.
टिप्पणी
1.
विज्ञानवादमतखण्डनं - बुद्धशिष्यं योगाचारं येऽनुसरन्ति ते क्षणिकविज्ञानरूपां बुद्धिमात्मेति वर्णयन्ति ।
Refutation of Vijñānavāda: Those who follow Yogācāra, the disciple of the Buddha, describe the intellect, which is of the nature of momentary consciousness, as the ātman.
तदसङ्गतम् ।
That is untenable:
(१) रूपादीनां ज्ञानरूपं कार्यं प्रति नेत्रादीन्द्रियं साधनम् ।
(1) Sense organs like the eye are instruments with respect to the effect in the form of the cognition of form, etc.
तथा निश्चयरूपकार्यं प्रति साधनभूता बुद्धिर्नात्मा भवितुमर्हति ।
Likewise, the buddhi, which is an instrument with respect to the effect of determinate cognition, cannot be the ātman.
किन्तु सर्वपदार्थनिश्चायिकाया बुद्धेर्यः साक्षी स एवात्मा ।
Rather, that which is the witness of the intellect that determines all objects is alone the ātman.
(२) स आत्मा स्वयं स्वयम्प्रकाशरूपत्वात्सदा भासते ।
(2) That ātman, by virtue of being self-luminous, always shines by itself.
अतो भास्यरूपादेर्भासकः सूर्यादिर्यथा भास्यविलक्षणस्तथा भास्यबुद्धेर्भासक आत्मा बुद्धेर्विलक्षणः सिद्ध्यति ।
Therefore, just as the sun, etc., the illuminator of the illuminated form, is distinct from the illuminated object, so the ātman, the illuminator of the illuminated intellect, is established to be distinct from the intellect.
यथा दीपादेः प्रकाशो घटादिना सम्बद्धो घटादेराकारमापद्य सम्मिश्रतया भासमानोऽपि वस्तुतो घटादेर्विलक्षणस्वभाव एव तथा ज्ञानस्वरूप आत्मा बुद्धिवृत्त्या सम्बद्धस्तदाकारमापद्याविविक्ततया भासमानोऽपि परमार्थतया बुद्धिवृत्तेर्विलक्षणो नित्यशुद्धासङ्गचिन्मात्ररूपः ।
Just as the light of a lamp, having contacted a pot, etc., and assumed its shape, appears as if mingled with it, yet in reality remains entirely distinct in nature from the pot, etc., so the ātman, which is of the nature of knowledge, though associated with the buddhi-vṛtti, assuming its form and appearing undifferentiated from it, is from the absolute standpoint distinct from the buddhi-vṛtti, being of the nature of eternally pure, unattached pure consciousness.
(३) अपञ्चीकृतभूतसमष्टिसत्त्वगुणांशकार्यभूतस्यान्तःकरणस्य निश्चयरूपक्रियया बुद्धिरिति, सङ्कल्पविकल्परूपक्रियया मन इति च व्यपदेशः ।
(3) The inner organ, which is an effect born of the sattva portion of the totality of unquintuplicated subtle elements, is designated as buddhi on account of its function of determinate resolve, and as manas on account of its function of thought and doubt.
तस्माद्बुद्धिरन्तःकरणादव्यतिरिक्ता ।
Therefore, the buddhi is non-different from the antaḥkaraṇa.
ततश्च भौतिकान्तःकरणाव्यतिरिक्तबुद्धेरपि भौतिकत्वाद्देहेन्द्रियमनोवदनात्मत्वमेव सिद्धम् ।
And consequently, since the buddhi, being non-different from the material antaḥkaraṇa, is itself material, its non-selfhood is established, just like the body, senses, and mind.
(४) कठोपनिषत्तृतीयवल्ल्यां आत्मनो रथस्वामित्वेन, बुद्धेः सारथित्वेन च वर्णनं दृश्यते ।
(4) In the third vallī of the Kaṭhopaniṣad, the description is found portraying the ātman as the chariot-master and the buddhi as the charioteer.
यथा सारथिविलक्षणो रथस्वामी तथा बुद्धिविलक्षण आत्मा भवति ।
Just as the chariot-master is distinct from the charioteer, so the ātman is distinct from the intellect.
मम बुद्धिरिदानीं मन्दा, इदानीं तीक्ष्णा इति ममताविषयत्वाद्बुद्धेरहन्ताविषयत्वं न युज्यते ।
(5) Since the intellect is the object of the sense of 'mine' (as in 'My intellect is dull now, sharp now'), it is not fitting for it to be the object of the sense of 'I'.
अतो न बुद्धिरात्मा ।
Therefore the intellect is not the ātman.
(६) आत्मनः क्षणिकत्वं विज्ञानवादिसम्मतमत्यन्तमसङ्गतम् ।
(6) The momentariness of the ātman accepted by the Vijñānavādin is utterly untenable.
तथात्वे उत्तमर्णो गतवत्सरे दत्तं धनमस्मिन् वत्सरेऽधमर्णान्ना... ॥
Were it so, a creditor would not [be able to recover] in this year the money lent to a debtor in the past year...
280
माध्यमिकबौद्धमतं (आनन्दमयकोश आत्मा) शून्यवादिनो बौद्धास्त्वेवमाहुः, आत्मा निरंशः ।
The view of the Mādhyamika Buddhists (the ānandamayakośa as the ātman): However, the Buddhist proponents of the void (śūnyavāda) state thus: The ātman is partless.
तस्मादेकस्यैवात्मनः प्रकाशरूपत्वमप्रकाशरूपत्वं च न घटेत ।
Therefore, both the nature of being luminous and the nature of being non-luminous cannot logically belong to one and the same ātman.
खद्योतस्य सांशत्वादेकोंऽशः प्रकाशरूपोऽपरोंऽशोऽप्रकाशरूपश्च भवति ।
Because a firefly has parts, one part is luminous and the other part is non-luminous.
न त्वात्मनो निरंशस्य विरुद्धोभयरूपवत्त्वकथनं युक्तम् ।
But it is not proper to state that the partless ātman possesses both contradictory natures.
यद्युभयरूपतासिद्धये आत्मनः सांशत्वं अङ्गीक्रियते तर्हि सांशानां घटादीनामुत्पत्तिनाशदर्शनादात्मनोऽपि उत्पत्तिनाशवत्त्वं प्रसज्येत ।
If having parts is accepted for the ātman in order to establish its dual nature, then, since objects with parts such as pots are seen to have origination and destruction, having origination and destruction would also entail for the ātman.
यदुत्पत्तिनाशवद्वस्तु तदुत्पत्तेः प्रागूर्ध्वं च नाशादसद्भवति ।
Whatever entity possesses origination and destruction is unreal prior to its origination and after its destruction.
आद्यन्तयोर्यदसत्तन्मध्येऽप्यसदेव भवति ।
That which is non-existent at the beginning and at the end is indeed non-existent in the middle as well.
आदावन्ते च यन्नास्ति वर्तमानेऽपि तत्तथा (मा. का. वै. ६) इति स्मृतेः ।
This is in accordance with the traditional text: That which does not exist in the beginning and in the end is likewise so even in the present (Mā. Kā. Vai. 6).
तस्मादुत्पत्तिनाशवत्त्वे आत्मा असद्रूपो भवेत् ।
Therefore, if it has origination and destruction, the ātman would be of the nature of non-existence.
तथा आत्मभिन्नः सर्वोऽपि पदार्थः उत्पत्तिनाशवत्त्वादसद्रूप एव ।
Likewise, every entity other than the ātman is also only of the nature of non-existence, because of possessing origination and destruction.
अनया रीत्या आत्मानात्मरूपसकलवस्तूनामसद्रूपत्वात् शून्यमेव परमतत्त्वमिति शून्यवादिनो माध्यमिकबौद्धस्य मतम् ।
In this way, because all entities consisting of the ātman and non-ātman are of the nature of non-existence, the void alone is the supreme reality — such is the doctrine of the Mādhyamika Buddhist who is a proponent of śūnya.
तेऽप्यज्ञानरूपानन्दमयकोशमेव प्रतिपादयन्ति ।
They too propound only the ānandamayakośa, which is of the nature of avidyā.
तथा हि, दृष्टिभेदेनाज्ञानं त्रिभी रूपैः प्रतीयते ।
For, according to the difference in viewpoint, avidyā is perceived in three forms.
(१) अद्वैतशास्त्रसंस्काररहितस्य जगदाकारेण परिणतमज्ञानं सत्यत्वेन प्रतीयते ।
(1) For one devoid of the latent impressions of the Advaita scripture, avidyā transformed into the form of the world is perceived as real.
(२) अद्वैतशास्त्रानुसारियुक्तिकुशलानां पण्डितानामज्ञानं तत्कार्यं जगच्च सदसद्विलक्षणानिर्वचनीयत्वेन भाति ।
(2) For scholars skilled in reasoning in accordance with Advaita scripture, avidyā and its effect, the world, appear as distinct from real and unreal and indeterminable (anirvacanīya).
(३) ज्ञाननिष्ठां प्राप्तस्य जीवन्मुक्तस्य विदुषोऽज्ञानं तत्कार्यं च तुच्छत्वेन प्रतीयते ।
(3) For the wise jīvanmukta who has attained steadfastness in knowledge, avidyā and its effect appear as utterly void (tuccha).
तुच्छम्, असत्, शून्यं इति त्रयः शब्दाः समानार्थाः ।
Tuccha, asat, and śūnya — these three words are synonymous.
तथा चोक्तं पञ्चदश्यां चित्रदीपे दातुमिच्छेत् ।
And so it is stated in the Pañcadaśī, in the Citradīpa chapter: [nor] would one wish to give.
प्रथमक्षणे भुक्तवान् पुरुष उत्तरक्षणे तृप्तोऽहमस्मि इति न ब्रूयात् ।
A person who has eaten in the first moment would not say in the next moment, I am satisfied.
आत्मनः क्षणिकत्वे गतवत्सरे धनं दत्तवत उत्तमर्णस्य, पूर्वक्षणे भुक्तवतः पुरुषस्य चेदानीमभावात् ।
Because if the ātman were momentary, the creditor who lent money in the past year, and the person who ate in the preceding moment, would both be non-existent now.
तस्मादात्मा न क्षणिकः ।
Therefore, the ātman is not momentary.
(७) आत्मनः क्षणिकत्वे मोक्षसाधनकलापो व्यर्थः स्यात् ।1
(7) If the ātman were momentary, the entire collection of means to mokṣa would be futile.
टिप्पणी
1.
आत्मा चिज्जडोभयात्मक इति भट्टपक्षोऽप्यसङ्गतः अयमन्धकारः प्रकाशः अयं पुरुषः स्थाणुः इतिवच्चैकत्र वस्तुनि चिज्जडांशविरोधात् ।
The Bhaṭṭa view that the Self is of a dual nature, both conscious and insentient, is also untenable, because, like saying 'this darkness is light' or 'this person is a pillar', there is an inherent contradiction between conscious and inert aspects in a single entity.
उभयांशत्वमङ्गीकृत्य नोभावप्यंशावनुभवगोचरौ किन्तु जडांश एवानुभवगोचरो न चेतनांशः इति कथनं तु न युक्तम् ।
And to claim, having accepted a dual nature, that 'both aspects are not objects of direct experience, but only the insentient aspect is experienced and not the conscious aspect', is not logical.
यथा दण्डदर्शनमात्रेण अयं दण्डी इति ज्ञानं न जायते; किन्तु दण्डपुरुषोभयदर्शनेनैव जायते तथा जडांशमात्रदर्शनेन न चिज्जडोभयात्मकात्मसिद्धिर्भवेत् ।
Just as the cognition 'this is a staff-bearer' does not arise merely by seeing the staff, but only upon seeing both the staff and the man, likewise merely by perceiving the inert aspect, the Self as composed of both conscious and inert parts cannot be established.
चेतनांशस्याप्यनुभवगोचरत्वाभ्युपगमे जाड्यं तत्र कल्पितमिति वक्तव्यम् ।
If the conscious aspect is also admitted to be an object of experience, then it must be admitted that insentience in the Self is merely illusory (superimposed).
हठादुभयोरंशयोः सत्यत्वाभ्युपगमे आत्मनो जडचेतनांशयोः परस्परं कः सम्बन्धः ।
If by stubborn insistence both parts are accepted as real, then what is the mutual relation between the inert and conscious aspects of the Self?
संयोगो वा विषयविषयिभावो वेति स प्रष्टव्यः ॥
He should be asked: Is it conjunction (saṁyoga) or the subject-object relation (viṣaya-viṣayi-bhāva)?
माया चेयं तमोरूपा तापनीये तदीरणात् । अनुभुतिस्तत्र मानं प्रतिजज्ञे श्रुतिः स्वयम् ॥ १२५॥
'And this māyā is of the nature of darkness, because it is declared as such in the Tāpanīya Upaniṣad; Śruti itself declared direct experience to be the proof thereof.' (Pañcadaśī 6.125)
जडं मोहात्मकं तच्चेत्यनुभावयति श्रुतिः । आबालगोपं स्पष्टत्वादानन्त्यं तस्य साब्रवीत् ॥ १२६॥
'Śruti makes us experience that darkness as inert and delusive; and because it is obvious to all from children to cowherds, Śruti declared its endlessness.' (Pañcadaśī 6.126)
इत्थं लौकिकदृष्ट्यैतत् सर्वैरप्यनुभूयते । युक्तिदृष्ट्या त्वनिर्वाच्यं नासदासीदिति श्रुतेः ॥ १२८॥
'Thus, from the worldly standpoint, it is experienced by all; but from the standpoint of logical inquiry it is inexpressible (anirvacanīya), according to the Śruti passage "there was neither non-existence [nor existence]".' (Pañcadaśī 6.128)
नासदासीद्विभातत्वान्नो सदासीच्च बाधनात् । विद्यादृष्ट्या श्रुतं तुच्छं तस्य नित्यनिवृत्तितः ॥ १२९॥
'It was not non-existent because it appeared, nor was it existent because it is sublated; from the standpoint of knowledge (vidyā), it is declared by Śruti to be non-entity (tuccha) because of its eternal absence.' (Pañcadaśī 6.129)
तुच्छानिर्वचनीया च वास्तवी चेत्यसौ त्रिधा । ज्ञेया माया त्रिभिर्बोधैः श्रौतयौक्तिकलौकिकैः ॥ १३०॥ इति ।
'Māyā is to be understood in three ways: as non-existent, indefinable, and real, through three types of perspectives—the scriptural, the logical, and the worldly.' (Pañcadaśī 6.130)
इत्थं जीवन्मुक्तानां तुच्छत्वेन प्रतीयमानेऽज्ञाने मोहमापन्नाः शून्यवादिनो न परमपुरुषार्थं लभन्ते ।
Falling into delusion regarding ignorance, which appears utterly void to the jīvanmuktas, the Śūnyavādins (nihilists) do not attain the supreme goal of human life.
किन्तु तुच्छरूप आनन्दमयकोश एवात्मेति वदन्ति ।
Rather, they assert that the ānandamayakośa, which is void in nature, is alone the Self.
आद्ये पक्षे अनित्ययोः सावयवयोर्द्वयोर्वस्तुनोरेव संयोग इति नियमादात्मनोऽनित्यत्वं प्रसज्येत ।
On the first alternative (conjunction), by the rule that 'conjunction occurs only between two non-eternal, partite things', the non-eternality of the Self would undesirably result.
द्वितीयपक्षे चिज्जडांशयोरुभयोरप्येकस्यैवात्मनः स्वरूपत्वाच्चिदंशो जडो भवेत् ।
In the second alternative, since both conscious and inert parts are the nature of the single Self, the conscious part would become inert.
जडांशश्च चिद्भवेत् ।
And the inert part would become conscious.
तृतीयपक्षे घटतज्ज्ञानवदुभयोरंशयोरनात्मत्वं भवेत् ।
In the third alternative (subject-object relation), both parts would be non-Self, like a pot and its cognition.
विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्म (बृ. ३.१.२७) प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म (ऐ. ३.१) सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म (तै. ब्र. १) इत्यादिश्रुतिप्रसिद्धज्ञानमात्रस्वरूपस्यात्मनोऽर्धांशस्य जडत्वाभ्युपगमे प्रमाणं नोपलभ्यते ।
There is no valid means of knowledge found to support accepting insentience for half of the Self, whose nature as pure consciousness alone is well known from Śruti texts such as 'Brahman is consciousness, bliss' (बृ. ३.१.२७), 'Consciousness is Brahman' (ऐ. ३.१), and 'Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite' (तै. ब्र. १).
सुप्तोत्थितस्य जडो निःसंज्ञोऽहमस्वाप्सम् इत्यात्मनो जडत्वसम्पादिका या स्मृतिरुक्ता सा सौषुप्ताज्ञानमेव विषयीकरोति ।
The recollection of one who has awakened from sleep, 'I slept inert and unconscious', which was cited as proving the insentience of the Self, actually takes as its object only the ignorance present during deep sleep.
तस्मादात्मनो जडचेतनोभयांशकत्वमसङ्गतमेव ।
Therefore, it is entirely untenable for the Self to possess both inert and conscious aspects.
सर्वं शून्यम्; शून्यमेव परमतत्त्वम्, सुषुप्तिकालीनाज्ञानरूपानन्दमयकोश एवात्मा इतीदं माध्यमिकमतमप्यसङ्गतमेव ।
The Mādhyamika view that 'everything is void; the void alone is the supreme reality, and the ānandamayakośa in the form of deep-sleep ignorance is alone the Self' is also utterly untenable.
तथा हि, किं शून्यं साक्षिसहितमुत साक्षिरहितमुत स्वप्रकाशमिति त्रिधा तत्र विकल्पो भवति ।
To explain: there arises a threefold dilemma here—is the void accompanied by a witness, or devoid of a witness, or self-luminous?
आद्यपक्षे यः शून्यस्य साक्षी स शून्याद्विलक्षण आत्मा सिद्ध्यते ।
In the first alternative, that witness of the void is established as the Ātman, distinct from the void.
द्वितीयपक्षे साक्षिरहितत्वाच्छून्यमेव न सिद्ध्यति ।
In the second alternative, due to the absence of any witness, the void itself is not established.
तृतीयपक्षे स्वप्रकाशत्वादस्मदभिमतं ब्रह्मैव शून्यमिति नामान्तरेणोक्तं भवति ।
In the third alternative, because of being self-luminous, the Brahman accepted by us is merely spoken of under another name as 'the void'.
तथा च शून्यासिद्धिरेव ।
And thus, the void is definitely unestablished.
असद्वा इदमग्र आसीत् (तै. ब्र. ७) असदेवेदमग्र आसीत् (छा. ६.२.१) इत्यादिवाक्यानि पूर्वापरविरोधात् न शून्यं प्रतिपादयन्ति ।
Passages such as 'Non-existent indeed was this in the beginning' (Tai. Brā. 7) and 'Non-existent alone was this in the beginning' (Chā. 6.2.1) do not teach an absolute void, because of contradiction with the preceding and succeeding contexts.
किन्तु नैयायिकवैशेषिकबौद्धादयः प्रागभावादीन् जगतः कारणत्वेन वर्णयन्ति, तदनूद्य तादृशविपरीतग्रहनिवर्तने एव तादृशश्रुतीनां तात्पर्यम् ।
Rather, the Naiyāyikas, Vaiśeṣikas, Buddhists, and others describe prior non-existence etc. as the cause of the universe; having restated that view, the purport of such śrutis lies solely in dispelling such erroneous conceptions.
असत् = अनभिव्यक्तनामरूपात्मकम्, इदं = जगत्, अग्रे = प्राक् सृष्टेरासीत् इति श्रुत्यर्थः ।
इत्थं शून्यवादोऽसङ्गत एव ।
Thus, the doctrine of Śūnyavāda is entirely untenable.
बौद्धशिष्याश्चत्वारः ।
The Buddhist disciples are of four schools:
(१) माध्यामिकः शून्यवादी, (२) योगाचारः क्षणिकविज्ञानवादी, (३) सौत्रान्तिकोऽनुमेयबाह्यपदार्थवादी, (४) वैभाषिकः प्रत्यक्षबाह्यार्थवादी ।
281 · प्राभाकरनैयायिकयोर्मतं (आनन्दमयकोश आत्मा)
पूर्वमीमांसकैकदेशिनः प्राभाकरा नैयायिकाश्चैवं कथयन्ति - नात्मा शून्यरूपः ।
The Prābhākaras (a school of Pūrva-Mīmāṁsā) and the Naiyāyikas say thus: 'The ātman is not of the nature of a void.'
आत्मा शून्यरूपः इति वदन्नेवं प्रष्टव्यः - शून्यरूपं तेनानुभूयते न वेति ।
One who says 'the ātman is of the nature of a void' should be questioned thus: 'Is the void experienced by him or not?'
यदि शून्यरूपमनुभूयते तदा येन तच्छून्यरूपमनुभूयते स एवात्मा ।
If the void is experienced, then the one by whom that void is experienced is himself the ātman.
स च शून्यविलक्षण इति च सिद्ध्यति ।
And it is established that he is distinct from the void.
यदि शून्यरूपं नानुभूयते तदा शून्यमेव नास्तीति सिद्ध्यति ।
If the void is not experienced, then it follows that the void itself does not exist.
अनया रीत्या शून्यविलक्षण आत्मा सिद्धः ।
In this manner, the ātman is established as distinct from the void.
तस्यात्मनो मनसा संयोगेन ज्ञानमुत्पद्यते ।
By the contact of that ātman with the mind, knowledge is produced.
तेन ज्ञानरूपेण गुणेनात्मा चेतनो भवति ।
Due to that quality of knowledge, the ātman becomes conscious.
स्वरूपतस्त्वात्मा जडः ।
However, in its intrinsic nature, the ātman is insentient.
सुखदुःखेच्छाद्वेषप्रयत्नधर्माधर्मा अप्यात्मनो गुणा इति ।
Pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, merit, and demerit are also qualities of the ātman.
तन्मतेऽप्यानन्दमयकोश एवात्मा ।
In their doctrine too, the ānandamayakośa alone is the ātman.
विज्ञानमयकोशस्था या बुद्धिः सात्मनो ज्ञानरूपो गुण इत्युच्यते ।
The intellect residing in the vijñānamayakośa is called the quality of knowledge belonging to the ātman.
तथा हि, आनन्दमयकोशे चैतन्यं गूढमास्ते ।
For, consciousness remains hidden within the ānandamayakośa.
विवेकहीनानां न तत्प्रतीयते ।
To those lacking discrimination, it is not perceived.
तस्मात्प्राभाकरा नैयायिकाश्च सुषुप्तमात्मानं ज्ञानहीनं मन्वानाः स्वरूपत एवात्मानं जडमाहुः ।
Therefore, the Prābhākaras and Naiyāyikas, regarding the ātman in deep sleep as devoid of knowledge, declare the ātman to be inherently insentient.
तस्माद्गूढचैतन्ये आनन्दमयकोशे एव तयोरात्मत्वभ्रान्तिरस्ति ।
Therefore, both of them hold the delusion of selfhood only regarding the ānandamayakośa, in which consciousness is concealed.
अपि च तन्मते आत्मस्वरूपं नित्यज्ञानं न जीवेऽभिमतम्, किन्त्वनित्यज्ञानमेव जीवेऽभिमतम् ।
Moreover, in their doctrine, eternal knowledge as the nature of the self is not accepted in the jīva; rather, only transient knowledge is accepted in the jīva.
तच्चानित्यं ज्ञानं सिद्धान्तेऽन्तःकरणवृत्त्यात्मकबुद्धिरूपं भवति ।
And that transient knowledge, in our siddhānta, is of the form of intellect constituted by the vṛtti of the inner organ.
इत्थं प्राभाकरनैयायिकयोर्मते आनन्दमयकोश आत्मा ।
Thus, in the doctrine of the Prābhākaras and Naiyāyikas, the ānandamayakośa is the ātman.
बुद्धिस्तस्यात्मनो गुणः ।
And intellect is a quality of that ātman.
इदमपि मतं न समीचीनम् ।
This view also is not sound.
ज्ञानभिन्नं यद्यज्जडवस्तु घटादिकं तत्सर्वमनित्यमस्ति ।
Whatever insentient object is distinct from knowledge, such as a pot etc., all that is non-eternal.
यद्यात्मा ज्ञानस्वरूपो न भवेत्तदा घटादिवज्जडोऽनित्यश्च भवेत् ।
If the ātman were not of the nature of knowledge, then, like a pot, it would be insentient and non-eternal.
आत्मनोऽनित्यत्वे मोक्षान्वयिनोऽभावात् मोक्षसाधनानां निष्प्रयोजनता स्यात् ।
If the ātman were non-eternal, there being no one to attain liberation, the means to liberation would become entirely futile.
इत्थं वेदान्तवाक्येष्वश्रद्दधाना बहिर्मुखाः पुरुषा गुरुसम्प्रदायशून्याः पञ्चकोशेष्वन्यतममेव स्वस्वबुद्ध्यनुसारेणात्मत्वेन मन्वाना मुख्यमात्मानं साक्षिणं न जानन्ति ।
Thus, externally-minded people who lack faith in Vedānta statements and are devoid of the lineage of a guru, regarding one or another of the five sheaths as the ātman according to their own intellect, do not know the primary ātman, the witness.
तस्मादन्नमयादय आत्मन आच्छादकत्वात् कोशा इति वर्ण्यन्ते ।1
Therefore, the annamayakośa and the others are described as 'sheaths' (kośas) because they conceal the ātman.
टिप्पणी
1.
प्राभाकरनैयायिकयोर्मतखण्डनं - सुषुप्तौ ज्ञानाभावादात्मा जडः इत्येतन्न युज्यते ।
Refutation of the doctrine of the Prābhākaras and Naiyāyikas: The assertion that 'the ātman is insentient because of the absence of knowledge in deep sleep' is incorrect.
सुखमहमस्वाप्सं न किञ्चिदवेदिषम् इति परामर्शबलात् सुषुप्तौ सुखाज्ञानयोरनुभवस्योपपादितत्वात् तेषां वचनं बाधितं भवति ।
Because the experience of bliss and ignorance in deep sleep is established on the strength of the subsequent recollection, 'I slept happily, I did not know anything,' their statement is sublated.
आत्मा यदि स्वरूपतो जडः स्यात् तदा सुषुप्तावनुभूतस्यानन्दस्य स्मरणं न स्यात् ।
If the ātman were intrinsically insentient, then there would be no recollection of the bliss experienced in deep sleep.
स्मर्यते तु ।
However, it is indeed remembered.
तस्मादात्मा न जडः ।
Therefore, the ātman is not insentient.
282 · ईश्वरीयपञ्चकोशैस्तत्स्वरूपाच्छादनम्
यथा जीवस्य पञ्चकोशा जीवस्य यथार्थस्वरूपं साक्षिणमावृण्वन्ति तथेश्वरस्य समष्टिपञ्चकोशा ईश्वरस्य यथार्थस्वरूपमावृण्वन्ति ।
Just as the five sheaths of the jīva veil the real nature of the jīva, namely the witness (sākṣin), so too the cosmic five sheaths of Īśvara veil the true nature of Īśvara.
तथा हि, ईश्वरस्य यथार्थं स्वरूपं तत्पदलक्ष्यं यद्रूपं तदेव ।
To explain: the true nature of Īśvara is indeed that very nature which is the implied meaning (lakṣyārtha) of the term 'Tat' (That).
तमेतं श्रौतमर्थं विहाय केचन मायारूपानन्दमयकोशविशिष्टमन्तर्यामिणं तत्पदवाच्यमेव परमतत्त्वमिति वदन्ति ।
Setting aside this Vedic truth, some claim that the Inner Controller (Antaryāmin), qualified by the sheath of bliss (ānandamayakośa) made of māyā, which is merely the expressed/literal meaning of the term 'Tat', is the supreme reality.
तथैवान्ये हिरण्यगर्भवैश्वानरविष्णुब्रह्मशिवगणेशदेवीसूर्यादिषु खड्गकुद्दालाश्वत्थार्कवेण्वन्तेषु पदार्थेषु परमात्मत्वभ्रान्तिमापन्नाः ।
Similarly, others fall into the delusion of attributing supreme Selfhood to various entities ranging from Hiraṇyagarbha, Vaiśvānara, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Śiva, Gaṇeśa, Devī, and Sūrya down to swords, spades, the sacred peepal tree, the sun-plant (arka), and bamboo.
यद्यपि सकलपदार्थेषु लक्ष्यभागः परमात्मनो न भिन्नः तथापि तत्तदुपाधिविशिष्टानेव परमात्मत्वेन मन्यन्ते ।
Although the implied essence in all objects is not different from the supreme Self, they nevertheless regard only the entities as qualified by their respective adjuncts (upādhis) as the supreme Self.
तदेतन्मतं तेषां भ्रान्तिरेव ।
This view of theirs is merely a delusion.
पञ्चकोशावृताज्जीवेश्वरयोः परमार्थस्वरूपाद्बहिर्मुखा देहादिष्वात्मत्वभ्रान्तिमापद्य पुण्यपापान्याचरन्ति ।
Turned away from the ultimate real nature of jīva and Īśvara covered by the five sheaths, they mistake the body and other non-Self objects for the Self and perform virtuous and sinful actions.
अन्तर्याम्यादिवंशपर्यन्तानां पदार्थानामीश्वरबुद्ध्या आराधनं कृत्वा सुखं प्राप्तुमिच्छन्ति ।
They desire to attain happiness by worshipping various objects ranging from the Inner Controller down to bamboo, viewing them as Īśvara.
यादृशमुपाधिमाराधयन्ति तदनुसारेण फलं च सिद्ध्यति ।
And whatever kind of adjunct they worship, the result is accomplished in accordance with that.
यस्मात्कारणसूक्ष्मस्थूलरूपः सर्वोऽपि प्रपञ्च ईश्वरशरीरेऽन्तर्भूतस्तस्मात् तत्तदुपासनानुसारि फलं भवति ।
Because the entire phenomenal world consisting of causal, subtle, and gross forms is included within the body of Īśvara, therefore the fruit corresponds to each specific form of worship.
तथा चोक्तं पञ्चदश्यां चित्रदीपे — एवमन्ये स्वस्वपक्षाभिमानेनान्यथान्यथा । मन्त्रार्थवादकल्पादीनाश्रित्य प्रतिपेदिरे ॥ १२०॥ अन्तर्यामिणमारभ्य स्थावरान्तेशवादिनः । सन्त्यश्वत्थार्कवंशादेः कुलदेवत्वदर्शनात् ॥ १२१॥ इत्यादिना ।
And so it is stated in the Pañcadaśī, in the Citradīpa chapter: In this manner, others, out of pride in their respective doctrines, have held diverse views relying on mantras, explanatory passages (*arthavāda*), ritual manuals (*kalpa*), and the like (120). There are theorists who assert Īśvara from the Inner Controller down to inanimate objects, since plants such as the holy peepal tree, the sun-plant, and bamboo are seen worshipped as family deities (121). and so on.
परन्तु मोक्षो 1न ब्रह्मज्ञानं विना सिद्ध्यति ।
However, liberation is never attained without the direct knowledge of Brahman.
यो मोक्ष
Whoever [desires] liberation...
टिप्पणी
1.
यथा जीवस्य पञ्चकोशा जीवस्य निजस्वरूपं प्रत्यगात्मानं जीवदृष्टिं प्रत्याच्छादयन्ति, न तथेश्वरस्य पञ्चकोशा ईश्वरस्य निजं स्वरूपं ईश्वरदृष्टिं प्रत्याच्छादयन्ति ।
Just as the five sheaths of the jīva conceal the inner Self, the true nature of the jīva, from the jīva's sight, the five sheaths of Īśvara do not in the same way conceal Īśvara's own true nature from Īśvara's sight.
ईश्वरस्यावरणरहितत्वेन नित्यमुक्तत्वात् न तस्य किञ्चिदपि कर्तव्यमस्ति ।
Because Īśvara is free from veiling (*āvaraṇa*) and is ever-liberated, He has nothing whatsoever to accomplish.
तस्मात् यथा व्यष्टिपञ्चकोशेभ्यः प्रत्यगात्मनो विवेचनं जीवेन कर्तव्यं तथा समष्टिपञ्चकोशेभ्यो ब्रह्मणो विवेचनमपि जीवेनैव कर्तव्यम् ।
Therefore, just as the discrimination of the inner Self from the individual five sheaths must be performed by the jīva, so too the discrimination of Brahman from the cosmic five sheaths must be done by the jīva alone.
सद्रूपः, चिद्रूपः, आनन्दरूपः, अद्वय इत्यात्मनश्चत्वारि विशेषणानि ।
'Of the nature of Existence, Consciousness, Bliss, and Non-dual' are the four primary qualifications of the Self.
देहादेस्तु अनृतः, जडः, दुःखरूपः, सद्वय इति चत्वारि विशेषणानि ।
On the other hand, 'unreal, insentient, of the nature of misery, and dual' are the four characteristics of the body and other adjuncts.
तत्रात्मनः सद्रूपचिद्रूपाभ्यां देहादेरनृतजडरूपयोस्तिरोधानं भवति ।
There, by the Existence and Consciousness natures of the Self, the unreality and insentience of the body and other objects are obscured.
तस्माद्देहादिः सत्त्वेन चेतनत्वेन च भाति ।
Consequently, the body and other adjuncts appear as existing and conscious.
देहादेः दुःखरूपेण सद्वयत्वेन चात्मन आनन्दरूपत्वाद्वयत्वयोरभिभवो भवति ।
And by the misery-nature and duality of the body etc., the bliss-nature and non-duality of the Self are eclipsed.
अतश्चात्मा दुःखित्वेन सद्वितीयत्वेन च भाति ।
Hence, the Self appears as subject to misery and as possessing a second (limited).
इत्थमात्मनः पञ्चकोशानां चान्योन्याध्यासोऽस्ति ।
In this way, there is mutual superimposition (*anyonyādhyāsa*) between the Self and the five sheaths.
तस्मान्मुमुक्षुरवश्यं पञ्चकोशविवेचनं कुर्यात् ।
Therefore, a spiritual seeker must necessarily carry out the discrimination of the five sheaths.
मिच्छति स विवेकेन जीवेश्वरयोः स्वरूपं पञ्चकोशेभ्यः पृथक्कृत्य जानीयात् ।
[Whoever] desires [liberation], he should know the true nature of jīva and Īśvara by separating it from the five sheaths through discrimination.
तत्र दृष्टान्तः ।
Here is an illustration for this.
यथा मिलितयोः मुञ्जेषीकयोः पृथक्करणं क्रियते, तथा विवेकेन जीवेश्वरयोः स्वरूपं पञ्चकोशेभ्यः पृथक्कृत्य जानीयात् ।
Just as the inner stalk is separated from the surrounding Muñja grass blade, so one should know the essential nature of both jīva and Īśvara by separating it from the five sheaths through discrimination.
283 · पञ्चकोशविवेकप्रकारः
स्वप्नावस्थायां स्थूलदेहो न भाति ।
In the dream state, the gross body does not appear.
परन्त्वात्मा भासते ।
However, the ātman shines.
तथा सुषुप्तौ सूक्ष्मशरीरस्य ज्ञानं न भवति ।
Likewise, in deep sleep there is no cognition of the subtle body.
सुखस्वरूप आत्मा स्वयम्प्रकाशस्वरूपेण प्रतीयते ।
The ātman, whose nature is bliss, is experienced in its self-luminous form.
सुषुप्तौ सुखज्ञानाभावे सुखमहमस्वाप्सम् इति स्मृतिः सुप्तोत्थितस्य न स्यात् ।
If there were no experience of bliss in deep sleep, one awakened from sleep would not have the recollection, 'I slept blissfully'.
तथा स्मृतेर्जायमानत्वादेव सुषुप्तौ सुखानुभवोऽभ्युपेयः ।
Precisely because such a recollection does arise, the experience of bliss in deep sleep must be accepted.
तच्च सुखं सुषुप्तौ न विषयजन्यम् ।
And that bliss in deep sleep is not born of sense-objects.
तदा सर्वकार्यप्रपञ्चप्रविलयात् ।
Because at that time there is complete dissolution of the entire universe of effects.
किन्तु तदात्मस्वरूपसुखमेव ।
Rather, it is the bliss that is the very nature of the ātman itself.
स चात्मा स्वयम्प्रकाशस्वरूपः ।
And that ātman is self-luminous by nature.
तस्मात्सुखस्वरूप आत्मा स्वयम्प्रकाशरूपेण सुषुप्तौ भासते ।
Therefore, the ātman, whose nature is bliss, shines in deep sleep in its self-luminous form.
निदिध्यासनफलभूतनिर्विकल्पकसमाधौ त्वात्मा अज्ञानकृतावरणरहितः प्रकाशते ।
In nirvikalpa-samādhi, however, which is the fruit of nididhyāsana, the ātman shines devoid of the veil created by ignorance (avidyā).
कारणशरीररूपाज्ञानमपि तदा न भासते ।
Even ignorance in the form of the causal body does not appear then.
इत्थं देहत्रयं व्यभिचरति एकामवस्थां विहायावस्थान्तरे अभानात् ।
In this way, the triad of bodies varies (is non-persistent), because each fails to appear in a state other than its own.
तस्माद्1,2,3देहत्रयमव्यापकम् ।
Therefore, the triad of bodies is non-pervasive (finite and mutable).
टिप्पणी
1.
मुञ्जा नाम कोशविशिष्टदीर्घतृणविशेषः ।
'Muñjā' means a specific variety of long grass equipped with an outer sheath.
ईषीका नाम तत्तृणमध्यस्थकाण्डविशेषः ।
'Īṣīkā' means the specific core stalk situated inside that grass.
2.
प्रातीतिकत्वं वेदान्तसिद्धान्ते जगतः स्फुटम् । सुषुप्तौ तु जगल्लीनं प्रबोधे जायते पुनः ॥ दृष्टिसृष्टिमिमां ब्रह्मानुभवी बहुमन्यते । इति ।
'In the established doctrine of Vedānta, the merely apparent existence (prātītikatva) of the world is obvious: in deep sleep the world is dissolved, and upon waking it arises anew. One who has realized Brahman holds this view of perception-creation (dṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-vāda) in high esteem.'
3.
यथा घटस्य उत्पत्तिविनाशयोः प्राक् ऊर्ध्वं च विद्यमानत्वात् एकत्वात् च आकाशः घटात् विभिन्नः अव्यभिचारी च, तथा स्थूलदेहस्य जननमरणयोः प्राक् ऊर्ध्वं च विद्यमानत्वात् एकत्वात् च आत्मा स्थूलदेहात् भिन्नः अव्यभिचारी च ।
Just as space is distinct from a pot and non-deviating because it exists prior to and after the pot's origin and destruction, and because space is one; so too the *ātman* is distinct from the gross body and non-deviating because it exists prior to and after the body's birth and death, and because the *ātman* is one.
घटः इव स्थूलदेहः जननमरणयोः प्राक् ऊर्ध्वं च अवर्तमानत्वात् अनेकत्वात् च आत्मनः भिन्नः व्यभिचारी च ।
Like a pot, the gross body is distinct from the *ātman* and variable, because it does not exist before birth or after death, and because bodies are manifold.
यत् अधिकदेशकालवर्ति तत् अव्यभिचारी इति उच्यते ।
That which exists across greater space and time is called 'invariable' (*avyabhicārin*).
सर्वशरीरवर्ती आत्मा एकः एव ।
The *ātman* residing in all bodies is one alone.
तस्मात् आकाशवत् आत्मा व्यापकः ।
Therefore, like space, the *ātman* is all-pervasive.
अतः सर्वदेशवर्ती भवति आत्मा ।
Hence, the *ātman* exists in all places.
देहानाम् उत्पत्तिमरणयोः प्राक् ऊर्ध्वं च आत्मा अस्ति ।
The *ātman* exists prior to and after the birth and death of bodies.
तस्मात् आत्मा कालत्रयाबाध्यः सर्वकालवर्ती च भवति ।
Therefore, the *ātman* is unsublated throughout the three periods of time and exists at all times.
एवं सर्वदेशकालवर्तित्वात् आत्मा अव्यभिचारी ।
Thus, because it exists across all space and time, the *ātman* is invariable (*avyabhicārin*).
यत् हि वस्तु स्वल्पदेशे स्वल्पकाले च वर्तते तत् व्यभिचारि ।
Indeed, whatever entity exists in limited space and limited time is variable (*vyabhicārin*).
घटः इव देहः अपि परिच्छिन्नः स्वल्पदेशे वर्तते ।
Like a pot, the body too is finite and exists in limited space.
उत्पत्तिनाशवान् च देहः सर्वकालवर्ती न भवति, किन्तु स्वल्पकाले एव वर्तते ।
And the body, having origin and destruction, does not exist at all times, but exists only for a limited duration.
अतः स्वल्पदेशकालवर्तित्वात् स्थूलदेहः व्यभिचारी ।
Hence, because it exists in limited space and time, the gross body is variable (*vyabhicārin*).
एवं देहात्मनोः व्यभिचारित्वाव्यभिचारित्वरूपविलक्षणधर्मवत्त्वात् एव तयोः परस्परं भेदः सिद्ध्यति ।
Thus, precisely because of possessing distinct attributes in the form of variability and invariability, the mutual difference between the body and the *ātman* is established.
तस्मात् न अहं स्थूलदेहः ।
Therefore, I am not the gross body.
न अपि मदीयः असौ देहः ।
Nor is this body mine.
किन्तु देहः पञ्चभूतकार्यत्वात् भौतिकः ।
Rather, the body is material (*bhautika*), being the product of the five elements.
मम स्थूलदेहव्यतिरिक्तत्वात् एव च तदाश्रितनामरूपजात्याश्रमकर्मादयः धर्माः न मां स्पृशन्ति ।
And precisely because I am distinct from the gross body, the attributes based on it—such as name, form, caste, stage of life, and action—do not touch me.
न अपि ते धर्माः मत्सम्बन्धिनः ।
Nor do those attributes belong to me.
इति स्थूलशरीरविवेकः ।
Thus ends the discernment of the gross body.
नित्यं च ।
And it is eternal.
आत्मा तु सर्वावस्थासु अनुगततया भाति ।
The *ātman*, however, shines as continuous throughout all states.
तस्मात् व्यापकः नित्यः च ।
Therefore, it is all-pervasive and eternal.
इत्थं देहत्रयविलक्षणतया विविच्य आत्मानं जानीयात् ।
In this manner, having discriminated the *ātman* as distinct from the three bodies, one should know it.
तत्र स्थूलशरीरं अन्नमयकोशः, कारणशरीरं आनन्दमयकोशः ।
Among them, the gross body is the *annamayakośa*, and the causal body is the *ānandamayakośa*.
सूक्ष्मशरीरे प्राणमयमनोमयविज्ञानमयाख्याः त्रयः कोशाः अन्तर्भूताः ।
In the subtle body, the three sheaths called *prāṇamaya*, *manomaya*, and *vijñānamaya* are included.
तस्मात् शरीरत्रयविवेकेन पञ्चकोशविवेकः जायते ।
Therefore, through discernment of the three bodies, the discernment of the five sheaths is accomplished.
यथा पञ्चकोशविलक्षणं जीवस्वरूपं तथैव ईश्वरस्वरूपम् अपि ।
Just as the true nature of the *jīva* is distinct from the five sheaths, so too is the true nature of *Īśvara*.
सुषुप्तिः मूर्च्छा मरणं प्रलयः ज्ञानम् इति पञ्चसु अवस्थासु लिङ्गदेहः स्वकारणे अज्ञाने लीयते ।
In the five states—deep sleep, fainting, death, cosmic dissolution, and knowledge—the subtle body (*liṅgadeha*) dissolves into its cause, *avidyā*.
तस्मात् सूक्ष्मदेहः व्यभिचारी असन् च ।
Therefore, the subtle body is variable and unreal.
आत्मा तु सर्वकालेषु अपि प्रकाशमानत्वात् अव्यभिचारी ।
The *ātman*, however, is invariable because it shines at all times.
अतः सद्रूपः च ।
Hence, it is of the nature of true existence (*sat*).
सद्रूपत्वात् आत्मा न लिङ्गदेहः ।
Due to being of the nature of existence, the *ātman* is not the subtle body.
लिङ्गदेहः अपि न आत्मसम्बन्धी ।
Nor does the subtle body belong to the *ātman*.
सः तु अपञ्चीकृतपञ्चमहाभूतकार्यम् ।
It is indeed the product of the five unquintuplicated subtle elements.
तस्मात् न अहम् लिङ्गदेहः ।
Therefore, I am not the subtle body.
कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वसुखदुःखादिलिङ्गदेहधर्माः अपि न अहम् ।
Nor am I the attributes of the subtle body, such as agency, experiencership, pleasure, and pain.
न अपि ते धर्माः मदीयाः ।
Nor are those attributes mine.
तेषां साक्षी अहम् तेभ्यः भिन्नः ।
I am their witness (*sākṣin*), distinct from them.
इति सूक्ष्मदेहविवेचनम् ।
Thus ends the discernment of the subtle body.
अज्ञानम् एव कारणदेहः ।
Ignorance (*avidyā*) alone is the causal body.
न अहम् कारणदेहः ।
I am not the causal body.
सः अपि न मदीयः ।
Nor is it mine.
कारणशरीरधर्मौ आवरणविक्षेपौ अपि न अहम् ।
Nor am I the two attributes of the causal body, veiling (*āvaraṇa*) and projection (*vikṣepa*).
न तौ धर्मौ मदीयौ ।
Nor are those two attributes mine.
तयोः साक्षी अहम् ताभ्यां भिन्नः ।
I am their witness (*sākṣin*), distinct from both.
इति कारणशरीरविवेचनम् ।
Thus ends the discernment of the causal body.
अवस्था नाम दशा भोगकालविशेषरूपा ।
A 'state' (*avasthā*) is indeed a condition in the form of a specific duration of experience.
स्वप्नसुषुप्त्यवस्थाविलक्षणत्वे सति इन्द्रियजन्यज्ञानतत्संस्काराधारभूतः कालविशेषः जाग्रदवस्था ।
The waking state (*jāgradavasthā*) is that specific period which, while distinct from dream and deep sleep, serves as the locus for sense-generated cognition and its latent impressions.
तस्याम् अवस्थायां चतुर्दशत्रिपुटीभिः जीवः व्यवहरति ।
In that state, the *jīva* transacts through the fourteen triads (*tripuṭī*s).
अस्याम् अवस्थायां षड् विशेषाः - (१) अवस्थातः जीवस्य स्थानं चक्षुः ।
In this state there are six particulars: (1) From the standpoint of this state, the seat of the *jīva* is the eye.
सकलशरीरवर्तिनः अपि जीवस्य चक्षुषः मुख्यस्थानत्वात् तत् एव स्थानम् इति उक्तम् ।
Even though the *jīva* pervades the entire body, because the eye is its primary abode, that alone is said to be its seat.
(२) शक्तिः क्रिया ।
(2) The power is action (*kriyā*).
(३) वाणी वैखरी ।
(3) The speech is *vaikharī* (audible speech).
(४) भोगः स्थूलः ।
(4) The experience is gross.
(५) गुणः सत्त्वम् ।
(5) The *guṇa* is *sattva*.
(६) संज्ञा विश्वः ।
(6) The designation is *viśva*.
इयं जाग्रदवस्था स्वप्नसुषुप्त्यवस्थयोः व्यभिचरति इति असन्मयी ।
Since this waking state ceases to exist in the dream and deep sleep states, it is unreal (*asanmayī*).
तत्साक्षिभूतः तु आत्मा सर्वासु अपि अवस्थासु अनुवर्तमानत्वात् सत्यस्वरूपः ।
The *ātman*, however, being its witness, is of the nature of Truth (*satya*) because it persists in all states.
तस्मात् जाग्रदवस्थातः अयम् विलक्षणः जीवः ।
Therefore, this *jīva* is distinct from the waking state.
इति जाग्रदवस्थाविवेकः ।
Thus ends the discernment of the waking state.
यस्याम् अवस्थायाम् इन्द्रियाणाम् उपरमात् तत्साहाय्यम् अन्तरेण एव मनः हिताख्यनाड्यन्तः जाग्रत्संस्कारवशात् विषयाकारेण परिणतं सत् स्वयंज्योतिःस्वरूपेण साक्षिणा अनुभूयते सा अवस्था स्वप्नावस्था ।
That state in which, upon the cessation of the senses and without their aid, the mind inside the *Hitā* channel—having transformed into the shape of objects due to waking impressions—is experienced by the self-luminous witness, is the dream state (*svapnāvasthā*).
अत्र जीवस्य (१) स्थानं कण्ठः ।
Here, regarding the *jīva*: (1) The seat is the throat.
(२) शक्तिः ज्ञानम् ।
(2) The power is knowledge (*jñāna*).
(३) वाणी मध्यमा ।
(3) The speech is *madhyamā*.
(४) भोगः सूक्ष्मः ।
(4) The experience is subtle.
(५) गुणः रजः ।
(5) The *guṇa* is *rajas*.
(६) संज्ञा तैजसः ।
(6) The designation is *taijasa*.
इति स्वप्नावस्थासामग्र्यः ।
Such are the constituents of the dream state.
जाग्रत्सुषुप्त्यवस्थयोः इयं स्वप्नावस्था न भवति ।
This dream state does not exist in the waking or deep sleep states.
आत्मा तु अवस्थात्रयसाक्षित्वात् स्वप्नावस्थातः अपि विलक्षणः ।
The *ātman*, however, being the witness of the three states, is distinct also from the dream state.
इति स्वप्नावस्थाविवेकः ।
Thus ends the discernment of the dream state.
यस्यां केवलं सुखम् अज्ञानं च अनुभूयते सा सुषुप्तिः ।
That state in which sheer bliss and ignorance alone are experienced is deep sleep (*suṣupti*).
अस्याः सामग्र्यः - (१) स्थानं हृदयम् ।
Its constituents are: (1) The seat is the heart.
(२) शक्तिः द्रव्यस्वरूपिणी ।
(2) The power is substantial / unmanifest in form (*dravyasvarūpiṇī*).
ज्ञानक्रियात्मव्यवहाराभावात् केवलज्ञानस्वरूपेण एव द्रव्येण सत्त्वात् द्रव्यशक्तिः इति उच्यते ।
Because there is no active transaction consisting of knowledge and action, and because it exists solely as a substance in the form of pure knowledge, it is termed 'substantial power' (*dravyaśakti*).
(३) वाणी पश्यन्ती ।
(3) The speech is *paśyantī*.
(४) भोगः आनन्दः ।
(4) The experience is bliss (*ānanda*).
(५) गुणः तमः ।
(5) The *guṇa* is *tamas*.
(६) संज्ञा प्राज्ञः ।
(6) The designation is *prājña*.
न जाग्रत्स्वप्नावस्थयोः सुषुप्त्यवस्था अस्ति ।
The deep sleep state does not exist in the waking or dream states.
आत्मा तु अवस्थात्रयसाक्षित्वात् सुषुप्त्यवस्थातः विलक्षणः ।
The *ātman*, however, being the witness of all three states, is distinct from the deep sleep state.
इति सुषुप्त्यवस्थाविवेकः ।
Thus ends the discernment of the deep sleep state.
समष्टिपञ्चकोशविलक्षणम् अस्ति ।
[The reality of Īśvara] is distinct from the cosmic five sheaths.
चतुर्थतरङ्गे चतुर्विधाकाशदृष्टान्तेन जीवेश्वरयोः लक्ष्यस्वरूपविवेचनं विस्तरेण उक्तम् ।
In the fourth chapter (*taraṅga*), the discernment of the implied essential nature (*lakṣyasvarūpa*) of both *jīva* and *Īśvara* was explained in detail through the illustration of the fourfold space.
उपरि षष्ठतरङ्गे अपि अस्ति-भाति-प्रिय-रूप-निरूपण-प्रसङ्गे महावाक्यार्थ-निरूपण-प्रसङ्गे च आत्मनः परमार्थस्वरूपं निरूपयिष्यते ।
Further, in the sixth chapter as well, in the context of delineating the nature of *asti-bhāti-priya* (existence-radiance-belovedness) and in the context of analyzing the meaning of the *mahāvākya*s, the ultimate nature of the *ātman* will be expounded.
सङ्ग्रहेण अत्र आत्मविवेचनं कृतम् ।
Here, the discernment of the *ātman* has been presented in summary.
महावाक्यार्थोपदेशनिरूपणम्॥ २८४–३१६ ॥
284 · महावाक्यार्थोपदेशः
इत्थं पञ्चकोशेभ्यो विविच्यात्मज्ञानेऽपि न कृतकृत्यतासिद्धिः ।
In this manner, even upon having knowledge of the ātman by discriminating it from the five sheaths, the attainment of having accomplished all that was to be done is not yet achieved.
अतो जीवब्रह्माभेदनिश्चयाय पुनरपि विचारः कर्तव्य एव ।
Therefore, for the definitive ascertainment of the non-difference of the jīva and Brahman, further inquiry must indeed be undertaken.
तस्माच्छिष्यस्य कृतकृत्यतासिद्धये गुरुस्तस्मै महावाक्यार्थमेवमुपदिदेश - पञ्चकोशविलक्षणतया ज्ञातमात्मानं ब्रह्माभिन्नं विजानीहि इति ।
Hence, for the attainment of the disciple's fulfillment, the Guru instructed him in the meaning of the *mahāvākya* in this manner: 'Know the ātman, which has been known as distinct from the five sheaths, to be non-different from Brahman.'
285 · कर्तुर्भोक्तुश्चात्मनो ब्रह्माभेदासम्भव इति प्रश्नः
नन्वात्मा पुण्यपापे कृत्वा स्वर्गनरकपृथिव्यादिलोकेषु नानाविधानि सुखदुःखान्यनुभवति ।
Now, the *ātman*, having performed virtue and sin, experiences various pleasures and pains in worlds such as heaven, hell, and earth.
तस्य ब्रह्मणैक्यं नोपपद्येत इति चेत् अत्रोच्यते ।
If it is objected that its identity with Brahman would therefore be impossible, here it is answered:
आक्षेपःपूर्वोक्तप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ २८६–३१६ ॥
286 · अकर्तुरभोक्तुर्नित्यमुक्तस्यात्मनः सदा ब्रह्माभेदः सिद्ध एव
ब्रह्मस्वरूपादात्मनो भिन्नतया दृश्यमानं शास्त्रेषु श्रुतं च पुण्यपापस्वर्गनरकादिकं सर्वं मिथ्येति विजानीहि ।
Know that everything such as merit, demerit, heaven, and hell, which is seen as distinct from the ātman of the nature of Brahman or heard in the scriptures, is illusory (mithyā).
न हि मिथ्यावस्त्वधिष्ठानं दूषयति ।
For indeed, an illusory object does not contaminate its substratum (adhiṣṭhāna).
स्वप्ने भिक्षामटन् राजा न दरिद्रो भवति ।
A king begging for alms in a dream does not become poor in reality.
न मरीचिकोदकेन भूमिरार्द्रीभवति ।
The earth does not become wet by the water of a mirage.
न मिथ्यासर्पेण रज्जुः सविषा भवति ।
A rope does not become venomous on account of an illusory snake.
अतस्त्वं मिथ्याभूतसकलशुभाशुभकर्मणां कर्तापि वस्तुतो न कर्ता, अकर्तृत्वाभोक्तृत्वादिबोधकश्रुतिप्रमाणात् ।
Therefore, even though you appear to be the agent of all illusory auspicious and inauspicious actions, in reality you are not the agent, on account of the authority of the śruti that reveals non-doership, non-enjoyership, and so on.
इत्थं तव स्वरूपम् अत्याश्चर्यं निरुपमं च भवति ।
Thus your true nature is exceedingly wondrous and matchless.
अस्यायमभिप्रायः ।
This is the purport of it:
तव ब्रह्माभिन्ने स्वरूपे स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीरे तत्फलजन्ममरणस्वर्गनरकसुखदुःखादिकं सर्वमविद्यया कल्पितम् ।
Upon your true nature, which is non-different from Brahman, the gross and subtle bodies, as well as all their consequences such as birth, death, heaven, hell, pleasure, and pain, are superimposed by avidyā.
तव ब्रह्मस्वभावस्ताभिः कल्पितसामग्रीभिर्नान्यथा भवति ।
Your essential nature as Brahman is never altered by those superimposed accessories.
तस्माज्ज्ञानात्पूर्वमप्यात्मा ब्रह्मस्वरूप एवास्ते ।
Therefore, even prior to knowledge, the ātman remains indeed of the nature of Brahman.
कालत्रयेऽप्यात्मनि शरीरस्य तद्धर्माणां च सम्बन्धो नास्ति ।
In all three periods of time, there is no connection of the body or its attributes with the ātman.
आत्मा सदा नित्यमुक्त एवास्ते ।
The ātman always remains ever-liberated indeed.
आत्मनो ब्रह्मणश्च न कदापि भेदोऽस्ति ।
There is never any difference between the ātman and Brahman.
287 · जीवन्मुक्तस्य निश्चयः, वेदान्तश्रवणफलं च
आत्मा यदि सदा नित्यमुक्तब्रह्मस्वरूप एव तदा ज्ञाननिवर्त्याज्ञानतत्कार्याद्यभावात् ज्ञानसाधनश्रवणादिवैयर्थ्यम् इति चेत् न ।
If it is objected that if the *ātman* is ever of the nature of eternally free *Brahman* alone, then, because of the absence of *avidyā* to be dispelled by knowledge and its effects, the means to knowledge such as *śravaṇa* become futile — this is not so.
जीवन्मुक्तस्य विदुषो दृष्ट्या अज्ञानं तत्कार्यं च सर्वं तुच्छम् एव ।
From the perspective of the *jīvanmukta* knower, *avidyā* and its entire effect are utterly non-existent (*tuccha*).
तस्य जीवन्मुक्तस्य निश्चय इदानीं प्रदर्श्यते — अयं प्रपञ्चो गगनारविन्दवत् न अस्ति एव ।
The conviction of that *jīvanmukta* is now set forth: 'This phenomenal universe does not exist at all, just like a lotus in the sky.'
तस्मात् जगतः कर्ता ईश्वरः अपि न अस्ति ।
Therefore, even *Īśvara*, the creator of the universe, does not exist [as a distinct entity].
साक्षिणो विषयभूतम् अज्ञानादिकं साक्ष्यम् इति उच्यते ।
That which is the object of the witness (*sākṣin*), namely *avidyā* and the rest, is called the witnessed (*sākṣya*).
तादृशसाक्ष्याभावात् साक्षी न अस्ति ।
Because of the non-existence of such a witnessed entity, the witness (*sākṣin*) does not exist [as a witness].
दृश्यावभासकं दृक् इति उच्यते ।
That which illumines the seen (*dṛśya*) is termed the seer (*dṛk*).
देहादिरूपदृश्याभावात् दृक् अपि न अस्ति ।
Due to the absence of the seen in the form of the body and so on, even the seer (*dṛk*) does not exist.
न च केवलकूटस्थचैतन्यस्य एव साक्षी इति दृक् इति च व्यपदिश्यमानत्वात् साक्षिदृशोः निषेधो न युज्यते इति वाच्यम् ।
And it should not be argued that since pure immutable consciousness itself is designated as 'witness' and 'seer', the negation of the witness and seer is untenable.
साक्ष्यापेक्षया हि साक्षी इति, दृश्यापेक्षया हि दृक् इति च व्यपदेशः ।
For the designation as '*sākṣin*' is only in relation to a witnessed object (*sākṣya*), and the designation as '*dṛk*' is only in relation to a seen object (*dṛśya*).
साक्ष्यदृश्ययोरभावे साक्षी इति दृक् इति च व्यपदेशमात्रं निषिध्यते ।
In the absence of the witnessed and the seen, only the mere designations 'witness' and 'seer' are negated.
न तु स्वरूपं निषिध्यते ।
The essential nature (*svarūpa*), however, is not negated.
यदि बन्धः स्यात् तदा बन्धनिवृत्तिरूपमोक्षः अपि स्यात् ।
If bondage were to exist, then *mokṣa* in the form of cessation of bondage would also exist.
बन्धः अपि न अस्ति, मोक्षः अपि न अस्ति ।
Neither does bondage exist, nor does liberation exist.
यदि अज्ञानं स्यात् तत् ज्ञानेन नश्येत् ।
If *avidyā* were to exist, it would be destroyed by knowledge.
अज्ञानाभावात् तन्नाशकज्ञानम् अपि न अस्ति इति ज्ञात्वा कर्तव्यं परित्यजेत् ।
Realizing that 'Since there is no *avidyā*, there is also no knowledge that destroys it', one should abandon all duty.
मया इदं कर्तव्यम् इति बुद्धिं परित्यजेत् इति यावत् ।
That is to say, one should abandon the notion: 'This is to be done by me.'
यतः अयम् लोकः परः च लोकः तुच्छः, तस्मात् तल्लाभार्थम् अनुष्ठेयं किञ्चित् अपि न अस्ति ।
Because this world and the other world are illusory, there is nothing whatsoever to be performed for their attainment.
आत्मनि बन्धो न अस्ति ।
There is no bondage in the Self.
तस्मात् मोक्षार्थम् अपि कर्तव्यं किञ्चित् अपि न अस्ति ।
Therefore, even for the sake of *mokṣa*, there is nothing whatsoever to be done.
इत्थम् आत्मानं नित्यमुक्तब्रह्मस्वरूपेण ज्ञात्वा निश्चलो यदा कर्तव्यम् अखिलं संन्यस्यति तदा अक्रियब्रह्मस्वरूपविदेहमोक्षं लभते ।
Knowing the Self thus as of the nature of ever-free *Brahman*, when one remains unwavering and renounces all duty, one attains *videhamukti*, which is the nature of actionless *Brahman*.
अस्य अयम् अभिप्रायः — आत्मा ज्ञानात् पूर्वम् अपि नित्यमुक्तब्रह्मस्वरूप एव आस्ते ।
The purport of this is as follows: The *ātman*, even prior to knowledge, exists only as the nature of ever-free *Brahman*.
तथापि ज्ञानात् पूर्वं आत्मा कर्ता भोक्ता च इति मिथ्याग्रहणेन सुखप्राप्तये दुःखहत्यै च पुरुषः अनेकसाधनानि अनुतिष्ठन् वृथा क्लेशम् अनुभवति ।
Even so, prior to knowledge, on account of the false misconception 'the Self is a doer and enjoyer', a person performs various means to attain pleasure and ward off pain, thus experiencing toil in vain.
पुरुषस्य बहुजन्मार्जितपुण्यपुञ्जपरिपाकात् यदा उत्तमाचार्यलाभो भवति तदा स गुरुः वेदान्तवाक्यम् उपदिशति ।
When, through the ripening of the store of merit accumulated across many births, a person gains an excellent spiritual teacher, that guru instructs him in the statement of Vedānta.
तादृशवेदान्तवाक्यश्रवणेन न अहं कर्ता भोक्ता वा, किन्तु अहं ब्रह्मस्वरूपः । अतः च न मे किञ्चित् अपि कर्तव्यम् अस्ति इति पुरुषस्य ज्ञानम् उदेति ।
By listening to such a Vedāntic statement, the knowledge arises in the person: 'I am neither a doer nor an enjoyer, but I am of the nature of *Brahman*; therefore, there is nothing whatsoever for me to do.'
एतादृशं ज्ञानम् एव वेदान्तश्रवणादिफलम् ।
Such knowledge alone is the fruit of Vedāntic *śravaṇa* and the rest.
ब्रह्मप्राप्तिः तु न वेदान्तश्रवणफलम्, ब्रह्मणः स्वस्वरूपतया नित्यप्राप्तत्वात् ।
The attainment of *Brahman*, however, is not the fruit of Vedāntic *śravaṇa*, because *Brahman*, being one's own true nature, is already eternally attained.
288
ज्ञान्यज्ञानिनोश्चिह्नमकर्तव्यताबुद्धिर्ज्ञानिनश्चिह्नम् ।
Regarding the distinguishing mark between the wise and the ignorant: the awareness of having nothing left to be done is the mark of the wise.
अज्ञानिनस्तु कर्तव्यताबुद्धिश्चिह्नम् ।
However, the sense of having duties to perform is the mark of the ignorant.
यः स्वातिरिक्तं किञ्चिद्वस्तु स्वेन प्राप्तव्यमस्तीति मत्वा तत्प्राप्तये मया प्रयत्नः कर्तव्य इति मन्यते सोऽज्ञानी ।
He who thinks that there is some object apart from oneself to be attained by oneself, and believes, 'I must make effort to attain it,' is an ignorant person.
यः पुनः स्वेन प्राप्तव्यमन्यन्नास्तीति दृढनिश्चयेन रूपान्तरप्राप्तिं नेच्छति, किन्तु शान्तसङ्कल्पो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते स ज्ञानी ।
He, on the other hand, who, with the firm conviction that 'there is nothing else to be attained by me', does not desire the attainment of any other state, but being of pacified resolve longs for no desire whatsoever, is an enlightened one.
289 · गोप्यतत्त्वोपदेशः
चैतन्यस्वरूपं ब्रह्मैकमखण्डमसङ्गं जन्मादिभावविकारशून्यमदृश्यं नामरूपरहितमद्वितीयं स्वप्रकाशानन्दरूपं चास्ते ।
Brahman exists as one, partless, unattached, devoid of modifications of existence such as birth, invisible, free from name and form, non-dual, and of the nature of self-luminous bliss and pure consciousness.
न तत्र मूलाज्ञानमस्ति ।
Primal ignorance (*mūlāvidyā*) does not exist there.
न स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीराणि सन्ति ।
Gross and subtle bodies do not exist.
न समष्टिव्यष्टिप्रपञ्चोऽस्ति ।
Neither the cosmic nor the individual universe exists.
नेशोऽस्ति ।
There is no *Īśvara*.
न सूत्रात्मा, न वा विराडस्ति ।
There is neither *Sūtrātman* nor *Virāj*.
न विश्वतैजसप्राज्ञाः सन्ति ।
There are no *Viśva*, *Taijasa*, or *Prājña*.
न च भोगो वा योगो वा बन्धो वा मोक्षो वास्ति ।
And there is neither enjoyment, nor yoga, nor bondage, nor liberation (*mokṣa*).
न किञ्चिदपि द्वैतं तत्र विद्यते ।
No duality whatsoever exists there.
अथापि तस्मिन् ब्रह्मणि सर्वमप्यस्ति ।
Even so, everything exists in that Brahman.
तथा हि, जाग्रत्काले सकलमिदं दृश्यं जगत्तस्मिन् ब्रह्मणि बुद्धिपरिकल्पितं विलसति ।
To explain: during the waking state, this entire perceptible world, projected by the intellect, appears in that Brahman.
स्वप्नकाले च भोगभोग्यादीनामभावेऽपि विचित्रो नानाविधः प्रपञ्चो बुद्धिपरिकल्पितः प्रतीयते ।
And during the dream state, even in the absence of actual experience and objects of experience, a diverse, manifold world projected by the intellect is experienced.
सुषुप्तिकाले तु सा बुद्धिः प्रविलीना भवति ।
In the state of deep sleep, however, that intellect becomes fully dissolved.
तदा सकलदृश्यद्वैतप्रपञ्चरहितमद्वैतं चिन्मात्रं ब्रह्म प्रकाशते ।
Then, Brahman, devoid of the entire perceived universe of duality, non-dual and pure consciousness alone, shines forth.
बुद्धिपरिकल्पितं सर्वं मनोरथमात्रं मिथ्यैव ।
Whatever is projected by the intellect is a mere mental fancy, purely illusory.
निश्चलं कूटस्थं ब्रह्मैव तां बुद्धिं प्रकाशयति ।
Brahman alone, motionless and immutable, illuminates that intellect.
यस्य1,2,1
Of whom...
टिप्पणी
1.
ज्ञानी स्वव्यतिरिक्तद्वितीयवस्तुदर्शनश्रवणादिकं न करोतीति भगवद्गीतायां पञ्चमाध्याये सप्तमाष्टमनवमेषु श्लोकेषूक्तोऽर्थो मुमुक्षूणां बुद्धिवैशद्याय विस्पष्टं व्याख्यायतेऽत्र— योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः । सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ (भ. गी. ५.७) ।
That the knower of truth does not perform seeing, hearing, etc., of any second object distinct from the Self—the meaning stated in the Bhagavad Gītā, fifth chapter, verses seven, eight, and nine, is here clearly explained for the lucidity of seekers' understanding: One endowed with yoga, of purified mind, of subdued self, who has conquered his senses, whose self is the Self of all beings, even while acting is not tainted. (भ. गी. ५.७).
अस्यायमर्थः —
The meaning of this verse is as follows:
योगयुक्तः = निष्कामकर्मयोगेन वा ब्रह्मनिष्ठारूपसन्न्यासयोगेन वा युक्तः; अत एव विशुद्धात्मा = विशुद्धः = रागद्वेषादिरहितः आत्मा = मनो यस्य सः ।
'Yogayuktaḥ' = endowed with selfless karma-yoga or the yoga of renunciation in the form of steadfastness in Brahman; and therefore 'viśuddhātmā' = one whose 'ātmā', meaning mind, is purified, that is, free from attachment, aversion, and the like.
अत एव विजितात्मा = विजितो विषयेषु तुच्छत्वबुद्ध्या अभावरूपतामापादितः, आत्मा = बाह्यवासनारूपस्वभावो यस्य सः ।
And therefore 'vijitātmā' = one whose 'ātmā', meaning habitual nature formed of external latent impressions, has been conquered, that is, reduced to non-existence through the insight of the worthlessness of sense objects.
अत एव जितेन्द्रियः = जितानि विषयग्रहणाद्विमुखीकृतानि, इन्द्रियाणि = द्विविधानीन्द्रियाणि येन सः ।
And therefore 'jitendriyaḥ' = one by whom the 'indriyas', meaning both types of sense organs (knowledge and action), have been conquered, that is, turned away from grasping sense objects.
अत एव सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा = सर्वभूतानां = ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बान्तनिखिलप्राणिनाम्, आत्मभूतः = स्वरूपभूतः, आत्मा = प्रत्यग्रूप आत्मा यस्य सः ।
And therefore 'sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā' = one whose 'ātmā', the innermost Self, is 'ātmabhūtaḥ', meaning the essential nature, of 'sarvabhūtānām', that is, of all creatures from Lord Brahmā down to a blade of grass.
एवं सर्वात्मभावं प्राप्तो यो ब्रह्मवित् सः कुर्वन्नपि = प्रारब्धाक्षिप्तशरीरयात्रानिर्वाहककर्माणि पुण्यपापमिश्रात्मकानि विधिपूर्वकमविधिपूर्वकं वानुतिष्ठन्नपि न लिप्यते = अकर्ताहमभोक्ताहमसङ्गः परमेश्वरः इति दृढतरनिश्चयवान् कर्मणां फलेन न सम्बध्यते ।
Thus, that knower of Brahman who has realised identity with all beings, 'kurvann api' = even while executing actions required for bodily sustenance impelled by prārabdha karma—comprising meritorious, sinful, or mixed traits, performed either formally or informally—'na lipyate' = is not bound by the results of actions, having the firm conviction: I am the non-doer, I am the non-experiencer, unattached, the Supreme Lord.
2.
निश्चलं कूटस्थं ब्रह्म बुद्धिं प्रकाशयतीति वेदान्तसिद्धान्तः ।
The established conclusion of Vedānta is that the motionless, immutable Brahman illuminates the intellect.
अतो न क्षणिकविज्ञानवादिमतेऽतिव्याप्तिः ।
Therefore, there is no over-extension into the doctrine of the momentariness-of-consciousness theorists (Vijñānavāda Buddhists).
तेषां मते बुद्ध्यतिरिक्तस्य प्रकाशकपदार्थस्याभावात् ।
For in their view, there is an absence of any illuminating entity distinct from the intellect.
हृदये दृढतरं ज्ञानमेवमुदेति तस्य हृदयादज्ञानान्धाकारो निश्शेषं ध्रुवं विनश्यति ।
When firm knowledge arises in this way in the heart, the blinding darkness of avidyā surely perishes completely from his heart.
स सदा असङ्गैकरसस्वयम्प्रकाशब्रह्मस्वरूपतयैवात्मानमनुभवति ।
He always experiences the Self solely as the nature of unattached, homogeneous, self-luminous Brahman.
तस्य दृष्ट्या न किञ्चिदपि दृश्यं द्वैतमभूत् भवति भविष्यति वा ।
From his perspective, no perceptible duality ever was, is, or will be.
तस्य दृष्ट्या सकलमिदं जगन्मनोरथमात्रविलसितम् ।
From his perspective, this entire world is merely a play of imagination.
न हि ज्ञानी तादृशस्य जगतः प्राप्तिं निवृत्तिं वा इच्छति ।
Indeed, the enlightened one does not desire the attainment or removal of such a world.
न हि ज्ञानिनः काचिदप्याशास्ति ।
For the enlightened one has no desire whatsoever.
ज्ञानी हि चक्षुषा पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ।
Indeed, even though the enlightened one sees with the eye, he does not see.
श‍ृण्वन्नपि न श‍ृणोति, रसयन्नपि न रसयति, स्पृशन्नपि न स्पृशति, जिघ्रन्नपि न जिघ्रति ।
Even while hearing he does not hear, tasting he does not taste, touching he does not touch, smelling he does not smell.
वदन्नपि न वदति ।
Even while speaking he does not speak.
गृह्णन्नपि न गृह्णाति ।
Even while grasping he does not grasp.
विसृजन्नपि न विसृजति ।
Even while discharging/relinquishing he does not discharge.
गच्छन्नपि न गच्छति ।
Even while walking he does not walk.
युवतिमनुभवन्नपि नित्यसन्न्यासी भवति ।
Even while experiencing a young woman, he remains an eternal renunciant.
गुरुःहे सोम्य, महदिदमाश्चर्यं विजानीहीत्याह गुरुः ।
'O gentle one, know this to be a great marvel,' said the Guru.
1.
इदानीं योगयुक्तत्वविशुद्धात्मत्वविजितेन्द्रियत्वसर्वभूतात्मभूतत्वरूपपञ्चलक्षणविशिष्टस्य आहारादिविषये प्रवृत्तस्य ब्रह्मविदो दर्शनश्रवणादिरूपेन्द्रियव्यापारेषु नाहं कर्ता इति या सुदृढा बुद्धिः सा उचिता एव इति द्वाभ्यां श्लोकाभ्याम् उच्यते— नैव किञ्चित् करोमि इति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् । पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन् अश्नन् गच्छन् स्वपन् श्वसन् ॥ प्रलपन् विसृजन् गृह्णन् उन्मिषन् निमिषन् अपि । इन्द्रियाणि इन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्ते इति धारयन् ॥ (भ. गी. ५.८-९) ।
Now, that the firm conviction 'I am not the doer' in the activities of the senses such as seeing and hearing is entirely appropriate for the knower of Brahman who is endowed with the five characteristics—steadfastness in yoga, pure mind, conquered senses, and being the self of all beings—and engaged in objects such as eating, is declared in two verses: 'The steadfast knower of truth should think: I do nothing at all, while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing, speaking, discharging, seizing, opening and closing the eyes—holding firmly that the senses operate among sense-objects' (Bhagavad-gītā 5.8-9).
अनयोः अर्थः— तत्त्ववित् = आत्मनः स्वभावं जानन् ब्रह्मवित् ।
The meaning of these two verses is: 'tattvavit' = the knower of Brahman who knows the essential nature of the Self.
युक्तः = आत्मनः कूटस्थत्वासङ्गत्वान्तर्बहिःपूर्णत्वादिदर्शनरूपप्रज्ञया युक्तः सन्, पश्यन् रूपम्, श‍ृण्वन् शब्दम्, स्पृशन् स्पर्शम्, जिघ्रन् गन्धम्, अश्नन् अन्नादिकम्, गच्छन् देशान्तरम्, स्वपन् = निद्रामनुभवन्, श्वसन् = प्राणव्यापारं कुर्वन्, प्रलपन् = शब्दमुच्चारयन्, विसृजन् = मलमूत्रादित्यागं कुर्वन्, गृह्णन् = दानादानादिकं कुर्वन्, उन्मिषन् = नेत्रोन्मीलनं कुर्वन्, निमिषन् = नेत्रनिमीलनं कुर्वन् ।
'yuktaḥ' = being endowed with wisdom consisting of the direct perception of the Self's immutability, unattachedness, all-pervading plenitude within and without, etc.; 'paśyan' = seeing form; 'śṛṇvan' = hearing sound; 'spṛśan' = touching touch; 'jighran' = smelling fragrance; 'aśnan' = eating food etc.; 'gacchan' = moving to another place; 'svapan' = experiencing sleep; 'śvasan' = functioning through the breath; 'pralapan' = uttering speech; 'visṛjan' = eliminating bodily wastes; 'gṛhṇan' = giving and receiving; 'unmiṣan' = opening the eyes; 'nimiṣan' = closing the eyes.
अपि-शब्दात् यदपि अन्यत् कर्म कर्तव्यतया प्राप्तं तत् सर्वं बहिर्दृष्ट्या अनुतिष्ठन् अपि ।
By the word 'api' (even), whatever other action is presented as a duty, even while performing all of that from the external standpoint—
इन्द्रियाणि = दशेन्द्रियाणि, इन्द्रियार्थेषु = शब्दादिस्वस्वविषयेषु वर्तन्ते = श्रवणादिरूपस्वस्वव्यापारं कुर्वन्ति इति = नाहं श्रोता, स्प्रष्टा, द्रष्टा, रसयिता, घ्राता, भोक्ता, गन्ता वा इत्यादिलक्षणां वृत्तिं धारयन् = सदा वहन्, नैव किञ्चित् करोमि इति इन्द्रियाणि एव स्वस्वकर्माणि कुर्वन्ति ।
'indriyāṇi' = the ten senses; 'indriyārtheṣu' = in their respective objects like sound etc.; 'vartante' = perform their respective functions such as hearing etc.; 'dhārayan' = constantly maintaining the mental modification of the form: 'I am not the hearer, toucher, seer, taster, smeller, enjoyer, or mover'; 'I do nothing at all' means that only the senses perform their respective actions.
अहं तु अक्रियत्वात् न किञ्चिदपि कर्म करोमि ।
'I, however, being actionless, do not perform any action whatsoever.
परन्तु तत्तदिन्द्रियकर्मणां साक्षी भूत्वा निष्क्रियस्वस्वरूपेण तूष्णीम् अस्मि इति मन्येत = जानीयात् ।
Rather, becoming the *sākṣin* of the functions of those respective senses, I remain quiet in my own actionless nature'—so he should think, that is, realize.
देहेन्द्रियादीनां व्यापारेषु अहं मम इति भावनां हित्वा विद्वान् तूष्णीं स्थातुम् अर्हति इति श्लोकद्वयस्य सम्पिण्डितः अर्थः ।
Abandoning the notions of 'I' and 'mine' regarding the operations of the body, senses, and the like, the wise knower ought to abide quietly—this is the consolidated meaning of the two verses.
अत्र इदम् आकूतम्— ज्ञानिनः सदा असङ्ग-निर्विकार-चिन्मात्र-स्वरूप-ब्रह्म एव अहम् इति दृढनिश्चयसत्त्वात् सः परमार्थतः न कामपि क्रियां करोति ।
Here, this is the underlying intention: because the jñānin possesses the constant, firm conviction 'I am indeed Brahman whose nature is unattached, immutable pure consciousness', he in absolute truth performs no action whatsoever.
प्रारब्धवशात् तु तस्य देहेन्द्रियद्वारा दर्शनादिकाः क्रियाः सम्भवन्ति ।
However, by the force of *prārabdha*, actions such as seeing occur through his body and senses.
ताः च क्रियाः तस्य प्रारब्धफलोपभोगरूपाः ।
And those actions constitute the experiencing of the fruit of his *prārabdha*.
परन्तु प्रारब्धबलात् आयातान् तान् तान् भोगान् भुञ्जानस्य अपि ज्ञानिनः न भोगेषु रागो जायते ।
However, even while experiencing those various objects brought by the momentum of *prārabdha*, no attachment arises in the *jñānin* toward those experiences.
तथा हि— नापि आत्मकृतः, आत्मनः सर्वदृश्यावभासकसाधारणनिर्विकारप्रकाशस्वरूपत्वात् ।
To explain: nor is attachment produced by the Self, because the Self is of the nature of changeless illumination, the common illuminator of all perceivable phenomena.
परिशेषात् विषयनिष्ठगुणदोषविवेचनसमर्थमनस एवानुकूले विषये रागो भवति ।
By elimination, attachment arises only in the mind that is capable of discerning virtues and flaws residing in objects, toward an agreeable object.
स च रागो ज्ञानिनो मनसि नैवोन्मिषति, ज्ञानिनो मनसोऽन्तर्मुखतयातीवोपशान्तत्वात् ।
And that attachment never arises in the mind of the *jñānin*, because his mind, being turned inward, is exceedingly tranquil.
रागो लिङ्गमबोधस्य (नै. सि. ४.६७) इति हि शास्त्रप्रसिद्धिः ।
For scriptural tradition confirms: 'Attachment is the mark of ignorance' (Naiṣkarmyasiddhi 4.67).
ज्ञानिनः सर्वथा रागानुदये तस्य शरीरस्थितिनिमित्तभोजनादावप्यप्रवृत्त्यापत्त्यां ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धानुभवो नास्तीत्यापद्येत ।
[Objection]: If no attachment arises whatsoever in the knower, then because of the contingency of non-engagement even in eating meant for bodily sustenance, it would result that the knower has no experience of *prārabdha* at all.
न च इयम् आपत्तिः इष्टा एव इति वक्तुं शक्यते, कर्मानुसारेण प्राणिनां फलदातुः ईश्वरस्य इच्छया ज्ञानिनः अपि प्रारब्धानुभवस्य आवश्यकत्वात् ।
Nor can it be said that this consequence is acceptable, because by the will of Īśvara, who dispenses fruits according to past karma, the experiencing of *prārabdha* is inevitable even for the knower.
तस्मात् ज्ञानिनः अपि प्रारब्धफलानुभवान्यथानुपपत्त्या भोजनादौ इच्छा उदेति इति वाच्यम् इति चेत्— तन्न ।
Therefore, one must state that desire for food etc. does arise in the knower too, by postulation without which the experience of *prārabdha* cannot be explained—if this is argued, that is not correct.
प्रारब्धजनितो रोगादिः यथा ज्ञानिनः इच्छाविरहेऽपि भवति तथैव तस्य मिथ्याज्ञानाभावात् प्रारब्धफलभोगे अदृढः आभासरूपः रागाभासरूपो रागो जायते ।
Just as disease etc. produced by *prārabdha* occurs to the knower even without any desire for it, exactly so, owing to the absence of erroneous knowledge in him, in the experiencing of the fruit of *prārabdha* there arises only a feeble, semblance-like attachment—a mere semblance of desire (*rāgābhāsa*).
अदृढत्वादेव स रागः स्वनिवृत्तये न वेदान्तविचारादिकमपेक्षते ।
Precisely because of being feeble, that attachment does not require Vedāntic inquiry and the like for its cessation.
सः अयम् अदृढः रागः स्वायत्तत्वेन भर्जितबीजवद् दुर्बलत्वेन च शरीरस्थितिमात्रनिमित्तशास्त्रीयभोगमात्रे हेतुर्भवति, न तु व्यसनकारणीभूतशास्त्रनिषिद्धभोगहेतुः ।
This feeble attachment, being under his control and weak like a roasted seed, becomes the cause only for scripturally permitted experiences meant merely for bodily sustenance, and never the cause for prohibited enjoyments that produce addiction.
अपि च ज्ञानिनो विषयसत्यताभ्रान्त्यभावात्, प्रत्युत दृढतरविषयमिथ्यात्वनिश्चयजनिततीव्रतरवैराग्यबलाच्च दृढरागो नैव भवति ।
Furthermore, because of the absence in the knower of any delusion regarding the reality of objects, and on the contrary, by virtue of the intense dispassion born of the firm conviction of the falsity of objects, firm attachment never occurs.
अयमर्थः स्पष्टं षष्ठतरङ्गे वक्ष्यते ।
This point will be explained clearly in the sixth wave.
अथवा शाखाग्रं वा रज्जुं वारुह्य नृत्यतोऽपि मल्लस्य चित्तं यथा स्वावलम्बे एव जागरूकं भवति, यथा वा क्षीरपूर्णं कुम्भं धृत्वा गच्छन्त्या योषितः पथि स्वसखीभिः सह वार्तासल्लापादिकं कुर्वाणाया अपि चित्तं क्षीरे एवैकाग्रं भवति, तथा ज्ञानिनोऽपि चित्तं प्रारब्धवशादापाततो विषयेषु प्रवृत्तमपि विशेषतो लक्ष्ये स्वात्मस्वरूप एव निष्ठितं भवति ।
Alternatively, just as an acrobat dancing atop a tree branch or a tightrope keeps his mind vigilant solely on his support, or just as a woman walking on the path carrying a pot full of milk keeps her mind one-pointed on the milk even while chatting with her friends, so too the mind of the *jñānin*, though casually engaged in objects by force of *prārabdha*, remains fundamentally established in its true target—the essential nature of the Self alone.
किञ्च ज्ञानिनो देहेन्द्रियादिवर्गो विनैव रागं प्रारब्धफलत्वेनोपगतदर्शनादिक्रिययैव कृतार्थतां याति ।
Moreover, the aggregate of body, senses, and so forth of the knower attains its fulfillment merely through the actions of seeing etc. that arrive as the fruits of *prārabdha*, entirely without any attachment.
अतश्च स्वात्मस्वरूपेऽवस्थितस्य ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धफलायातभोगाभासेषु न दृढतररागसम्भवः ।
And therefore, for the *jñānin* established in his own true Self, there is no possibility of firm attachment toward the semblances of enjoyment brought by the fruit of *prārabdha*.
कदाचित्, विषयप्रवृत्तिहेतुभूतप्रारब्धवतो ज्ञानिनो मनो मत्तगजेन्द्रवत्प्रमत्तं सत् विषयेषु विक्षिप्तमपि, विषयेषु दोषदृष्ट्यात्मकविवेकमृगेन्द्रोन्मेषात् झटित्येव विक्षेपाद्विमुक्तं प्रशान्तं भवति ।
Sometimes, even if the mind of the *jñānin* endowed with *prārabdha* that causes engagement in objects becomes distracted among objects like a mad elephant, it instantly becomes freed from distraction and tranquil through the manifestation of the lion of discrimination whose nature is seeing defects in objects.
स्वान्तःकरणे तीव्ररागाभावात् भोगहेतुप्रारब्धसत्त्वाच्च गङ्गानिमग्नार्धगात्रः पुरुष इव ज्ञानी मुख्यतया स्वरूपसुखे रमते ।
Owing to the absence of strong attachment in his mind and the presence of *prārabdha* causing experience, the *jñānin*, like a man half-submerged in the sacred waters of the Gaṅgā, primarily delights in the intrinsic bliss of his true Self.
अमुख्यतया वेतनग्राही भृतक इव क्लेशं सहमानः तीव्रप्रारब्धफलं चानुभवति ।
Secondarily, like a hired servant enduring hardship for wages, he endures suffering and experiences the intense fruit of *prārabdha*.
शिथिलप्रारब्धफलभूतनिषिद्धविषयान् प्रयत्नेन परिहरति च ।
And he deliberately avoids prohibited objects that are the fruits of weak *prārabdha*.
तथापि ज्ञाननिर्भिन्नहृदयग्रन्थेर्ज्ञानिनोऽन्तःकरणस्य क्षीणवासनत्वात्तीव्रतररागाभावाच्च निषिद्धविषयपरित्यागेनादृढरागेण विहितविषयभोगेऽपि विकलपुरुषचित्तस्येव ज्ञानिनोऽन्तःकरणस्य न मुख्यतेत्ययमभिप्रायः, इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्ते इति जडेन्द्रियाणामेव स्वस्वविषयेषु प्रवृत्तिं वर्णयता गीताश्लोकेन बोध्यते ।
Nevertheless, because the *jñānin*, whose heart-knot has been severed by knowledge, has attenuated latent impressions and lacks strong attachment, even when he experiences permitted objects with feeble attachment while renouncing prohibited ones, his mind has no primary involvement, just like the mind of an indifferent person—this very import is conveyed by the Gītā verse describing the activity of the inert senses alone among their respective objects with 'indriyāṇi indriyārtheṣu vartante'.
ज्ञानी युवतिम् अनुभवन् अपि सन्न्यासी इति उक्तेः अयम् आशयः— विरक्तस्य दारैषणातः व्युत्थितस्य सन्न्यासिनः ज्ञानिनः न स्त्रीभोगप्रसक्तिः ।
The purport of the saying 'The jñānin, even while experiencing a young woman, is a sannyāsin' is this: for a renunciant *jñānin* who is dispassionate and has risen above the desire for a wife, there is no possibility of enjoying a woman.
तस्य स्त्रीप्रसक्तौ व्युत्थानशास्त्रं निरर्थकं भवेत् ।
If he were attached to women, the scriptures ordaining renunciation (*vyutthāna*) would become completely futile.
वान्ताशी स सन्न्यास्येव न भवेत् ।
Eating what has been vomited, he would not even be a renunciant.
किन्तु वेषधारी डाम्भिकः गृहस्थात् अपि अधमः अपूज्यः च ।
Rather, he would be a mere hypocritical impostor in ascetic garb, lower than even a householder and unworthy of reverence.
परिशेषात् गृहस्थे ज्ञानिनि स्त्रीभोगः प्रसज्यते ।
By elimination, enjoyment of a woman applies only in the case of a householder *jñānin*.
स ज्ञानी गृहस्थो घृता-॥
That householder knower [is like one smeared with] ghee...
लयचिन्तनक्रमः॥ २९०–२९२ ॥
290
सकलमपि प्रपञ्चमीश्वरस्वरूपतया चिन्तयेत् इत्थं परमार्थतत्त्वे उपदिष्टेऽपि शिष्यमुखेऽप्रसन्नतामालक्ष्य नूनमयमकृतार्थो यतोऽस्य मुखमप्रसन्नमास्ते इति गुरुर्निरचिनोत् ।
Even though the ultimate reality was instructed in this way—'One should contemplate the entire universe as the nature of Īśvara'—the Guru, noticing discontent on the disciple's face, determined: 'Surely this disciple remains unfulfilled, since his face looks despondent.'
अतः पुनरपि तं स्थूलदृष्ट्योपदिशन्प्रपञ्चलयचिन्तनप्रकारमाह - यथा मृत्कार्यभूतो घटोऽन्तर्बहिश्च मृदेव भवतीति मृत्कार्यं सर्वमपि मृदेव ।
Therefore, instructing him once more from a gross viewpoint, the Guru explains the manner of contemplating the dissolution of the universe: Just as a pot, which is an effect of clay, is clay alone inside and out, so every effect of clay is clay alone.
यथा च जलकार्यभूतफेनबुद्बुदादिकं सर्वमपि जलमेव भवति ।
And just as foam, bubbles, and other effects of water are all water alone,
तथा यद्यस्य कार्यं तत्तादृशकारणस्वरूपमेव भवति ।
likewise, whatever is the effect of something, that effect is of the very nature of such a cause alone.
न कार्यं कारणस्वरूपादतिरिच्यते ।
An effect is not distinct from the nature of its cause.
सकलस्य प्रपञ्चस्य मूलकारणमीश्वर एव ।
The primal cause of the entire phenomenal world is Īśvara alone.
तस्मात्सकलोऽपि कार्यप्रपञ्च ईश्वरस्वरूपान्नातिरिच्यते ।
Therefore, the entire universe of effects is not separate from the nature of Īśvara.
सकलप्रपञ्चस्यापि स्वरूपमीश्वर एव ।
The essential nature of the entire universe is Īśvara alone.
स चेश्वरोऽहमेव इति ज्ञात्वा सकलप्रपञ्चस्य लयं स्वस्मिन्ननुचिन्तयेत् ।
Realising 'And that Īśvara is myself alone', one should contemplate the dissolution of the entire universe in oneself.
291
स्थूलप्रपञ्चस्य पञ्चीकृतभूतस्वरूपत्वं सूक्ष्मसृष्टेरपञ्चीकृतभूतस्वरूपत्वं च चिन्तयेत् ।
One should contemplate the nature of the gross world as quintupled elements, and the nature of the subtle creation as unquintupled elements.
शिनस्तैलपाने प्रवृत्तिवत् सन्तानार्थी सन् शास्त्रविधिमनतिक्रम्य विधिनोढां जायामृतुकाले गच्छन्नपि न लिप्यते, यतः स भोगासक्त्या न स्त्रियं गच्छति ।
