Just as a sick man takes oil (as medicine without craving), one who desires progeny, without transgressing scriptural rules, approaching his lawfully wedded wife at the fertile season, is not tainted, because he does not approach the woman out of attachment to sensual enjoyment.
विषयमिथ्यात्वदर्शनेन विवेकवैराग्यादिसम्पन्नत्वात् तादृशो गृहस्थो ज्ञानी उपचारात्सन्न्यासीत्युच्यते ।
Because of being endowed with discrimination, dispassion, and so on through the perception of the unreality of sense-objects, such a householder who is a knower of truth is figuratively called a renunciant (*saṃnyāsin*).
सन्न्यासिन इव तस्यापि विवेकवैराग्यादिसम्पन्नत्वात् ।
For like a *saṃnyāsin*, he too is endowed with discrimination, dispassion, and the like.
यस्तु विवेकवैराग्यादिविकलो भोगासक्त्यैव स्त्रियं गच्छति स वेदान्तप्रवचनपटुरपि न ज्ञानी ।
He, however, who, devoid of discrimination and dispassion, approaches a woman purely out of attachment to enjoyment, is not a knower of truth, even if he is skilled in lecturing on Vedānta.
रागादेरनिवृत्त्या सोऽज्ञान्येव ।
Because of the non-cessation of attachment and other defects, he is only an ignorant person.
अत्र स्त्रीरूपविषयमधिकृत्य कृतो विचारः सर्वविषयविचारोपलक्षणार्थः ।
Here, the deliberation made regarding the object in the form of a woman is meant as illustrative of deliberation on all sense-objects.
रागरूपदोषप्रतिषेधश्च द्वेषादिसर्वदोषप्रतिषेधोपलक्षणार्थो वेदितव्यः ।
And the prohibition of the defect in the form of attachment should be understood as indicating the prohibition of all defects such as hatred and the like.
अयमभिप्रायः - इन्द्रियेषु स्वस्वव्यापारेषु व्यापृतेष्वपि न मे तत्रास्ति सम्पर्कः । नाहमिन्द्रियवर्गः । इन्द्रियवर्गश्च न मम । अहं तु साक्षी कूटस्थोऽसङ्गः । इन्द्रियाणि विषयेषु प्रवर्तन्तां वा ततो निवर्तन्तां वा । न मे तत्र सम्बन्धलेशोऽपि इत्येवं ज्ञानिनो निश्चयसत्त्वादेव स कर्माणि कुर्वन्निव लक्ष्यमाणोऽपि न परमार्थतः किञ्चिदपि करोति ।
The purport is: 'Even when the senses are active in their respective operations, I have no contact with them. I am not the senses, nor are the senses mine. I am the witness (*sākṣin*), changeless (*kūṭastha*), unattached. Let the senses engage in sense-objects or withdraw from them; I do not have even the slightest relation to them.' Because the enlightened one has such firm conviction, even though he appears to be performing actions, in ultimate reality he does nothing at all.
टिप्पणी
1.
अभिलषितार्थप्राप्तौ चित्तचाञ्चल्यहेतुभूतेच्छारूपवृत्तिनाशे तेनैव निमित्तेनोदितायामन्तर्मुखायामन्तःकरणस्य सात्त्विकवृत्तौ निश्चलदर्पणादाविव स्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बो भवति ।
Upon attaining a desired object, when the desire-mode (*vṛtti*) causing mental agitation is destroyed, the reflection of intrinsic bliss (*svarūpānanda*) arises in the inward-turned *sāttvika* mode of the mind produced by that very circumstance, just as in an unmoving mirror.
तमानन्दमनुभवतो मुखविकासो भवति ।
For the person experiencing that bliss, a cheerful bloom on the face occurs.
प्रकृते च शिष्यस्याविद्यातत्कार्यनिवृत्तिपूर्वकपरमानन्दरूपमोक्षो ज्ञानद्वारा प्राप्तुमिष्टः ।
In the present context, liberation (*mokṣa*)—which is of the nature of supreme bliss preceded by the cessation of *avidyā* and its effects—is desired to be attained by the disciple through knowledge.
अभिलषितार्थसिद्ध्यभावाच्च शिष्यस्येच्छारूपचित्तवृत्तिविनाशो नाभवत् ।
And because the attainment of the desired end was not achieved, the destruction of the mental mode in the form of desire did not occur for the disciple.
इच्छारूपवृत्तिनिवृत्त्यात्मकनिमित्ताभावादन्तर्मुखवृत्त्युदयः, तस्मिन् स्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बोदयः, तदनुभवजन्यमुखविकासश्च न शिष्यस्याभवत् ।
Due to the absence of the cause consisting of the cessation of the desire-mode, neither the emergence of the inward-turned mental mode, nor the reflection of intrinsic bliss in it, nor the facial radiance generated by that experience occurred for the disciple.
तेन मुखविकासाभावेन शिष्यस्याकृतार्थतानुमिताभूत् ।
By that absence of facial radiance, the disciple's state of not having attained his goal was inferred.
2.
कार्यस्य कारणस्वरूपतां ज्ञात्वा तदनतिरिक्तत्वचिन्तनमेव लयचिन्तनमुच्यते ।
Knowing an effect to have the nature of its cause, contemplating its non-difference from it is alone called dissolution-contemplation (*laya-cintana*).
स्थूलमिदं ब्रह्माण्डमखिलमपि पञ्चीकृतभूतकार्यम् ।
This entire gross universe is an effect of the quintupled elements.
तत्र पृथिवीकार्यं सर्वं पृथिवीस्वरूपम् ।
There, all that is an effect of earth is of the nature of earth.
जलकार्यं सर्वं जलस्वरूपम् ।
All that is an effect of water is of the nature of water.
इत्थमेव यद्यद्भूतकार्यं तत्तद्भूतस्वरूपमित्यखिलस्यापि ब्रह्माण्डस्य पञ्चीकृतपञ्चभूतस्वरूपत्वमनुचिन्तयेत् ।
In this manner, whatever is an effect of a given element is of the nature of that element; thus one should contemplate the entire cosmos as being of the nature of the quintupled five elements.
तथैव पञ्चीकृतं सर्वमपि भूतमपञ्चीकृतभूतकार्यत्वादपञ्चीकृतभूतस्वरूपमिति चिन्तयेत् ।
Likewise, one should contemplate that every quintupled element, being an effect of unquintupled elements, is of the nature of unquintupled elements.
अन्तःकरणादिसूक्ष्मसृष्टिरप्यपञ्चीकृतभूतकार्यत्वादपञ्चीकृतभूतस्वरूपमिति चिन्तयेत् ।
One should also contemplate that the subtle creation beginning with the inner organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*), being an effect of the unquintupled elements, is of the nature of the unquintupled elements.
अन्तःकरणं सर्वभूतसमष्टिसत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वात्सत्त्वगुणस्वरूपमेव ।
The inner organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*), being an effect of the collective *sattva-guṇa* of all elements, is of the nature of *sattva-guṇa* alone.
तथा प्राणोऽपि पूर्वोक्तपञ्चभूतसमष्टिरजोगुणकार्यत्वात् रजोगुणस्वरूप एव ।
Likewise, the vital breath (*prāṇa*), being an effect of the collective *rajo-guṇa* of the aforementioned five elements, is of the nature of *rajo-guṇa* alone.
पाय्विन्द्रियं पृथिव्या रजोगुणकार्यत्वात् पृथिव्या रजोगुणस्वरूपमेव ।
The excretory organ (*pāyvindriya*), being an effect of the *rajo-guṇa* of earth, is of the nature of the *rajo-guṇa* of earth alone.
घ्राणेन्द्रियं पृथिव्याः सत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वात् पृथिव्याः सत्त्वगुणस्वरूपमेव ।
The olfactory organ (*ghrāṇendriya*), being an effect of the *sattva-guṇa* of earth, is of the nature of the *sattva-guṇa* of earth alone.
तथैव रसनेन्द्रियमुपस्थेन्द्रियञ्च जलस्य क्रमेण सत्त्वगुणरजोगुणकार्यत्वात् तत्तत्स्वरूपमेव ।
Similarly, the organ of taste and the organ of generation, being effects respectively of the *sattva-guṇa* and *rajo-guṇa* of water, are of their respective natures alone.
चक्षुरिन्द्रियं पादेन्द्रियञ्च तेजसः क्रमेण सत्त्वगुणरजोगुणस्वरूपे ।
The organ of sight and the organ of movement (feet) are of the nature of the *sattva-guṇa* and *rajo-guṇa* of fire respectively.
त्वगिन्द्रियं पाणीन्द्रियञ्च वायोः क्रमेण सत्त्वगुणरजोगुणस्वरूपे ।
The organ of touch and the organ of action (hands) are of the nature of the *sattva-guṇa* and *rajo-guṇa* of air respectively.
श्रोत्रेन्द्रियं वागिन्द्रियं चाकाशस्य क्रमेण सत्त्वगुणरजोगुणस्वरूपे ।
The organ of hearing and the organ of speech are of the nature of the *sattva-guṇa* and *rajo-guṇa* of space respectively.
इत्थं सूक्ष्मसृष्टिः समग्राप्यपञ्चीकृतभूतस्वरूपैवेति चिन्तयेत् ।
Thus one should contemplate that the entire subtle creation is of the nature of unquintupled elements alone.
292 · अपञ्चीकृतभूतानां प्रकृतौ प्रधाने प्रधानस्य ब्रह्मणि च लयं चिन्तयेत्
प्रागुक्तचिन्तनानन्तरमपञ्चीकृतभूतानामपि लयश्चिन्तनीयः ।
After the aforementioned contemplation, the dissolution of the unquintuplicated elements also is to be meditated upon.
पृथिवी जलकार्यत्वात् जलस्वरूपा ।
Earth, being an effect of water, is of the nature of water.
जलं तेजःकार्यत्वात्तेजःस्वरूपम् ।
Water, being an effect of fire, is of the nature of fire.
तेजो वायुकार्यत्वाद्वायुस्वरूपम् ।
Fire, being an effect of air, is of the nature of air.
वायुराकाशकार्यत्वादाकाशस्वरूपः ।
Air, being an effect of space, is of the nature of space.
आकाशस्तमोगुणप्रधानप्रकृतिकार्यत्वात्प्रकृतिस्वरूपः ।
Space, being an effect of prakṛti predominated by tamoguṇa, is of the nature of prakṛti.
प्रकृतिर्मायाया अवस्थाविशेषत्वान्मायास्वरूपा ।
Prakṛti, being a particular state of māyā, is of the nature of māyā.
एकमेव वस्तु प्रधानम्, प्रकृतिः, माया, अविद्या, अज्ञानम्, शक्तिः इत्यनेकशब्दैर्व्यपदिश्यते ।
The very same entity is designated by various terms: 'pradhāna', 'prakṛti', 'māyā', 'avidyā', 'ajñāna', and 'śakti'.
तदेव वस्तु सकलमपि कार्यजातं स्वस्मिन्नुपसंहृत्य प्रलयकाले उदासीनस्वरूपेण वर्तमानत्वात् प्रधानं इत्युच्यते ।
That very entity, because it exists in a dormant/neutral state at the time of cosmic dissolution after withdrawing the entire aggregate of effects into itself, is called pradhāna.
तदेव वस्तु प्रपञ्चसृष्ट्युपादानतायोग्यतमोगुणप्रधानस्वरूपेण विद्यमानत्वात् प्रकृतिरित्याखायते ।
That very entity, because it exists in a form predominated by tamoguṇa suitable for being the material cause in the creation of the world, is designated as prakṛti.
देशकालादिसामग्रीं विनैवेन्द्रजालेन दुर्घटानेक1
टिप्पणी
1.
सकलमिदं जगत् यस्मात् प्रकर्षेण क्रियते तादृशं सृष्ट्युपादानभूतं वस्तु प्रकृतिः इत्युच्यते ।
That entity from which this entire universe is eminently produced, which is the material cause of creation, is called 'prakṛti'.
अथवा प्र इति सत्त्वगुणः, कृ इति रजोगुणः, ति इति सत्त्वरजस्सहिततमोगुण उच्यते ।
Alternatively, 'pra' denotes sattvaguṇa, 'kṛ' denotes rajoguṇa, and 'ti' denotes tamoguṇa accompanied by sattva and rajas.
तथा च तमोगुणप्रधाना प्रकृतिरिति सिद्ध्यति ।
And thus it is established that prakṛti is predominated by tamoguṇa.
पदार्थोत्पादनकाले इन्द्रजालं माया इति व्यपदिश्यते ।
At the time of producing magical appearances, jugglery is designated as 'māyā'.
तद्वदेवासङ्गेऽद्वितीये ब्रह्मणि दुर्घटेच्छाद्युत्पादकत्वात्तदेव वस्तु मायेति भण्यते ।
Just so, because of producing impossible phenomena such as desire in the unattached, non-dual Brahman, that very entity is declared to be 'māyā'.
तदेव वस्तु ब्रह्मस्वरूपावारकत्वादज्ञानमिति कीर्त्यते ।
That very entity, because of veiling the true nature of Brahman, is described as 'ajñāna'.
तदेव वस्तु ब्रह्मविद्याविनाश्यत्वादविद्येति वर्ण्यते ।
That very entity, because of being destructible by the knowledge of Brahman, is described as 'avidyā'.
तदेव वस्तु कदापि स्वातन्त्र्येणानवस्थितं सत् ब्रह्मचैतन्यमाश्रित्यैव वर्तमानत्वाच्छक्तिरिति च व्यपदिश्यते ।
And that very entity, never existing independently, but existing solely by depending upon Brahman-consciousness, is designated as 'śakti'.
इत्थं प्रकृत्यादयः प्रधानस्यावस्थाविशेषत्वात्प्रधानस्वरूपा एव भवन्ति ।
Thus, prakṛti and the rest, being specific states of pradhāna, are indeed identical in nature with pradhāna.
तच्च प्रधानं ब्रह्मचैतन्यस्य शक्तिः ।
And that pradhāna is the power of Brahman-consciousness.
यथा पुरुषगता सामर्थ्यरूपा शक्तिः पुरुषात्पृथक्तया नास्ति तथा ब्रह्मचैतन्यगता प्रधानरूपा शक्तिरपि ब्रह्मचैतन्याद्व्यतिरेकेण नास्ति ।
Just as the power in the form of capacity inhering in a person does not exist separately from the person, similarly the power in the form of pradhāna inhering in Brahman-consciousness also does not exist separately from Brahman-consciousness.
इत्थं ब्रह्मचैतन्ये सकलानात्मपदार्थानां लयश्चिन्तनीयः ।
In this manner, the dissolution of all non-Self entities into Brahman-consciousness is to be meditated upon.
ततः तादृशमद्वितीयं ब्रह्माहमेव इति चिन्तयेत् ।
Then one should meditate: 'I alone am such non-dual Brahman'.
यस्य हि मन्दबुद्धेर्बुद्धिमान्द्यादिरूपप्रतिबन्धैर्वेदान्तविचारे न प्रवृत्तिरुपजायते ।
For that dull-witted person in whom, on account of obstacles such as dullness of intellect, engagement in the inquiry of Vedānta does not arise,
कृते वा विचारे साक्षात्कारो न सम्पद्यते तस्येदं लयचिन्तनरूपं ध्यानमुक्तम् ।
or for whom, even when inquiry is carried out, direct realization does not occur, for him this meditation in the form of contemplation of dissolution has been prescribed.
293
ज्ञानं हि प्रमाणप्रमेययोरधीनम्, न तु विधेः पुरुषेच्छादेर्वाधीनम् ।
For knowledge is dependent upon the means of knowledge (pramāṇa) and the object of knowledge (prameya), not however dependent upon an injunction (vidhi) or the person's will and so on.
ध्यानं तु विधेः पुरुषेच्छाश्रद्धयोः हठात्कारस्य चाधीनम् ।
Meditation, on the other hand, is dependent upon an injunction, upon the person's will and faith, and upon forceful effort.
टिप्पणी
1.
ननु यदि ब्रह्मणः शक्तिर्ब्रह्मणो भिन्ना तदा अद्वैतश्रुतिविरोधः ।
[Objection:] If the power (śakti) of Brahman is distinct from Brahman, then there is a contradiction with the non-dual scriptures.
यद्यभिन्ना तदा तस्या ब्रह्मस्वरूपत्वादेव ब्रह्मणः शक्तिः इति पृथक्तया व्यवहारानुपपत्तिः ।
If it is non-different, then since it is identical with the nature of Brahman itself, the usage as separate in 'the power of Brahman' becomes untenable.
तस्माद्ब्रह्मणः शक्तेश्च भेदाभेदौ वाच्यौ ।
Therefore, both difference and non-difference between Brahman and the power must be admitted.
तथात्वे च तमःप्रकाशयोरिव विरुद्धस्वभावयोर्भेदाभेदयोः सामानाधिकरण्यानुपपत्तिरिति चेन्न ।
And if it is objected that in that case, just as in the case of darkness and light, there is the impossibility of co-existence of mutually contradictory difference and non-difference in the same locus, this is not so.
रज्वा सह सर्पस्येव ब्रह्मणा सह शक्तेः कल्पितभेदो वास्तवाभेदश्चेत्यनिर्वचनीयतादात्म्यसम्बन्धोऽभ्युपेयते ।
Because, just as between a snake and the rope, an indeterminable relation of identity (anirvacanīya-tādātmya-sambandha) consisting of superimposed difference and real non-difference is accepted between Brahman and the power (śakti).
ततश्च शक्तेः स्वाश्रयेण सह वास्तवभेदाभावात् केनापि प्रमाणेन तस्याः स्वाश्रयाद्भिन्नतया प्रतीत्यभावाच्च प्रलयकाले मायायाः सत्त्वेऽपि न तया ब्रह्मणः सद्वितीयत्वम् ।
And therefore, due to the absence of real difference of the power from its own substratum, and because there is no cognition by any means of knowledge of it as distinct from its substratum, even though māyā exists during cosmic dissolution, Brahman does not thereby become possessed of a second.
सृष्टिकालेऽपि मायाकार्यद्वैतप्रपञ्चे प्रतीयमानेऽपि न तेन प्रपञ्चेन ब्रह्मणः सद्वितीयत्वम् ।
Even during the time of creation, though the dual world which is an effect of māyā is perceived, Brahman does not become possessed of a second by that phenomenal world.
रज्जौ कल्पितसर्पादेर्यथा परमार्थतो रज्जुस्वरूपत्वमेव तथा ब्रह्मणि कल्पितप्रपञ्चस्यापि परमार्थतो ब्रह्मस्वरूपत्वेन तदतिरेकेण प्रपञ्चस्याभावात् ।
For, just as the snake superimposed on a rope is in absolute reality nothing but the rope itself, so too the universe superimposed on Brahman is in absolute reality identical in essence with Brahman, because the universe has no existence over and above it.
तस्माद्ब्रह्म सदाद्वितीयमेव ।
Therefore, Brahman is ever non-dual alone.
2.
अत्र आदिशब्देन वर्तमानः भूतह् भावी च इति त्रिविधः प्रतिबन्धः ग्राह्यः ।
Here, by the word 'ādi' (etcetera), the threefold obstacle—present, past, and future—is to be understood.
तत्र इष्टवस्तुषु अहम् मम इति दृढतर-वासना-रूपा विषय-आसक्तिः, पर-उक्त-अर्थ-ग्रहण-सामर्थ्य-अभाव-रूप-बुद्धि-मान्द्यम्, आचार्य-आदि-आप्त-उक्त-अर्थे विश्वास-अभावात् अन्यथा-कल्पन-रूपः कुतर्कः, देह-आदिषु आत्म-बुद्धि-रूपः विपर्यय-आख्य-दुराग्रहः इति एतत्-चतुष्टयम् वर्तमान-प्रतिबन्धः ।
Among them, the 'present obstacle' consists of these four: attachment to objects in the form of deep-seated impressions of 'I' and 'mine' towards desired objects; dullness of intellect in the form of inability to grasp meanings stated by others; fallacious logic in the form of perverse interpretation arising from lack of faith in the words of authoritative persons like the preceptor; and stubborn misconception termed *viparyaya* in the form of taking the body and the like to be the *ātman*.
धन-पुत्र-कलत्र-आदि-इष्ट-वस्तु-नाश-अनन्तरम् अपि तत्-अनुचिन्तनम् भूत-प्रतिबन्धः ।
Brooding over desired objects such as wealth, children, and spouse even after their loss is the 'past obstacle'.
ब्रह्मलोक-आदि-प्राप्ति-इच्छा भावि-जन्म-हेतु-भूत-प्रारब्ध-कर्म-शेषः वा भावि-प्रतिबन्धः ।
The desire to attain Brahmaloka etc., or the remnant of *prārabdha-karma* that causes a future birth, is the 'future obstacle'.
एतेषाम् ज्ञान-उत्पत्ति-प्रतिबन्धकानाम् निरूपणम् पञ्चदश्याम् ध्यानदीपे ३८-५३ श्लोकेषु द्रष्टव्यम् ।
The detailed exposition of these obstacles to the arising of knowledge is to be seen in the *Dhyānadīpa* chapter of the *Pañcadaśī*, verses 38–53.
तत्र प्रत्यक्ष-ज्ञाने प्रमाणम् चक्षुः-आदि-इन्द्रियम्, प्रमेयः घट-आदिः ।
There, in perceptual cognition, the means of knowledge (*pramāṇa*) is a sense organ like the eye, and the object of knowledge (*prameya*) is a pot or the like.
घट-चक्षुषोः सन्निकर्षे सति विना अपि पुरुषस्य इच्छा-आदिकम् घट-प्रत्यक्षम् भवति ।
When there is contact between the pot and the eye, perception of the pot occurs even without the desire etc. of the person.
चतुर्थ्याम् चन्द्रः न द्रष्टव्यः इति निषेधः अस्ति ।
There is a scriptural prohibition: 'The moon must not be looked at on the fourth lunar day (caturthī)'.
तथा सति अपि अस्मिन् दिने चन्द्रम् अहम् न पश्येयम् इति निश्चयवतः अपि पुरुषस्य अनिच्छतः एव येन केन अपि कारणेन चक्षुः-चन्द्रयोः प्रमाण-प्रमेययोः सन्निकर्षे सति चन्द्रस्य प्रत्यक्ष-ज्ञानम् जायते एव ।
Even so, when for whatever reason contact occurs between the eye and the moon—the *pramāṇa* and *prameya*—the perceptual knowledge of the moon arises invariably, even for a person who does not want to see it and has resolved: 'I will not look at the moon today'.
इत्थम् ज्ञानम् प्रमाण-प्रमेय-मात्र-अधीनम् ।
Thus, knowledge is dependent solely upon the means and the object of knowledge (*pramāṇa-prameya-mātrādhīna*).
न तु विधेः पुरुष-इच्छा-आदेः वा अधीनम् ।
It is not dependent upon an injunction or upon human desire and the like.
सालग्राम-शिला विष्णु-रूपा इति ध्यायतः उत्तमम् फलम् भवति ।
For one who meditates that 'the *śālagrāma* stone is the form of Viṣṇu', supreme fruit is attained.
तत्र पुरुषः शास्त्रेण विष्णुम् चतुर्भुजत्वेन शङ्ख-चक्र-गदा-पद्म-लक्ष्मी-सहितत्वेन च जानाति ।
There, through scripture, the person knows Viṣṇu as possessing four arms and being accompanied by the conch, discus, mace, lotus, and Lakṣmī.
चक्षुषा तु सालग्रामम् शिलात्वेन एव जानाति ।
With the eye, however, he knows the *śālagrāma* only as a stone.
तथापि शास्त्र-विधौ विश्वासेन ध्यान-फले इच्छया च सालग्रामः विष्णुः इति ध्यायति पुरुषः ।
Nevertheless, due to faith in the scriptural injunction and desire for the fruit of meditation, the person meditates: 'The *śālagrāma* is Viṣṇu'.
1.
ज्ञानं त्रिविधं - भ्रमज्ञानम्, स्मृतिज्ञानम्, प्रमाज्ञानं चेति ।
Knowledge is threefold: error-cognition, memory-cognition, and valid cognition.
तत्र भ्रान्तिज्ञानं केवलं कल्पितवस्त्वधीनम् ।
Among these, erroneous cognition depends solely on an imagined (superimposed) object.
स्मृतिज्ञानं स्वविषयसदृशवस्तुदर्शनेन वा तत्सम्बन्धिवस्तुदर्शनेन वोदिता या पूर्वानुभूतवस्तुविषयकमनोवृत्तिस्तदधीनम् ।
Memory-cognition is dependent on that mental mode concerning a previously experienced object, which is aroused either by the sight of an object similar to its content or by the sight of an object related to it.
प्रमाज्ञानं त्वन्तर्गतसुखादिविषयकज्ञानं न्यायमते वाचस्पतिमते च मनोरूपप्रमाणस्य सुखादिरूपप्रमेयस्य चाधीनम् ।
As for valid cognition, the knowledge regarding internal pleasure and so forth, in the Nyāya school and the view of Vācaspati Miśra, is dependent on the instrument of knowledge in the form of the mind and the object of knowledge in the form of pleasure etc.
सिद्धान्ते तु मनसः प्रमाणत्वानभ्युपगमेन सुखादिज्ञानं केवलप्रमेयाधीनम् ।
In the Advaita siddhānta, however, because the mind is not accepted as an independent pramāṇa, the knowledge of pleasure etc. is dependent solely on the object of knowledge (prameya).
बाह्यप्रमाज्ञानं तु इन्द्रियानुमानादिरूपप्रमाणस्य प्रमेयरूपवस्तुनश्च सम्बन्धाधीनम् ।
External valid cognition, however, depends upon the connection between the means of knowledge (such as sense-organs, inference, etc.) and the knowable object.
शब्दप्रमाणजन्यब्रह्मज्ञानरूपा शाब्दीप्रमा तु महावाक्यरूपशब्दप्रमाणस्य प्रत्यगभिन्नब्रह्मरूपप्रमेयस्य च यो लक्षणावृत्तिरूपपरम्परासम्बन्धस्तज्ज्ञानाधीना ।
The verbal valid cognition that is the knowledge of Brahman born of the verbal testimony, however, depends on knowing that mediate relation in the form of the indicative capacity (lakṣaṇā-vṛtti) between the verbal pramāṇa (the Mahāvākya) and the prameya (Brahman identical to the inner Self).
इतरलौकिकपदार्थविषयकशाब्दी प्रमा तु क्वचित् शक्तिवृत्तिरूपसम्बन्धज्ञानाधीना ।
Whereas verbal valid cognition concerning other worldly objects is in some cases dependent on the knowledge of the relation in the form of the primary expressive power (śakti-vṛtti).
क्वचिल्लक्षणावृत्तिरूपसम्बन्धज्ञानाधीना ।
And in other cases, it is dependent on knowledge of the relation in the form of the secondary indicative power (lakṣaṇā-vṛtti).
इत्थं च किञ्चिज्ज्ञानं ज्ञेयवस्तुमात्राधीनम् ।
Thus, some knowledge is dependent solely on the object to be known.
किञ्चिज्ज्ञानं प्रमाणप्रमेयसम्बन्धाधीनम् ।
Some knowledge is dependent on the contact/relation between the pramāṇa and the prameya.
अथवा तत्सम्बन्धज्ञानाधीनम् ।
Or it is dependent on the knowledge of that relation.
भ्रमप्रमासाधारण्येन ज्ञानस्य विषयो प्रमेय इत्युच्यते ।
In a broad sense encompassing both error and valid knowledge, the object of knowledge is called 'prameya'.
तत्र ज्ञेयत्वमप्यस्ति ।
The characteristic of being knowable (jñeyatva) is also present therein.
इत्थं सर्वमपि ज्ञानं वस्त्वधीनमेव ।
In this way, all knowledge is strictly object-dependent (vastu-tantra).
इदं वस्तु [ इह ज्ञानम् ] इति शब्देन ईश्वरसृष्टेन वा मनोमयेन वा (परोक्षज्ञानविषयेण वा) भ्रमसिद्धेन वा वस्तुना प्रमाणद्वारा साक्षाद्वा वृत्तेः सम्बन्धो गृह्यते ।
By the term 'this object' [here 'knowledge'], what is meant is the contact of the mental vṛtti, either through a pramāṇa or directly, with an object that is created by Īśvara, mind-made, an object of mediate knowledge, or established through error.
तस्माज्ज्ञानं न विध्याद्यधीनम् ।
Therefore, knowledge does not depend on an injunction (vidhi) or the like.
ध्यानरूपमुपासनं तु न वस्त्वधीनम् ।
Upāsanā, which is of the nature of meditation (dhyāna), however, is not dependent on the object.
किन्तु कर्त्रधीनम् ।
Rather, it is dependent on the agent (kartṛ-tantra).
यद्यपि ध्यानमपि मनोवृत्त्यात्मकमेव तथापि पुरुषस्येच्छाद्यधीनं तद्भवति ।
Although meditation is also in the form of a mental mode (mano-vṛtti), still it is dependent on the person's will (desire, effort, etc.).
न वस्त्वधीनम् ।
It is not dependent on the object.
तस्माद्ध्यानं मानसत्वेऽपि न ज्ञानम् ।
Therefore, meditation, despite being mental, is not knowledge.
किन्तु क्रियैव ।
Rather, it is an action alone.
ब्रह्मसाक्षात्काररूपज्ञाने प्रत्यगभिन्नं ब्रह्म प्रमेयं वेदान्तमहावाक्यं प्रमाणम् ।
In the knowledge that is direct realization of Brahman, Brahman identical with the inner Self is the object of knowledge (prameya), and the Vedānta Mahāvākya is the means of knowledge (pramāṇa).
गुरुमुखाद्वेदान्तश्रवणं कुर्वतो वेदान्तमहावाक्याद्ब्रह्मात्मसाक्षात्कारो जायते ।
For one undertaking the hearing (śravaṇa) of Vedānta from the Guru's mouth, direct realization of the Self as Brahman arises from the Vedānta Mahāvākya.
महावाक्यरूपप्रमाणमन्तरा केवलेच्छादिना नात्मसाक्षात्कारो भवति ।
Without the instrument of knowledge in the form of the Mahāvākya, direct realization of the Self cannot occur by mere desire or will.
उपासनं त्वैश्वर्यं विधिमपेक्षते ।
Upāsanā, on the other hand, depends on a scriptural injunction (vidhi).
शास्त्रविधिमनुसृत्य क्रियमाणमेवोपासनं फलाय कल्पते ।
Upāsanā leads to its fruit only when performed according to the injunction of the scripture.
विधिमन्तरा स्वेच्छया स्वसङ्कल्पानुसारेण यत्किञ्चिदर्थध्यानं नेष्टफलाय प्रभवति ।
Without an injunction, meditating on some arbitrary object by one's own whim and according to one's own imagination does not yield the desired result.
तदिदं ध्यानमनेकविधम् ।
This meditation is of manifold kinds.
सालग्रामशिलायां विष्णुबुद्धिकरणवदन्यस्मिन्नन्यबुद्धिकरणं प्रतीकध्यानम् ।
Symbolic meditation (pratīka-dhyāna) consists in imposing the thought of something onto another, like imposing the cognition of Viṣṇu upon a Śālagrāma stone.
वैकुण्ठवासिनो विष्णोश्चतुर्भुजत्वादिरूपेण ध्यानं तु नान्यस्मिन्नन्यबुद्धिकरणरूपं प्रतीकध्यानम् ।
Meditation on Viṣṇu residing in Vaikuṇṭha in His four-armed form, however, is not a symbolic meditation involving the imposition of one idea upon something else.
किन्तु तद्ध्यानं ध्येयवस्तुस्वरूपानुसारि ध्यानमेव ।
Rather, that meditation is indeed a meditation that conforms to the actual nature of the object to be meditated upon.
वैकुण्ठवासिनो विष्णोः स्वरूपं न प्रत्यक्षगोचरम्, किन्तु शास्त्रैकसमधिगम्यम् ।
The form of Viṣṇu residing in Vaikuṇṭha is not within the scope of direct perception, but is knowable solely through scripture.
शास्त्रे च विष्णोः स्वरूपं चतुर्भुजत्वेन शङ्खचक्राद्युपेतत्वेन च वर्णितम् ।
And in scripture, Viṣṇu's form is described as four-armed and endowed with conch, discus, etc.
अतस्तथा विष्णोर्ध्यानं ध्येयवस्तुस्वरूपानुसार्येव ।
Therefore, meditating on Viṣṇu in that manner faithfully accords with the true nature of the object of meditation.
विधिशास्त्रे विश्वासस्य, इच्छादेश्चाभावे ध्यानं न सिद्ध्यति ।
In the absence of faith in the injunctive scripture and of desire etc., meditation cannot be accomplished.
इदमुपासीत इत्येवंरूपं पुरुषस्य प्रवर्तकं वचनं विधिः ।
An injunction (vidhi) is a statement of the form 'One should meditate on this', which impels a person to act.
तद्वचने श्रद्धा विश्वासः ।
Faith (śraddhā) in that statement is conviction (viśvāsa).
अन्तःकरणस्य रजोगुणपरिणामरूपा कामात्मिका वृत्तिरिच्छा ।
Desire (icchā) is that longing mental mode which is a transformation of the rajoguṇa of the internal organ.
हठादपि ध्यानं सिद्ध्यति ।
Meditation can even be accomplished through forceful effort (haṭhāt).
ज्ञाने तु न तदपेक्षा ।
In knowledge, however, there is no need for such forceful effort.
नैरन्तर्येण ध्येयाकारचित्तवृत्तिप्रवाहो हि ध्यानम् ।
For meditation is an uninterrupted continuous flow of the mind's modifications taking the form of the object of meditation.
तत्र चित्तवृत्तेर्विक्षेपे सति हठात्तां स्थिरीकुर्यात् ।
There, when the mental modification gets distracted, one should forcefully stabilize it.
ज्ञानरूपान्तःकरणवृत्त्युदयकाल एव विषयावरणभङ्गस्य सिद्धत्वाद्वृत्तिस्थैर्यसम्पादनस्य नास्त्युपयोगः ।
Since the destruction of the veil obscuring the object is accomplished at the very moment of the dawn of the mental modification in the form of knowledge, there is no utility in cultivating the continuous stability of the mental modification.
तस्मान्न ज्ञाने हठापेक्षा ।
Therefore, in knowledge there is no requirement for forceful effort.
अहङ्ग्रहध्यानम्—वैकुण्ठवासिचतुर्भुजविष्णुध्यानवत् अहं ब्रह्म इति ध्यानमपि ध्येयस्वरूपानुसार्येव ध्यानम्, न तु प्रतीकध्यानम् ।
Ahaṅgraha-dhyāna: Like the meditation on the four-armed Viṣṇu residing in Vaikuṇṭha, the meditation 'I am Brahman' is also a meditation that conforms to the true nature of the meditated reality, and is not a symbolic meditation (pratīka-upāsanā).
किन्त्विदमहङ्ग्रहध्यानम् ।
Rather, this is ahaṅgraha-dhyāna (meditation on the non-difference of oneself and Brahman).
ध्येयस्वरूपस्य स्वाभिन्नतयानुसन्धानं अहङ्ग्रहध्यानं उच्यते ।
Contemplating the form of the meditated object as non-different from oneself is called ahaṅgraha-dhyāna.
यस्य वेदान्तविचारेऽप्यपरोक्षज्ञानं नोदेति, स वेदस्याज्ञारूपोपासनाविधिवाक्ये विश्वासवान् नैरन्तर्येण हठात् अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इत्यहङ्ग्रहध्यानमनुतिष्ठेत् ।
He for whom direct knowledge does not arise even through Vedāntic inquiry, should, placing faith in the Vedic injunction of upāsanā commanding it, diligently practice the ahaṅgraha-meditation 'I am Brahman' without interruption.
तस्य क्रमेण ज्ञानोत्पत्तिद्वारा मोक्षः सिद्ध्यति ।
For him, liberation is attained gradually through the eventual dawn of knowledge.
प्रणवोपासननिरूपणम्॥ २९४–३२६ ॥
294 · प्रणवे अहङ्ग्रहध्यानं
प्रकारान्तरेणाहङ्ग्रहध्यानम्1,2
Now the meditation identifying with the Self is explained in another way.
टिप्पणी
1.
यस्य बुद्धिः शास्त्रोक्ते परोक्षे ध्येये न सहसा स्थिरीभवति, स पुरुषप्रेरकेण शास्त्रविधिना बोधिते परोक्षध्येयप्रतिनिधिभूते प्रत्यक्षे सालग्रामादौ अन्यस्मिन् वा ध्येयविष्णुबुद्धिकरणरूपं अन्यबुद्धिकरणरूपं वा प्रतीकध्यानं कुर्यात् ।
One whose mind does not immediately become steady upon the imperceptible object of meditation taught in the scriptures should perform symbolic meditation (pratīkopāsanā)—which consists in superimposing the cognition of Viṣṇu or another deity upon a perceptible object such as a Śālagrāma stone, which serves as a representative instructed by the scriptural injunction that impels spiritual seekers.
अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति निर्गुणोपासनं तु अहङ्ग्रहध्यानं ध्येयस्वरूपानुसारित्वात् तस्य ।
However, meditation on the attributeless as 'I am Brahman' is termed ahaṅgraha-dhyāna (meditation of self-identification), because it directly accords with the real nature of the object of meditation.
2.
यद्यप्यत्र ध्यानविषयीभूतं ब्रह्म न परमार्थरूपम्, किन्तु मनःकल्पितमेव ।
Although here Brahman as the object of meditation is not its absolute transcendent nature, but rather conceived by the mind,
तस्मात् तद्विषयकचित्तवृत्तिप्रवाहरूपध्यानमपि भ्रान्तिज्ञानमेव, न यथार्थज्ञानम् ।
and therefore meditation in the form of a continuous stream of mental thoughts directed towards It is also merely an erroneous cognition, not direct veridical knowledge,
तथापि मणिप्रभायां मणिबुद्धिरूपसंवादिभ्रान्त्या धावतः पुंसो मणिज्ञानद्वारा मणिलाभवत् प्रकृताहङ्ग्रहध्यानेन ब्रह्मज्ञानलाभेन मोक्षः सिद्ध्यत्येव ।
nevertheless, just as a person who runs towards the lustre of a jewel mistaking it for the jewel itself (a fruitful error or saṁvādi-bhrama) gains the jewel via direct perception, similarly, through the present ahaṅgraha meditation, liberation is certainly achieved by attaining the direct knowledge of Brahman.
इदानीमुच्यते - प्रणवरूपे ओङ्कारे अहङ्ग्रहध्यानं माण्डूक्यादिश्रुत्यनुसारेण सुरेश्वराचार्यैः कथितम् ।
Now it is stated: Sureśvarācārya, in accordance with the Māṇḍūkya and other Upaniṣads, has expounded the ahaṅgraha-dhyāna on the syllable Om (Praṇava).
तदनुष्ठानमप्युचितं मोक्षकामस्य ।
Its practice is indeed suitable for a seeker of liberation.
तस्यैवं क्रमः - प्रणवरूपमक्षरं ब्रह्मस्वरूपमेव ।
Its method is as follows: the imperishable syllable Praṇava is verily the nature of Brahman.
तादृशप्रणवस्वरूपं ब्रह्म अहमेव इति नैरन्तर्येणानवरतं ध्यायेत् ।
One should meditate continuously and uninterruptedly: 'I myself am Brahman whose nature is Praṇava.'
नैतत्समं किञ्चिदपि ध्यानमस्ति ।
There is no meditation equal to this.
एतद्ध्यानस्य विशेषक्रमः सुरेश्वराचार्यैः पञ्चीकरणाख्ये ग्रन्थे प्रतिपादितः ।
The detailed procedure of this meditation has been expounded by Sureśvarācārya in the text named Pañcīkaraṇa.
एतदुपासकोऽपारं संसारं तरति ।
The practitioner of this meditation crosses over boundless saṁsāra.
अत्राधिकारी सन्न्यास्येव ।
Here, only a renunciant (saṁnyāsin) is the qualified aspirant.
295
निर्गुणप्रणवोपासनस्य सगुणप्रणवोपासनस्य च फलम् ।
The fruit of meditation on the nirguṇa-praṇava and saguṇa-praṇava.
प्रणवोपासनमनेकोपनिषत्सु वर्णितम् ।
Meditation on Praṇava is described in many Upaniṣads.
माण्डूक्योपनिषदि विशेषेण वर्णितम् ।
It is described especially in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad.
तदुपनिषद्व्याख्याने भाष्यकारैरानन्दगिर्याचार्यैश्च विस्पष्टं वर्णितञ्च ।
And it has been described with great clarity by the commentator (Śaṅkarācārya) and by Ānandagiri Ācārya in their commentaries on that Upaniṣad.
तत्र यः क्रमः स एव वार्तिककारैः पञ्चीकरणग्रन्थे प्रतिपादितः ।
The method that is found there has also been set forth by the Vārttikakāra in the Pañcīkaraṇa text.
तादृशप्रौढग्रन्थविचारासमर्थानामनायासेन बोधाय प्रणवोपासनक्रमोऽत्र निरूप्यते ।
For the effortless understanding of those who are incapable of studying such advanced texts, the method of Praṇava meditation is explained here.
उपनिषत्सु प्रणवोपासनं द्विधा वर्णितं - परब्रह्मरूपेण प्रणवस्योपासनम्, अपरब्रह्मरूपेण प्रणवस्योपासनं चेति ।
In the Upaniṣads, meditation on Praṇava is described in two ways: meditation on Praṇava as Para-Brahman (the supreme Brahman), and meditation on Praṇava as Apara-Brahman (the qualified Brahman).
निर्गुणं ब्रह्म परं ब्रह्म इत्युच्यते ।
The attributeless Brahman is called 'Para-Brahman'.
सगुणं ब्रह्म अपरं ब्रह्म इति कीर्त्यते ।
Brahman with attributes is designated as 'Apara-Brahman'.
परब्रह्मरूपेण प्रणवोपासको मोक्षमेव लभते ।
The one who meditates on Praṇava as Para-Brahman attains liberation alone.
अपरब्रह्मरूपेण प्रणवोपासकस्तु ब्रह्मलोकम् आप्नोति ।
However, the one who meditates on Praṇava as Apara-Brahman attains the world of Brahmā (Brahmaloka).
इत्थं निर्गुणसगुणभेदेन प्रणवोपासनं द्विविधम् ।
Thus, meditation on Praṇava is twofold through the division of nirguṇa and saguṇa.
निर्गुणप्रणवोपासनक्रमः॥ २९६–३१५ ॥
296 · सर्ववस्तूनामोङ्कारस्वरूपत्वं
निर्गुणप्रणवोपासनक्रम एवात्र निरूप्यते, न सगुणोपासनक्रमः ।
Here, only the method of meditation on the attributeless Praṇava (Oṅkāra) is expounded, not the method of meditation on the qualified form.
सगुणोपासनस्य फलमपि निर्गुणोपासनेऽन्तर्भवति ।
For the fruit of meditation on the qualified form is also subsumed within meditation on the attributeless.
तथा हि, निर्गुणोपासकस्यापि ब्रह्मलोकेच्छावत इच्छारूपप्रतिबन्धसत्त्वान्न ज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षलाभः ।
To explain: even in the case of a meditator on the attributeless who harbors a desire for Brahmaloka, the attainment of mokṣa does not occur directly through knowledge here, because of the presence of the obstacle in the form of desire.
किन्तु तस्य ब्रह्मलोकप्राप्तिर्भवति ।
Instead, he attains Brahmaloka.
स तत्र हिरण्यगर्भसमान् भोगाननुभूय तत्रैव ब्रह्मविचारेण ज्ञानोदयद्वारा मोक्षं लभते ।
There, having enjoyed pleasures equal to those of Hiraṇyagarbha, he attains mokṣa right there through inquiry into Brahman by means of the dawn of knowledge.
ब्रह्मलोकेच्छारहितस्य निर्गुणोपासकस्य त्विहैव लोके ज्ञानलाभान्मोक्षः सिद्ध्यति ।
However, for a meditator on the attributeless who is free from the desire for Brahmaloka, mokṣa is accomplished in this very world through the attainment of knowledge.
इत्थं सगुणोपासनफलस्य निर्गुणोपासनान्तर्भूतत्वादिह निर्गुणोपासनमेव निरूप्यते ।
Thus, because the fruit of meditation on the qualified form is subsumed under meditation on the attributeless, only meditation on the attributeless is expounded here.
कारणकार्यरूपं सर्वं वस्त्वोङ्कारस्वरूपमेव ।
Every entity appearing as cause and effect is indeed of the nature of Oṅkāra alone.
अतः सर्वोऽपि रूपप्रपञ्च ओङ्कार एव ।
Therefore, the entire manifold world of forms is Oṅkāra alone.
सर्वेष्वपि पदार्थेषु नाम रूपं चेत्यंशद्वयमस्ति ।
In all objects whatsoever, there exist two aspects: name and form.
तत्र1
Regarding that...
टिप्पणी
1.
माण्डूक्यशब्देन गौडपादकारिकापि ग्राह्या ।
By the word 'Māṇḍūkya', the Gauḍapāda Kārikā is also to be understood.
आदिशब्देन कठप्रश्नाद्युपनिषदो गृह्यन्ते ।
By the word 'ādi' ('etc.'), Upaniṣads such as the Kaṭha, Praśna, etc., are comprehended.
रूपात्मकोंऽशः तत्तन्नामात्मकांशान्नातिरिच्यते ।
The aspect consisting of form is not distinct from the aspect consisting of its respective name.
किन्तु नामस्वरूपमेव रूपांशोऽपि ।
Rather, even the aspect of form is only of the nature of name.
तथा हि, पदार्थानां रूपात्मको य आकारविशेषस्तदभिधायकनामपदैरेव सर्वे पदार्था निरूपतिआः सन्तो गृह्यन्ते त्यज्यन्ते वा ।
For, all objects, being determined only through the name-words that denote them, are either accepted or rejected according to the particularity of shape which constitutes their form.
तत्तदभिधानज्ञानमन्तरा केवलाकारमात्रेण व्यवहारो न सिद्ध्यति ।
Without the knowledge of the respective names, practical transaction cannot be accomplished merely by shape alone.
अतो नामैव सारभूतम् ।
Therefore, the name alone is essential.
आकारनाशेऽपि नामावशिष्यते ।
Even upon the destruction of the shape, the name persists.
यथा नष्टेऽपि घटे मृदवशिष्यते इति मृद्व्यतिरेकेण घटो नास्ति ।
Just as clay remains even when the pot is destroyed, showing that the pot has no existence apart from clay;
किन्तु मृत्स्वरूपमेव भवति ।
rather, it is nothing but of the nature of clay;
तथा आकारे नष्टेऽपि मृद्वदवशिष्यमाणनाम्नो न भिद्यते आकारः ।
similarly, even when the shape is destroyed, shape is not distinct from the name that remains like clay.
किन्तु नामस्वरूपमेव भवत्याकारोऽपि ।
Rather, even the shape is only of the nature of the name.
अथवा घटशरावोदञ्चनादिषु मृदनुगता भवति ।
Alternatively: in pot, shallow bowl, pail, etc., clay is constant.
घटशरावोदञ्चनादयः परस्परं व्यभिचरन्ति ।
Pot, shallow bowl, pail, etc., vary from one another.
तस्माद्घटशरावादयो मिथ्या ।
Therefore, pot, shallow bowl, etc., are false.
तेष्वनुगता मृत्सत्या ।
The clay that persists in them is real.
एवं घटस्याकारा नाना ।
In the same way, the shapes of pots are manifold.
तेषामभिधायकं घटः इति नामैकमेव ।
The name denoting them—'pot'—is only one.
एकस्य घटस्याकारो न घटान्तरेऽस्ति ।
The shape of one pot is not present in another pot.
तस्मादाकारा व्यभिचारिणः ।
Therefore, shapes are variable.
सर्वेष्वपि घटाकारेषु एकमेव नामानुगतं वर्तते ।
In all pot-shapes, the one single name persists throughout.
तस्मान्मिथ्याभूत आकारः सत्यभूतान्नाम्नो नातिरिच्यते ।
Therefore, shape, being false, is not distinct from the name, which is real.
इत्थमेव सर्वपदार्थानामाकारोऽपि तत्तन्नाम्नो न व्यतिरिक्तः ।
In this very way, the shape of all objects also is not distinct from their respective name.
तस्मान्नामस्वरूप एवाकारः ।
Therefore, shape is only of the nature of name.
सर्वोऽयं नामप्रपञ्च ओङ्कारव्यतिरेकेण नास्ति ।
This entire world of names has no existence apart from *Oṃkāra*.
किन्तु ओङ्कारस्वरूपमेव सर्वं नाम ।
Rather, all names are purely of the nature of *Oṃkāra*.
तथा हि, वाचकशब्द एव नाम इति कथ्यते ।
For, an expressive word alone is called a 'name'.
लोके वेदे च प्रयुक्तः सर्वः शब्द ओङ्कारादेवोत्पन्न इति श्रुतिषूच्यते ।
It is stated in the *Śruti*s that all speech used in the world and in the Veda is born from *Oṃkāra* alone:
तद्यथा शङ्कुना सर्वाणि पर्णानि सन्तृण्णानि एवमोङ्कारेण सर्वा वाक् सन्तृण्णा ओङ्कार एवेदं सर्वम् इति ।
'Just as all leaves are held together by a rib, so all speech is held together by *Oṃkāra*', and '*Oṃkāra* alone is all this.'
कार्यं सर्वं कारणस्वरूपमेव भवति ।
Every effect is non-different from its cause in nature.
तस्मादोङ्कारकार्यभूतानि वाचकशब्दात्मकानि नामानि ओङ्कारस्वरूपाणि ।
Therefore, all names consisting of expressive words, being the effects of *Oṃkāra*, are of the nature of *Oṃkāra*.
इत्थं रूपांशो यः पदार्थाकारः स नामस्वरूपः ।
Thus, that form-aspect which is the shape of an object is of the nature of name.
नाम च सर्वमोङ्कारस्वरूपम् ।
And every name is of the nature of *Oṃkāra*.
तस्मात्सर्वस्वरूप ओङ्कारः ।
Therefore, *Oṃkāra* is the true essence of everything.
297
ओङ्कारस्य ब्रह्माभेदेन चिन्तनम् ।
Contemplation of the syllable Om as non-different from Brahman.
यथा सर्वस्वरूप ओङ्कारः ।
Just as the syllable Om is of the nature of everything,
तथा सर्वस्वरूपं ब्रह्म ।
so also Brahman is of the nature of everything.
तस्मात् ओङ्कारो ब्रह्मरूपः ।
Therefore, the syllable Om is the very form of Brahman.
अथवा ओङ्कारो ब्रह्मणो वाचकः ।
Alternatively, the syllable Om is the signifier (vācaka) of Brahman,
ब्रह्म ओङ्कारस्य वाच्यम् ।1
and Brahman is the signified (vācya) of the syllable Om.
टिप्पणी
1.
यथा पुण्याधिक्यान्मनुष्यापेक्षयाधिककालस्थायी देवः अमरः इत्युपचारेणोच्यते तथैव घटादिपदार्थानामाकारापेक्षया घटादिनाम्नामधिककालस्थायित्वात् नाम्नां सत्यत्वमुपचारादुच्यते ।
Just as a deva, who endures for a longer duration compared to human beings due to an abundance of merit, is called 'immortal' by figurative usage, even so the reality of names such as 'pot' is spoken of figuratively because they outlast the transient physical shapes of pots and other objects.
वाच्यवाचकयोरभेदोऽस्ति ।
There is non-difference between the signified and the signifier.
तस्मादप्योङ्कारो ब्रह्मरूपः ।
From this consideration also, the syllable Om is of the nature of Brahman.
किञ्च विचार्यमाणे यदक्षरं ब्रह्मण्यध्यस्तं तस्य ब्रह्माधिष्ठानं भवति ।
Furthermore, when inquired into, the syllable that is superimposed upon Brahman has Brahman as its substratum.
अध्यस्तस्य स्वरूपमधिष्ठानान्नातिरिच्यते ।
The true nature of the superimposed is not distinct from its substratum.
तस्मादप्योङ्कारो ब्रह्मैव ।
Therefore also, the syllable Om is Brahman alone.
तस्मादोङ्कारं ब्रह्मरूपेण चिन्तयेत् ।
Therefore, one should contemplate the syllable Om as identical with Brahman.
ब्रह्मस्वरूपस्योङ्कारस्यात्मनश्चाभेदः॥ २९८–३०५ ॥
298 · आत्मनो ब्रह्मणश्च पादचतुष्टयादिनिरूपणम्
ब्रह्मरूपम् ओङ्कारम् आत्मनः अभिन्नतया चिन्तयेत् ।
One should meditate upon the sacred syllable Om, which is the nature of Brahman, as non-different from one's own Self (*ātman*).
तथा हि, आत्मनः ब्रह्मणा सह मुख्यः अभेदः अस्ति ।
For indeed, there is an absolute non-difference of the *ātman* with Brahman.
ब्रह्मणः इव आत्मनः चत्वारः पादाः सन्ति ।
Just as in the case of Brahman, there are four quarters (*pādas*) of the *ātman*.
पादः नाम भागः अंशः वा ।
A *pāda* means a part or a portion.
विराट्, हिरण्यगर्भः, ईश्वरः, तत्पदलक्ष्यार्थभूतेश्वरसाक्षी च इति ब्रह्मणः चत्वारः पादाः ।
Virāṭ, Hiraṇyagarbha, Īśvara, and the witness of Īśvara (which is the implied meaning of the word *tat*) are the four quarters of Brahman.
विश्वः, तैजसः, प्राज्ञः, त्वम्पदलक्ष्यजीवसाक्षी च इति चत्वारः आत्मनः पादाः ।
Viśva, Taijasa, Prājña, and the witness of the *jīva* (which is the implied meaning of the word *tvam*) are the four quarters of the *ātman*.
जीवसाक्षिणः एव तुरीयः इति व्यपदेशः ।
The witness of the *jīva* alone is designated as the *turīya* (the Fourth).
समष्टिस्थूलप्रपञ्चसहितचेतनस्य विराड् इति नाम ।
The name 'Virāṭ' belongs to Consciousness associated with the aggregate gross universe.
व्यष्टिस्थूलाभिमानिनः विश्वः इति नाम ।
The name 'Viśva' belongs to the one who identifies with the individual gross body.
विराजः विश्वस्य च स्थूलोपाधिकत्वात् विश्वः विराड्रूपः एव न ततः अन्यः ।
Because both Virāṭ and Viśva have the gross realm as their limiting adjunct (*upādhi*), Viśva is indeed of the nature of Virāṭ and not different from him.
विराड्रूपस्य विश्वस्य सप्त अङ्गानि सन्ति ।
Of Viśva, who is identical with Virāṭ, there are seven limbs.
द्यौः = स्वर्गलोकः शिरः ।
Heaven (= the heavenly realm) is the head.
सूर्यः चक्षुः ।
The sun is the eye.
वायुः प्राणः ।
Air is the vital breath.
आकाशः उरः ।
Space is the chest.
समुद्रादिरूपं जलं मूत्रस्थानं (बस्तिः) ।
Water in the form of oceans and so on is the urinary bladder (*basti*).
पृथिवी पादौ ।
The earth is the two feet.
आहवनीयः = होमाधिकरणः अग्निः मुखम् ।
The *āhavanīya* fire (= the sacrificial fire) is the mouth.
इति एतानि सप्त विश्वस्य अङ्गानि ।
These are the seven limbs of Viśva.
द्युलोकादीनि यद्यपि न विश्वस्य अङ्गानि तथापि विराजः अङ्गानि भवन्ति ।
Even though heaven and the rest are not strictly limbs of the individual Viśva, they are limbs of Virāṭ.
तस्य विराजः विश्वेन अभेदः अस्ति ।
And that Virāṭ is non-different from Viśva.
तस्मात् माण्डूक्योपनिषदि विश्वाङ्गत्वेन तानि उक्तानि ।
Therefore, in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad, they are spoken of as the limbs of Viśva.
एवम् एव विराडात्मकविश्वस्य एकोनविंशतिमुखानि सन्ति ।
Likewise, Viśva, identical in essence with Virāṭ, has nineteen mouths (instruments of cognition/experience).
प्राणाः पञ्च, कर्मेन्द्रियाणि पञ्च, ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि पञ्च, अन्तःकरणचतुष्टयम् इति एतानि मुखानि ।1,2,3,4,5
The five vital breaths, the five organs of action, the five organs of sense-perception, and the fourfold internal organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*) — these are the nineteen mouths.
टिप्पणी
1.
सकलप्राणिशरीरेषु अहम् इति अभिमानकरणात् ईश्वरः वैश्वानरः इति कथ्यते ।
Because He identifies as 'I' in the bodies of all living beings, Īśvara is called Vaiśvānara.
विविधं राजते = अनेकधा प्रकाशते इति सः एव वैश्वानरः विराट् इति अभिधीयते ।
Because 'He shines diversely' (= He shines in manifold ways), that very Vaiśvānara is called 'Virāṭ'.
2.
सकलजीवानां कर्मानुसारेण फलदानात् ईश्वरः इति नाम ।
The name 'Īśvara' is applied because He dispenses the fruits in accordance with the *karma* of all *jīvas*.
3.
सूक्ष्मदेहाभिमानापरित्यागेन एव स्थूलदेहे अहम् इति अभिमानवान् जाग्रदभिमानी जीवः विश्वः इति उच्यते ।
The *jīva* who identifies with the waking state, possessing the sense of 'I' in the gross body without abandoning identification with the subtle body, is called 'Viśva'.
4.
तेजश्शब्दवाच्यान्तःकरणसहितः प्राणेन्द्रियाध्यक्षः स्वप्नाभिमानी जीवः तैजसः इति अभिधीयते ।
The *jīva* who identifies with the dream state, presiding over the vital breaths and faculties, associated with the *antaḥkaraṇa* denoted by the word 'tejas' (light), is designated as 'Taijasa'.
5.
प्राज्ञः = प्र + अज्ञः ।
Prājña = *pra* + *ajña* (completely ignorant).
सुषुप्तिकाले स्वप्रकाशात्मानन्देन सह अज्ञानवृत्तेः सत्त्वात् सुषुप्त्यभिमानी जीवः प्राज्ञः इति कीर्त्यते ।
Because during deep sleep the modification of ignorance (*avidyā-vṛtti*) exists along with the bliss of the self-luminous *ātman*, the *jīva* identifying with deep sleep is proclaimed as 'Prājña'.
भोगस्य साधनभूतत्वात् मुखानि इति उच्यन्ते ।
They are called 'mouths' because they serve as the instruments for experiencing objects.
जाग्रदवस्थायाम् एतैः एकोनविंशतिमुखैः स्थूलशब्दादयः बाह्यवृत्त्या अनुभूयन्ते ।
In the waking state, gross objects such as sounds are experienced through external mental modifications (*bāhya-vṛttis*) by means of these nineteen mouths.
तस्मात् विराड्रूपः विश्वः स्थूलभुक् इति, बाह्यवृत्तिः इति, जाग्रदवस्थः इति च कथ्यते ।
Therefore, Viśva, who is of the nature of Virāṭ, is called 'the experiencer of the gross' (*sthūlabhuk*), 'externally cognitive' (*bāhyavṛtti*), and 'abiding in the waking state' (*jāgradavastha*).
299 · चतुर्दशत्रिपुट्यः
भोगसाधनेषु प्राणादिष्वेकोनविंशतिमुखेषु श्रोत्रादिदशेन्द्रियाणि अन्तःकरणचतुष्टयं चेति चतुर्दशमुखानि स्वस्वविषयाणां साहाय्यं स्वस्वदेवतानां च साहाय्यमपेक्षन्ते ।
Among the nineteen mouths which are instruments of experience, the fourteen mouths—namely, the ten senses beginning with hearing and the fourfold internal organ—require the aid of their respective objects and the aid of their respective presiding deities.
देवताविषययोः साहाय्यमन्तरा केवलैरेतैश्चतुर्दशमुखैर्भोगो न सम्भवति ।
Without the assistance of the deity and the object, experience is not possible by these fourteen mouths alone.
तस्मात्पञ्च प्राणाश्चतुर्दश त्रिपुट्यश्च विराड्रूपविश्वस्य मुखानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
Therefore, the five prāṇas and the fourteen triads are said to be the mouths of Viśva in the cosmic form of Virāj.
मुखम्, देवता, विषयश्चेति त्रयाणां समूहस्य त्रिपुटी इति नाम ।
The collection of these three—mouth (organ), deity, and object—is named 'triad' (tripuṭī).
सा च त्रिपुटी एवं वर्ण्यते -
And that triad is described as follows:
(१) श्रोत्रेन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, तद्विषयः शब्दोऽधिभूतम्, दिगभिमानिनी देवता अधिदैवम् ।
(1) The sense-organ of hearing is the adhyātma; its object, sound, is the adhibhūta; the deity presiding over the directions is the adhidaiva.
अत्र क्रियाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिभ्यां युक्तानीन्द्रियाणि अन्तःकरणं चाध्यात्मं इत्युच्यते ।
Here, the sense-organs and the internal organ, endowed with the powers of action and knowledge, are termed *adhyātma*.
तेषां विषयोऽधिभूतं इति कीर्त्यते ।
Their object is designated as *adhibhūta*.
तेषां सहायभूता देवता अधिदैवं इत्यभिधीयते ।
The presiding deity that assists them is named *adhidaiva*.
(२) त्वगिन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, तद्विषयः स्पर्शोऽधिभूतम्, वाय्वभिमानिनी देवता अधिदैवम् ।
(2) The organ of touch (skin) is the adhyātma; its object, touch, is the adhibhūta; the deity presiding over air is the adhidaiva.
(३) नेत्रेन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, रूपमधिभूतम्, सूर्योऽधिदैवम् ।
(3) The organ of sight (eye) is the adhyātma; form/color is the adhibhūta; the Sun is the adhidaiva.
(४) रसनेन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, रसोऽधिभूतम्, वरुणोऽधिदैवम् ।
(4) The organ of taste (tongue) is the adhyātma; taste is the adhibhūta; Varuṇa is the adhidaiva.
(५) घ्राणेन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, गन्धोऽधिभूतम्, अश्विनीकुमारौ अधिदैवम् ।
(5) The organ of smell (nose) is the adhyātma; smell is the adhibhūta; the two Aśvins are the adhidaiva.
अथवा पृथिव्यभिमानिनी देवता अधिदैवम् ।
Alternatively, the deity presiding over the earth is the adhidaiva.
(६) वागिन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, वक्तव्यं अधिभूतम्, अग्निदेवता अधिदैवम् ।
(6) The organ of speech is the adhyātma; the spoken word is the adhibhūta; the deity Agni is the adhidaiva.
(७) पाणीन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, पदार्थग्रहणमधिभूतम्, इन्द्रोऽधिदैवम् ।
(7) The organ of hands is the adhyātma; grasping objects is the adhibhūta; Indra is the adhidaiva.
(८) पादेन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, गमनमधिभूतम्, विष्णुरधिदैवम् ।
(8) The organ of feet is the adhyātma; walking is the adhibhūta; Viṣṇu is the adhidaiva.
(९) पायुरध्यात्मम्, मलविसर्जनमधिभूतम्, यमोऽधिदैवम् ।
(9) The organ of excretion is the adhyātma; excretion of waste is the adhibhūta; Yama is the adhidaiva.
(१०) उपस्थेन्द्रियमध्यात्मम्, ग्राम्यसुखोत्पत्तिः (मैथुनसुखोत्पत्तिः) अधिभूतम्, प्रजापतिरधिदैवम् ।
(10) The generative organ is the adhyātma; the generation of carnal pleasure (generation of copulatory pleasure) is the adhibhūta; Prajāpati is the adhidaiva.
(११) मनोऽध्यात्मम्, मन्तव्यं (सङ्कल्पः) अधिभूतम्, चन्द्रोऽधिदैवम् ।
(11) The mind is the adhyātma; the object of thought (volition) is the adhibhūta; the Moon is the adhidaiva.
(१२) बुद्धिरध्यात्मम्, बोद्धव्यं (निश्चयः) अधिभूतम्, बृहस्पतिरधिदैवम् ।
(12) The intellect is the adhyātma; the ascertainable object (ascertainment) is the adhibhūta; Bṛhaspati is the adhidaiva.
(१३) अहङ्कारोऽध्यात्मम्, अहङ्कर्तव्यमधिभूतम्, रुद्रोऽधिदैवम् ।
(13) The ego (ahaṅkāra) is the adhyātma; what is to be identified with is the adhibhūta; Rudra is the adhidaiva.
(१४) चित्तमध्यात्मम्, चिन्तनीयम1,2
(14) The citta is the adhyātma; that which is to be contemplated...
टिप्पणी
1.
सूर्याश्वस्य घ्राणाभ्यामश्विनीकुमारयोरुत्पत्तिवर्णनात् घ्राणदेवते अश्विनीकुमाराविति केचनाहुः ।
Some say that the presiding deities of the sense of smell are the Aśvinīkumāras, because their origin is described as springing from the nostrils of Sūrya's horse (mare).
पृथिव्या घ्राणस्योत्पन्नत्वात्पृथिव्यभिमानिनी देवता घ्राणदेवतेति वार्तिककारा आहुः ।
The Vārtikakāra says that because the sense of smell is produced from the earth element, the deity presiding over the earth is the deity of the olfactory sense.
2.
वचनक्रियाया विषयभूतः पदार्थो वक्तव्यमित्युच्यते ।
The object that serves as the content of the act of speaking is called 'vaktavya' (the speakable).
स वचनक्रियाद्वारा वागिन्द्रियस्याधिभूतम् ।
That, via the action of speaking, is the adhibhūta of the organ of speech.
एवमेव सर्वेन्द्रियाणां स्वस्वक्रियाद्वारा विषयभूतः पदार्थः अधिभूतमिति ज्ञेयम् ।
In the very same manner, the entity that becomes the object through each respective organ's action should be understood as the adhibhūta for all the sense-organs.
क्वचित्तु स्थूलदृष्ट्या वचनादिक्रियैवाधिभूतमित्युच्यते ।
However, in some places, from an approximate viewpoint, the very activity such as speaking is itself referred to as the adhibhūta.
धिभूतम्, क्षेत्रज्ञः साक्षी अधिदैवम् ।
...[a]dhibhūta; the Kṣetrajña (Witness) is the adhidaiva.
एताश्चतुर्दश त्रिपुट्यः पञ्च प्राणाश्च मिलित्वैतानि विराड्रूपस्य विश्वस्यैकोनविंशतिमुखानि ।
These fourteen triads and the five prāṇas together constitute the nineteen mouths of the Viśva in the form of Virāj.
300
विश्वः विराट् अकारमात्रा इत्येतेषामभेदचिन्तनम् ।
Contemplation of the non-difference of Viśva, Virāṭ, and the syllable 'A'.
विराजो विश्वस्य च यथाभेदस्तथा ओङ्कारप्रथममात्राया अकारस्य विराड्रूपविश्वेन सहाभेदोऽस्ति ।
Just as there is non-difference between Virāṭ and Viśva, so too there is non-difference of 'A', the first mora of Oṃkāra, with Viśva in the form of Virāṭ.
तथा हि, ब्रह्मणश्चतुर्षु पादेषु प्रथमः पादो विराट् ।
For instance, among the four quarters of Brahman, the first quarter is Virāṭ.
आत्मनश्चतुर्षु पादेषु प्रथमः पादो विश्वः ।
Among the four quarters of the Self (jīva), the first quarter is Viśva.
ओङ्कारस्य मात्रात्मकेषु चतुर्षु पादेषु प्रथमः पादोऽकारः ।
Among the four quarters consisting of morae of Oṃkāra, the first quarter is the letter 'A'.
त्रयाणामेषामादित्वरूपधर्मसामान्यसत्त्वात् विश्वविराडकाराणामभेदं चिन्तयेत् ।
Due to the presence of the common property of being the first among all three, one should meditate upon the non-difference of Viśva, Virāṭ, and the syllable 'A'.
इत्थं विश्वस्य सप्ताङ्गान्येकोनविंशतिमुखानि च व्याख्यातानि ।
Thus the seven limbs and nineteen mouths of Viśva have been explained.
301 · विश्वतैजसयोर्भेदः
विश्वस्योक्तानि सप्ताङ्गान्येकोनविंशतिमुखानि च तैजसस्यापि सन्तीत्यवगन्तव्यम् ।
It should be understood that the seven limbs and nineteen mouths described for Viśva belong to Taijasa as well.
किन्तु इयानस्ति भेदः — विश्वस्याङ्गानि मुखानि चेश्वरसृष्टानि ।
However, this much is the difference: the limbs and mouths of Viśva are created by Īśvara.
तैजसस्य त्विन्द्रियदेवताविषयरूपत्रिपुट्यः शिराद्यङ्गानि च मनोमयानि ।
Whereas for Taijasa, the triads of senses, presiding deities, and objects, as well as limbs such as the head, are made purely of the mind.
तैजसस्य भोगः सूक्ष्मः ।
The experience (bhoga) of Taijasa is subtle.
भोगो नाम सुखदुःखाद्यनुभवः ।
Experience (bhoga) indeed means the perception of pleasure, pain, and the like.
यद्यप्यनुभवरूपे ज्ञाने स्थूलत्वसूक्ष्मत्वभेदो न सम्भवति ।
Even though in knowledge as pure experience the distinction of grossness and subtlety is not possible,
तथापि बाह्यशब्दादिविषयसम्बन्धात्साक्षाज्जायमानसुखदुःखादिसाक्षात्कारः स्थूल इत्युच्यते ।
nevertheless, the direct perception of pleasure, pain, etc., arising from contact with external objects such as sound, is called 'gross'.
मानसशब्दादिसम्बन्धाज्जायमानसुखदुःखादिसाक्षात्कारः सूक्ष्म इत्युच्यते ।
And the direct perception of pleasure, pain, etc., arising from contact with purely mental sounds and the like, is called 'subtle'.
तथा च श्रुतिः — स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः (मा. आ. ३) प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसः (मा. आ. ४) इति ।
And so says the śruti: 'Vaiśvānara is the experiencer of the gross' (Mā. Ā. 3), 'Taijasa is the experiencer of the subtle' (Mā. Ā. 4).
विश्वो हि स्थूलभुङ्नित्यं तैजसः प्रविविक्तभुक् (मा. आ. ५) इति च ।
And also: 'Viśva is always the experiencer of the gross, and Taijasa is the experiencer of the subtle' (Mā. Ā. 5).
तैजसस्य भोगयोग्याः शब्दादयो मानसत्वात्सूक्ष्माः ।
The objects such as sound fit for the experience of Taijasa are subtle because they are purely mental.
तदपेक्षया विश्वस्य भोगयोग्याः शब्दादयो बाह्यत्वात्स्थूलाः ।
In comparison to that, the objects such as sound fit for the experience of Viśva are gross because they are external.
किञ्च विश्वो बहिष्प्रज्ञः ।
Furthermore, Viśva is outwardly conscious (bahiṣprajña).
तैजसस्त्वन्तःप्रज्ञः ।
Taijasa, on the other hand, is inwardly conscious (antaḥprajña).
यतो विश्वस्यान्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपा प्रज्ञा बहिर्गच्छति ।
Because the cognition in the form of mental modification of Viśva goes outwards.
तैजसस्य प्रज्ञा न बहिर्गच्छति ।
The cognition of Taijasa does not go outwards.
तस्मात्तौ क्रमेण बहिष्प्रज्ञत्वेनान्तःप्रज्ञत्वेन च व्यपदिश्येते ।
Therefore, they are designated as outwardly conscious and inwardly conscious, respectively.
302
तैजसः हिरण्यगर्भः उकारः इत्येतेषामभेदचिन्तनम् ।
Contemplation of the non-difference of Taijasa, Hiraṇyagarbha, and the syllable 'U'.
यथा विश्वविराजोरभेदस्तथा तैजसहिरण्यगर्भयोरभेदो ज्ञेयः ।
Just as there is non-difference between Viśva and Virāṭ, so should the non-difference between Taijasa and Hiraṇyagarbha be understood.
तैजसस्योपाधिः सूक्ष्मः ।
The upādhi of Taijasa is subtle.
हिरण्यगर्भस्योपाधिरपि सूक्ष्मः ।
The upādhi of Hiraṇyagarbha is also subtle.
तस्मात्1तयोरैक्यं
Therefore, their unity...
टिप्पणी
1.
साक्षिचैतन्यं चित्तस्याश्रयत्वात्तस्यानुग्रहं करोति ।
Being the substratum of the citta, the witness-consciousness (sākṣin) favors (illumines) it.
तस्मात्साक्षिचैतन्यं चित्तस्याधिदैवमित्युच्यते ।
Therefore, the witness consciousness is said to be the presiding deity of the mind (citta).
अत एव केचनाचार्याश्चिन्तनरूपं स्मृतिज्ञानं साक्ष्याश्रितमाहुः ।
For this very reason, some teachers say that memory knowledge, which has the form of contemplation, is directly supported by the witness (sākṣin).
क्वचिच्चित्तस्याधिदैवं नारायणः (वासुदेवः) इत्युक्तम् ।
In some places, the presiding deity of citta is mentioned as Nārāyaṇa (Vāsudeva).
बोध्यम् ।
[...is to be understood.]
तैजसहिरण्यगर्भयोरेकत्वं निश्चित्य ओङ्कारस्य द्वितीयमात्रया उकारेण सह तयोरभेदं चिन्तयेत् ।
Having determined the oneness of Taijasa and Hiraṇyagarbha, one should meditate upon their non-difference with the second mora of Oṃkāra, the letter 'U'.
आत्मनश्चतुर्षु पादेषु द्वितीयः पादस्तैजसः ।
Among the four quarters of the Self (jīva), the second quarter is Taijasa.
ब्रह्मणो द्वितीयः पादो हिरण्यगर्भः ।
The second quarter of Brahman is Hiraṇyagarbha.
ओङ्कारमात्रासु द्वितीया मात्रा उकारः ।
Among the morae of Oṃkāra, the second mora is the letter 'U'.
द्वितीयत्वं त्रयाणामेषां समानधर्मः ।
Being second is the common property of these three.
तस्मात्त्रयाणामैक्यं चिन्तयेत् ।
Therefore, one should meditate upon the oneness of these three.
303 · प्राज्ञः, ईश्वरः, मकारः, इत्येतेषामभेदचिन्तनम्
प्राज्ञमीश्वररूपं जानीयात् ।
One should know *Prājña* as identical in nature to *Īśvara*.
प्राज्ञस्य कारणशरीरमुपाधिः ।
The causal body is the *upādhi* of *Prājña*.
ईश्वरस्यापि कारणमेवोपाधिः ।
The causal principle alone is the *upādhi* of *Īśvara* as well.
ईश्वरः प्राज्ञश्च पादेषु तृतीयौ ।
Both *Īśvara* and *Prājña* are the third among the quarters (*pādas*).
ओङ्कारस्य तृतीया मात्रा मकारः ।
The third *mātrā* of the syllable *Om* is the letter 'm' (*makāra*).
त्रिष्वेतेषु तृतीयत्वस्य समानधर्मत्वात्तेषामैक्यं चिन्तयेत् ।
Because being the third is a common attribute among these three, one should meditate upon their identity.
सोऽयं प्राज्ञः प्रज्ञानघनः भवति ।
This *Prājña* is a 'mass of consciousness' (*prajñānaghana*).
यस्मात् जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोर्यावन्ति ज्ञानानि स्थितानि तानि सर्वाणि सुषुप्तौ घनीभवन्ति, अविद्यामात्ररूपतां भजन्तीति यावत् ।
Because whatever cognitions existed in waking and dream all become condensed in deep sleep, that is to say, they assume the form of mere *avidyā*.
तस्मात्प्राज्ञः प्रज्ञानघनः इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore *Prājña* is called 'a mass of consciousness' (*prajñānaghana*).
अयं प्राज्ञः आनन्दभुक् इति श्रूयते ।
This *Prājña* is heard in the scriptures as 'the experiencer of bliss' (*ānandabhuk*).
आनन्दभुक् प्राज्ञः (मा. आ. ५) यतोऽयं प्राज्ञोऽविद्यावृतमानन्दं भुङ्क्ते ततः आनन्दभुक् इति व्यपदिश्यते ।
*Prājña* is the experiencer of bliss (मा. आ. ५); since this *Prājña* experiences bliss veiled by *avidyā*, he is designated as 'the experiencer of bliss' (*ānandabhuk*).
विश्वतैजसयोरिव प्राज्ञस्यापि भोगे त्रिपुटी वर्ण्यते - चैतन्यप्रतिबिम्बसहिताविद्यावृत्तिरध्यात्मम्, अज्ञानावृतस्वरूपानन्दोऽधिभूतम्, ईश्वरोऽधिदैवमिति ।
Just as with *Viśva* and *Taijasa*, a triad (*tripuṭī*) is described in the experience of *Prājña* as well: the *avidyā-vṛtti* endowed with the reflection of consciousness is the *adhyātma*, the essential bliss veiled by ignorance is the *adhibhūta*, and *Īśvara* is the *adhidaiva*.
इत्थं विश्वो बहिष्प्रज्ञः ।
Thus *Viśva* is conscious of the external world (*bahiṣprajña*).
तैजसोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः ।
*Taijasa* is conscious of internal objects (*antaḥprajña*).
प्राज्ञः प्रज्ञानघनश्च भवति ।
And *Prājña* is a mass of consciousness (*prajñānaghana*).
304 · विश्वादीनां त्रयाणामेकत्वम्, तुरीयस्येश्वरसाक्षिणाभेदं च चिन्तयेत्
इत्थं विश्वादीनां त्रयाणां मिथो भेद उपाधिप्रयुक्त एव ।
Thus, the mutual distinction among the three beginning with *Viśva* is solely caused by limiting adjuncts (*upādhis*).
विश्वस्य स्थूलं सूक्ष्ममज्ञानं चेति त्रयमप्युपाधिः, तैजसस्य सूक्ष्ममज्ञानं चेति द्वयमुपाधिः, प्राज्ञस्याज्ञानं एकमेवोपाधिः ।
For *Viśva*, all three—gross, subtle, and ignorance—are the *upādhi*; for *Taijasa*, the two—subtle and ignorance—are the *upādhi*; and for *Prājña*, ignorance alone is the single *upādhi*.
इत्थमुपाधीनामाधिक्यन्यूनत्वाभ्यां त्रयाणां भेदेऽपि वस्तुतः स्वरूपेण न भेदः ।
Thus, even though there is a distinction among the three due to the excess or decrease of their *upādhis*, in truth, in their essential nature, there is no difference.
विश्वतैजसप्राज्ञेषु त्रिष्वनुगतं चैतन्यं परमार्थत उपाधित्रयासम्बद्धमवतिष्ठते ।
The consciousness immanent in the three—*Viśva*, *Taijasa*, and *Prājña*—in reality remains entirely unattached to the three *upādhis*.
त्रयाणामुपाधीनामधिष्ठानं तुरीयम् ।
The substratum (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the three *upādhis* is *Turīya*.
तद्धि न बहिष्प्रज्ञम् ।
For that is not conscious of the external world (*na bahiṣprajñam*).
नान्तःप्रज्ञम् ।
Nor is it conscious of internal objects (*nāntaḥprajñam*).
न प्रज्ञानघनम् ।1
Nor is it a mass of consciousness (*na prajñānaghanam*).
टिप्पणी
1.
यथा तण्डुलकणा जलेन पिण्डीकृता एकीभवन्ति यथा वा वृष्ट्युदकबिन्दवो निम्नदेशं प्राप्य तडागादिरूपेणैकीभवन्ति ।
Just as rice grains made into a lump by water become one, or just as drops of rainwater reaching a low-lying area become one in the form of a pond and the like;
तथा जाग्रत्स्वप्नकालीननानाज्ञानानि सुषुप्ताविद्यायामेकीभवन्ति ।
so also, the manifold cognitions of waking and dream states become unified in the *avidyā* of deep sleep.
तादृशाविद्याप्रतिबिम्बितचैतन्यरूपः प्राज्ञजीवोऽधिष्ठानकूटस्थसहितः प्रज्ञानघन इत्युच्यते ।
The *Prājña-jīva*, whose nature is consciousness reflected in such *avidyā*, together with the underlying *Kūṭastha*, is called a 'mass of consciousness' (*prajñānaghana*).
न कर्मेन्द्रियाणां ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणां वा विषयः ।
It is not an object of the organs of action or the organs of perception.
न बुद्धेर्विषयः ।
It is not an object of the intellect.
न कस्यापि शब्दस्य विषयः ।
It is not the direct referent of any word.
एतादृशं तुरीयं परमात्मनश्चतुर्थपादात्मकेश्वरसाक्षिरूपशुद्धब्रह्मस्वरूपं जानीयात् ।
One should know such *Turīya* as the essential nature of pure *Brahman*, which is the witness of *Īśvara* constituting the fourth quarter of the supreme Self (*Paramātman*).
305
द्विस्वरूपस्य आत्मनः द्विस्वरूपेण ओङ्कारेण अभेदम् आत्मपादानाम् ओङ्कारमात्राणां च अभेदं चिन्तयेत् ।
One should contemplate the non-difference of the dual-natured *ātman* with the dual-natured *oṅkāra*, and the non-difference of the quarters of the *ātman* with the morae of *oṅkāra*.
इत्थं परमार्थरूपम् अपरमार्थरूपम् इति आत्मनः द्विविधं स्वरूपम् उक्तम् ।
Thus the two-fold nature of the *ātman* has been explained as the real nature (*paramārtha-rūpa*) and the non-real nature (*aparamārtha-rūpa*).
तत्र त्रयः पादाः अपरमार्थस्वरूपम् ।
Among them, three quarters constitute the non-ultimate nature.
तुरीयः पादः परमार्थस्वरूपम् ।
The fourth quarter (*turīya*) is the ultimate real nature.
आत्मनः इव ओङ्कारस्य अपि स्वरूपद्वयम् अस्ति ।
Just like the *ātman*, *oṅkāra* also has two aspects.
अकारोकारमकारात्मकमात्रात्रयरूपाणि अक्षराणि अपरमार्थस्वरूपम् ।
The letters constituting the triad of morae comprising 'A', 'U', and 'M' are the non-ultimate nature.
मात्रात्रयव्यापकम्, अस्तिभातिप्रियरूपम् अधिष्ठानचैतन्यं परमार्थस्वरूपम् ।
The substratum-consciousness, all-pervading through the three morae and having the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss (*asti-bhāti-priya*), is the ultimate real nature.
ओङ्कारस्य परमार्थस्वरूपं श्रुतौ अमात्रः इति शब्देन व्यपदिश्यते ।
The ultimate nature of *oṅkāra* is designated in the Śruti by the word 'moraless' (*amātra*).
अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः (मा. आ. १२) इति ।
'The fourth is moraless and unempirical' (Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad 12).
यतस्तस्मिन् परमार्थस्वरूपे मात्राणां विभागो नास्ति तस्मात्तदमात्रमित्युच्यते ।
Because in that ultimate reality there is no division of morae, therefore it is called 'moraless' (*amātra*).
इत्थं स्वरूपद्वयवत ओङ्कारस्य स्वरूपद्वयवता आत्मना सहाभेदं जानीयात् ।
Thus, one should realize the identity of *oṅkāra*, which has a dual nature, with the *ātman*, which likewise has a dual nature.
(१) व्यष्टिसमष्टिस्थूलप्रपञ्चसहितयोर्विश्वविराजोरकारेणाभेदं जानीयात् ।
(1) One should recognize the identity of Viśva and Virāj (associated with the individual and cosmic gross universe) with the letter 'A' (*a-kāra*).
आत्मनः पादेषु विश्वः प्रथमः ।
Among the quarters of the *ātman*, Viśva is the first.
ओङ्कारस्य मात्रासु अकारः प्रथमा मात्रा ।
Among the morae of *oṅkāra*, 'A' is the first mora.
अतस्तयोरैक्यं विद्यात् ।
Therefore one should realize their oneness.
(२) सूक्ष्मप्रपञ्चसहितहिरण्यगर्भात्मकतैजसमुकाररूपेण जानीयात् ।
(2) One should realize Taijasa, who is identical with Hiraṇyagarbha and associated with the subtle world, as the letter 'U' (*u-kāra*).
आत्मनः पादेषु तैजसो द्वितीयः ।
Among the quarters of the *ātman*, Taijasa is the second.
ओङ्कारस्य मात्रासु उकारो द्वितीया मात्रा ।
Among the morae of *oṅkāra*, 'U' is the second mora.
तस्मात्तयोरैक्यं विद्यात् ।
Therefore one should realize their oneness.
(३) कारणोपाधिसहितेश्वररूपं प्राज्ञं मकाररूपेण विद्यात् ।
(3) One should understand Prājña, who is identical with Īśvara possessing the causal *upādhi*, as the letter 'M' (*ma-kāra*).
आत्मनः पादेष्वीश्वरस्वरूपः प्राज्ञस्तृतीयः ।
Among the quarters of the *ātman*, Prājña, who is of the nature of Īśvara, is the third.
ओङ्कारमात्रासु मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा ।
Among the morae of *oṅkāra*, 'M' is the third mora.
ततस्तयोरभेदं जानीयात् ।
Hence, one should know their non-difference.
आत्मनस्त्रिष्वपि पादेष्वनुगतं परमार्थरूपं तुरीयं ओङ्कारस्य तिसृष्वपि मात्रास्वनुगतात् ओङ्कारस्य परमार्थस्वरूपादमात्रादभिन्नतया जानीयात् ।
One should know *turīya*, the ultimate real nature immanent in all three quarters of the *ātman*, as non-different from the moraless (*amātra*) state, which is the ultimate real nature immanent in all three morae of *oṅkāra*.
विश्वादिषु तुरीयोऽनुगतः ।
*Turīya* is immanent in Viśva and the others.
तथा अकारादिषु तिसृषु मात्रासु अमात्रोऽनुगतः ।
Similarly, the moraless (*amātra*) is immanent in the three morae 'A' and the rest.
तस्मादोङ्कारस्य परमार्थस्वरूपममात्रं तुरीयं चाभिन्नं जानीयात् ।
Therefore, one should know the moraless (*amātra*) ultimate nature of *oṅkāra* and *turīya* to be non-different.
अनया रीत्या आत्मपादानां त्रयाणां ओङ्कारमात्राणां तिसृणां चैकताचिन्तनरूपं लयचिन्तनं कुर्यात् ।
In this manner, one should perform the meditation of absorption (*laya-cintana*), which has the form of meditating on the oneness of the three quarters of the *ātman* and the three morae of *oṅkāra*.
306 · लयचिन्तनानुवादःएकैकमात्रारूपविश्वादीनामन्यमात्रारूपता
लयचिन्तनमिदानीं निरूप्यते ।
The meditation on dissolution is now explained.
विश्वात्मकोऽकारः तैजसात्मकादुकारान्न भिन्नः ।
The letter 'A', which is of the nature of Viśva, is not different from the letter 'U', which is of the nature of Taijasa.
किन्तूकाररूप एव ।
Rather, it is of the very nature of the letter 'U'.
एवं चिन्तनमेव लय इत्युच्यते ।
Such contemplation alone is called dissolution (laya).
एवमेवेतरास्वपि मात्रासूह्यम् ।
In the very same manner, it is to be inferred in the case of the other mātrās as well.
यस्मिन्नुकारेऽकारस्य लयः कृतस्तं तैजसात्मकमुकारं प्राज्ञात्मकमकारे लीनं कुर्यात् ।
The letter 'U' (identical to Taijasa), into which the letter 'A' was dissolved, one should merge into the letter 'M' (identical to Prājña).
प्राज्ञरूपं मकारमपि तुरीयरूपे ओङ्कारस्य परमार्थस्वरूपे अमात्रे लीनं कुर्यात् ।
One should also merge the letter 'M', which is of the form of Prājña, into the partless (amātra) state, the supreme essential reality of Omkāra, which is the nature of Turīya.
यतः स्थूलस्योत्पत्तिः सूक्ष्माद्भवति स्थूलस्य लयश्च सूक्ष्मे भवति, तस्माद्विश्वरूपोऽकारस्तैजसरूपे उकारे लीयेत ।
Since the origin of the gross is from the subtle and the dissolution of the gross occurs in the subtle, therefore the letter 'A', which is of the form of Viśva, should dissolve into the letter 'U', which is of the form of Taijasa.
सूक्ष्मस्योत्पत्तिः कारणाद्भवति, सूक्ष्मस्य लयश्च कारणे भवति ।
The origin of the subtle arises from the causal, and the dissolution of the subtle takes place in the causal.
तस्मात्तैजसरूप उकारः तत्कारणे प्राज्ञरूपे मकारे लीयेत ।
Therefore, the letter 'U', of the form of Taijasa, should merge into its cause, the letter 'M', which is of the form of Prājña.
अत्र विश्वादिग्रहणेन स्वस्वत्रिपुट्या सह समष्टिविराडादयोऽपि गृहीता भवन्ति ।
Here, by mentioning Viśva and so on, along with their respective triads, the cosmic entities such as Virāṭ are also included.
यस्मिन् प्राज्ञरूपे मकारे उकारस्य लयः कृतः तं मकारं तुरीयरूपे ओङ्कारस्य परमार्थरूपे अमात्रे लीनं कुर्यात् ।
The letter 'M', which is of the nature of Prājña and into which the letter 'U' was merged, one should merge into the partless (amātra), the true absolute reality of Omkāra, which is Turīya.
ओङ्कारपरमार्थस्वरूपस्य तुरीयस्य चाभेदोऽस्ति ।
And there is non-difference between the supreme reality of Omkāra and Turīya.
तच्च तुरीयं ब्रह्मैव ।
And that Turīya is Brahman alone.
तस्मिन् शुद्धे ब्रह्मणीश्वरः प्राज्ञश्च कल्पितौ ।
In that pure Brahman, both Īśvara and Prājña are superimposed.
यद्यस्मिन् कल्पितं तत्तत्स्वरूपमिति न्यायः ।
'Whatever is superimposed upon something is essentially identical to that locus' — such is the logical maxim.
तस्मादीश्वरसहितप्राज्ञरूपमकारस्यामात्रे लयो युज्यत एव ।
Therefore, the dissolution into the amātra (partless) of the letter 'M', which is of the form of Prājña together with Īśvara, is entirely appropriate.
इत्थं यस्मिन् ओङ्कारस्य परमार्थस्वरूपे अमात्रे सर्वेषां प्रविलयः कृतः स एवाहमस्मि इत्यैकाग्र्येणानवरतं चिन्तयेत् ।
In this way, one should ceaselessly contemplate with one-pointed focus: 'I am that very amātra, the absolute nature of Omkāra, in which the total dissolution of everything has been effected.'
निखिलचराचरप्रपञ्चात्मकासङ्गाद्वयासंसारिनित्यमुक्तनिर्भयब्रह्मरूपो य ओङ्कारस्तस्य यत् परमार्थस्वरूपं तदेवाहमस्मि इत्यादरेण नैरन्तर्येण च दीर्घकालं यश्चिन्तयति तस्य ज्ञानमुदेति ।
Knowledge dawns in him who contemplates for a long time, uninterruptedly and with deep reverence: 'I am that very ultimate nature of Omkāra, which is the nature of Brahman — the self of the entire moving and unmoving universe, unattached, non-dual, free from transmigration, ever-liberated, and fearless.'
ततो ज्ञानद्वारा मुक्तिरूपफलमपि सिद्ध्यति ।
Then, through knowledge, the fruit in the form of liberation (mokṣa) is also attained.
तदेवमोङ्कारस्य निर्गुणोपासनं सर्वोपासनेभ्यः श्रष्ठम् ।
Therefore, this attributeless meditation (nirguṇa-upāsanā) on Omkāra is the highest among all meditations.
307 · ओङ्कारोपासने परमहंसस्यैवाधिकारः
पूर्वोक्तरीत्या ओङ्कारस्वरूपं यो जानाति स मुनिः ।
He who knows the true nature of Omkāra according to the method explained earlier is a sage (muni).
मननान्मुनिरित्युच्यते ।
He is called a 'muni' because of his constant reflection (manana).
एवमोङ्कारस्य चिन्तनं मननरूपं भवति ।
Thus, the meditation on Omkāra is of the nature of reflection (manana).
यस्यैवमोङ्कारचिन्तनरूपमननं नास्ति न स मुनिः ।
One who lacks such reflection in the form of contemplation on Omkāra is not a muni.
इत्थं माण्डूक्योपनिषदुक्तरीत्या सङ्क्षेपेणोङ्कारचिन्तनं वर्णितम् ।
In this manner, meditation on Omkāra has been briefly described according to the method taught in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad.
नृसिंहतापिन्याद्युपनिषत्स्वप्योङ्कारोपासनक्रमो वर्णितः (नृ. उ. ५) ।
The sequence of meditation on Omkāra is described in Upaniṣads such as the Nṛsiṃhatāpinī as well (नृ. उ. ५).
इदं चोङ्कारचिन्तनं परमहंसानामेव गोप्यं धनम् ।
And this meditation on Omkāra is the secret wealth of paramahaṃsa renunciates alone.
बहिर्मुखस्य नास्त्यत्राधिकारः ।
An extroverted person has no eligibility here.
अत्यन्तान्तर्मुखस्यैवात्राधिकारः ।
Only one who is deeply introverted is qualified for this.
गृहस्थानां नास्त्यत्राधिकारः ।
Householders do not have eligibility in this.
दारापत्यवित्तादिपरिग्रहरहितः परमहंस एवात्राधिकारी ।
Only a paramahaṃsa who is devoid of possessions such as spouse, progeny, and wealth is qualified for this.
फलितम्ओङ्कारध्यानफलम्॥ ३०८–३०९ ॥
308
ओङ्कारध्यानं ज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षफलकम् ।
Meditation on Omkāra yields the fruit of mokṣa through knowledge.
उक्तरीत्या ब्रह्मरूपेणोङ्कारोपासकस्य ज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षः सिद्ध्यति ।
In the stated manner, mokṣa is attained through knowledge for one who meditates on Omkāra as Brahman.
परन्तु यस्य पुनरैहिकभोगे आमुष्मिकब्रह्मलोकभोगे वेच्छास्ति तीव्रवैराग्यं च नास्ति, तथापि हठादिच्छां निरुध्य दारापत्यधनादिकं परित्यज्य परमहंसगुरूपदेशेन यावज्जीवमोङ्काररूपं ब्रह्माभिध्यायेत्, तस्य भोगेच्छा ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धिका भवति ।
However, for one who still has desire for worldly enjoyment or enjoyment in the other-worldly Brahmaloka and lacks intense dispassion, yet forcefully suppresses that desire, abandons wife, progeny, wealth, etc., and by the instruction of a Paramahaṃsa Guru meditates all his life on Brahman as Omkāra, his desire for enjoyment becomes an obstacle to knowledge.
तस्मात्तस्येह न ज्ञानं जायते ।
Therefore, knowledge does not arise for him here in this life.
किन्तु स ध्यानानुष्ठानपूर्वकमेवैतच्छरीरं त्यक्त्वा शरीरान्तरमादत्ते ।
Instead, departing from this body while still engaged in the practice of meditation, he takes another body.
ऐहिकभोगेच्छानिरोधपूर्वकं ध्यानानुष्ठानकारणात्स मनुष्यलोके सतां शुचीनां श्रीमतां कुलेऽभिजायते ।
On account of the practice of meditation performed with suppression of worldly desires, he is born in the human world into a family of the virtuous, pure, and prosperous.
तत्र पूर्वजन्मेच्छाविषयभूतान् सकलान् भोगान् भुक्त्वा पूर्वजन्मानुष्ठितध्यानसंस्कारबलाद्भूयोऽपि ध्याने वा विचारे वा प्रवर्तते ।
There, having exhausted all enjoyments that were the objects of his desire in the past birth, he engages again either in meditation or in inquiry by the power of the saṃskāras of meditation practiced in the past life.
ततो ज्ञानम्, ज्ञानान्मोक्षं च लभते ।
Thence he attains knowledge, and through knowledge, mokṣa.
309
ओङ्कारध्यानं ब्रह्मलोकप्राप्तिफलकम् ।
Meditation on Omkāra also has the attainment of Brahmaloka as its fruit.
यः पुनर्ब्राह्मलौकिकभोगेच्छां निरुध्योङ्काररूपब्रह्मध्यानमकरोत्स शरीरपातानन्तरं ब्रह्मलोकं गच्छति ।
On the other hand, one who, having suppressed even the desire for enjoyments in Brahmaloka, meditated on Brahman in the form of Omkāra, goes to Brahmaloka after the fall of the body.
तत्र मनुष्यपितृदेवानां दुर्लभं स्वातन्त्र्यं तत्प्रयुक्तमानन्दं चानुभवति ।
There he experiences freedom that is rare even for humans, ancestors, and gods, and the ānanda arising from it.
हिरण्यगर्भतुल्यभोगान् सत्यसङ्कल्पत्वाद्यैश्वर्यविशेषांश्च लभते ।
He attains enjoyments equal to those of Hiraṇyagarbha and distinct divine faculties such as *satya-saṅkalpatva* (the power of having desires instantly fulfilled).
(३१०)॥ ३१०–३१६ ॥
310 · ब्रह्मलोकमार्गःब्रह्मलोकगमनमार्गक्रमस्त्वेवं
ब्रह्मोपासनतत्परः पुरुषो यदा म्रियते तदा तस्यान्तःकरणमिन्द्रियाणि च सम्मूर्च्छितानि भवन्ति ।
When a person intent on meditation on Brahman dies, his mind and sense-organs become totally stupefied.
ततः स न किञ्चिदपि बोद्धुं कर्तुं वा शक्नोति ।
Consequently, he is unable to comprehend or perform anything.
तथापि यमदूतास्तस्य लिङ्गशरीरं नेतुं न तदन्तिकमागच्छन्ति ।
Even then, the messengers of Yama do not come near him to carry away his subtle body.
किन्त्वग्न्यभिमानिनी देवता तस्य मरणसमये तमुपासकं शरीराद्वियोज्य स्वलोकं नयति ।
Rather, at the time of his death, the deity presiding over Fire separates that meditator from the body and leads him to its realm.
ततोऽग्निलोकात्तमुपासकमहरभिमानिनी देवता स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, from the realm of Fire, the deity presiding over Day leads that meditator to its realm.
ततः शुक्लपक्षाभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over the bright fortnight leads that meditator to its realm.
तत उत्तरायणाभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over Uttarāyaṇa (the northern path of the sun) leads that meditator to its realm.
ततः संवत्सराभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over the Year leads that meditator to its realm.
ततो देवलोकाभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over the Devaloka leads that meditator to its realm.
ततो वाय्वभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over Air (Vāyu) leads that meditator to its realm.
ततः सूर्याभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over the Sun leads that meditator to its realm.
ततश्चन्द्राभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।
Then, the deity presiding over the Moon leads that meditator to its realm.
ततो विद्युदभिमानिनी देवता तमुपासकं स्वलोकं नयति ।1
Then, the deity presiding over Lightning leads that meditator to its realm.
टिप्पणी
1.
मरणसमये जीवापेतस्थूलदेहाल्लिङ्गशरीरं वियुक्तं भवति ।
At the time of death, the subtle body becomes detached from the gross body which has been abandoned by the jīva.
तदा चैतन्याभावात्सम्मूर्च्छितान्युपासकस्यान्तःकरणमिन्द्रियाणि च स्वतः न किञ्चिदपि ज्ञातुं शक्नुवन्ति ।
Then, because of the absence of consciousness, the meditator's mind and sense-organs, being stupefied, are unable on their own to know anything at all.
क्रियाशक्तियुक्तप्राणोऽपि स्वरूपत एवाचेतनत्वेनेच्छाभावान्न क्वचिदपि गन्तुं शक्नोति ।
Even the prāṇa, although endowed with the power of action, is essentially insentient, and thus devoid of desire/will, cannot move anywhere on its own.
तत्र विद्युल्लोके हिरण्यगर्भाज्ञया हिरण्यगर्भलोकवासी हिरण्यगर्भसरूपश्च कश्चनामानवो दिव्यपुरुषस्तमुपासकं नेतुमागच्छति ।
There, in the realm of Lightning, by the command of Hiraṇyagarbha, a certain non-human divine person, who is a resident of Hiraṇyagarbha's realm and possesses a form resembling Hiraṇyagarbha, arrives to guide that meditator.
स चामानवः पुरुषस्तमुपासकं विद्युल्लोकाद्वरुणलोकं नयति ।
And that non-human person leads that meditator from the realm of Lightning to the realm of Varuṇa.
विद्युदभिमानिनी देवता च वरुणलोकपर्यन्तं तमनुगच्छति ।
And the deity presiding over Lightning accompanies him up to the realm of Varuṇa.
ततोऽप्यमानव एव पुरुषस्तमुपासकं वरुणलोकादिन्द्रलोकं नयति ।
Then, that very non-human person leads the meditator from the realm of Varuṇa to the realm of Indra.
वरुणदेवता चेन्द्रलोकपर्यन्तं तमनुसरति ।
And the deity Varuṇa follows him up to the realm of Indra.
ततोऽपि स दिव्यः पुरुष एव तमुपासकमिन्द्रलोकात्प्रजापतिलोकं नयति ।
From there as well, that divine person alone leads the meditator from the realm of Indra to the realm of Prajāpati.
इन्द्रश्च प्रजापतिलोकपर्यन्तं तमनुसरति ।
And Indra accompanies him up to the realm of Prajāpati.
प्रजापतेर्ब्रह्मलोकगमनसामर्थ्याभावादमानवपुरुषोऽसहकृत एव तमुपासकं प्रजापतिलोकात् ब्रह्मलोकं नयति ।
Because Prajāpati lacks the capacity to enter Brahmaloka, the non-human person alone, unaccompanied, leads that meditator from the realm of Prajāpati to Brahmaloka.
ब्रह्मलोकस्याधिपतिर्हिरण्यगर्भः ।
The sovereign lord of Brahmaloka is Hiraṇyagarbha.
समष्टिसूक्ष्माभिमानी चेतनो हिरण्यगर्भ इति कीर्त्यते ।
The conscious entity identifying with the aggregate subtle universe is declared to be Hiraṇyagarbha.
तमेव हिरण्यगर्भमपरब्रह्मेति कार्यब्रह्मेति च वदन्ति ।
That very Hiraṇyagarbha they call 'Apara Brahman' (lower Brahman) and 'Kārya Brahman' (effect Brahman).
कार्यब्रह्माधिष्ठित एव लोको ब्रह्मलोक इत्युच्यते ।
Only the realm presided over by the Kārya Brahman is called Brahmaloka.
311
सायुज्यमुक्तिवर्णनम् ।
Description of sāyujya-mukti (liberation of union with the conditioned Brahman).
यद्यपि पूर्वोक्तरीत्या ओङ्कारोपासनं शुद्धब्रह्मरूपेणोक्तम्, शुद्धब्रह्मोपासकस्य शुद्धब्रह्मप्राप्तिरेवोचिता ।
Although, according to the manner explained earlier, the meditation on *Oṁkāra* was stated in the form of pure *Brahman*, and for a meditator on pure *Brahman* the attainment of pure *Brahman* alone is proper,
यथाक्रतुरस्मिन् लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति (छा. ३-१४-१) इति श्रुतेः ।
— because of the *Śruti* statement: 'Whatever conviction a person has in this world, such he becomes upon departing from here' (Chā. 3.14.1),
यं यं वापि स्मरन् भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ (भ. गी. ८.६) इति स्मृतेर्न्यायाच्च ।
— and from the *Smṛti* rule: 'Remembering whatever state of being one gives up the body at the end, to that very state he goes, O son of Kuntī, constantly absorbed in that thought' (Bh.Gītā 8.6), as well as from logical reasoning;
तथापि शुद्धब्रह्मप्राप्तेर्वेदान्तप्रमाणजन्यद्वैतमिथ्यात्वपूर्वकाद्वैतज्ञानमात्रसाध्यत्वात् भोगेच्छारूपप्रतिबन्धसत्त्वाच्च यस्य ज्ञानं न सञ्जातं तस्य कार्यब्रह्मप्राप्तिरूपसायुज्यमुक्तिरेव सिद्ध्यति ।
even so, since the attainment of pure *Brahman* can only be achieved solely through non-dual knowledge preceded by the understanding of the falsity of duality generated from the *pramāṇa* of Vedānta, and because of the existence of an obstacle in the form of desire for celestial enjoyments, for one in whom such knowledge has not arisen, only *sāyujya-mukti* in the form of attaining *kārya-Brahman* (Hiraṇyagarbha) results.
ब्रह्मलोकं गतस्योपासकस्य हिरण्यगर्भस्य मानविभूत्यैश्वर्यादिकं सिद्ध्यति ।
