For the meditator who has gone to *Brahmaloka*, honor, glory, divine sovereignty, and other attributes equal to those of Hiraṇyagarbha are attained.
सत्यसङ्कल्पत्वमिच्छानुरूपं शरीरं सङ्कल्पमात्रेणाभीष्टभोगलाभश्च सिद्ध्यति ।
Unfailing will (*satya-saṅkalpatva*), bodies fashioned according to his wish, and the obtainment of desired enjoyments by mere thought alone are accomplished.
युगपदेव नानाशरीरैर्नानाभोगानुभवेच्छायां सत्यां सङ्कल्पमात्रादेव क्षणेनैव नानाविचित्रशरीराणि पृथक् पृथक् भोगोपकरणसिद्धिश्च भवति ।
When there is a desire to experience various objects through multiple bodies simultaneously, by mere wish within a moment various diverse bodies and distinct instruments of enjoyment are manifested.
किं बहुना ।
What more need be said?
यद्यत्सङ्कल्पयति तत्सर्वमप्रत्यूहेन सद्यः सम्पद्यते ।
Whatever he resolves, all of it comes to pass instantly and without impediment.
परन्तु जगत्सृष्टिपालनसंहरणव्यतिरिक्ताः सर्वा विभूतयो हिरण्यगर्भसमाः सिद्ध्यन्ति ।
However, with the exception of the creation, preservation, and dissolution of the universe, all other powers and glories equal to those of Hiraṇyagarbha are attained.
अनेकेश्वरत्वे जगत उन्मथप्रसङ्गात् सृष्ट्यादित्रिकातिरिक्तसकलैश्वर्याण्युपासकस्य सिद्ध्यन्ति ।
Because multiple rulers would lead to the chaos and destruction of the world, all lordly powers other than the threefold cosmic function of creation, maintenance, and destruction belong to the meditator.
इयमेव सायुज्यमुक्तिरिति कथ्यते ।
This alone is called *sāyujya-mukti*.
एवमुपासको हिरण्यगर्भसमः सन् चिरकालं सङ्कल्पमात्रसिद्धान् नाना दिव्यभोगान् भुञ्जानः प्रलयकाले हिरण्यगर्भलोकस्यावसानकाले समुदिताद्वैतात्मज्ञानो विदेहमोक्षं लभते ।
Thus, the meditator, equal to Hiraṇyagarbha, enjoying for a long duration various divine pleasures accomplished by mere will, attains disembodied liberation (*videha-mokṣa*) at the time of cosmic dissolution (*pralaya*), at the end of the realm of Hiraṇyagarbha, when non-dual Self-knowledge arises.
ब्रह्मणा सह ते सर्वे सम्प्राप्ते प्रतिसञ्चरे । परस्यान्ते कृतात्मानः प्रविशन्ति परं पदम् ॥ (कू. पु. १२.२६९) इत्यादिवचनात् ।
— as stated in verses such as: 'At the time of the great dissolution, when the end of the life of the supreme creator arrives, all of them having realized the Self enter the supreme state along with Brahmā' (Kū. Pu. 12.269).
312 · अहङ्ग्रहध्यानादेव ब्रह्मलोकप्राप्तिरिति नियमः
यथा ओङ्काररूपब्रह्मोपासकस्य ब्रह्मलोकप्राप्तिद्वारा मोक्षलाभः फलं तथोपनिषत्सूक्तानामितरेषामपि ब्रह्मोपासनानामिदमेव फलम् ।
Just as for one who meditates on *Brahman* in the form of *Oṁkāra*, the fruit is the attainment of liberation through reaching *Brahmaloka*, likewise this very fruit belongs to the other meditations on *Brahman* taught in the Upaniṣads as well.
किन्तु अहङ्ग्रहोपासनं विनेतरोपासनेन न ब्रह्मलोकोऽवाप्यत इति सूत्रकारैर्भाष्यकारैश्च ब्रह्मसूत्रेषु भाष्यादिषु च चतुर्थाध्याये वर्णितम् ।
However, it has been described by the author of the Sūtras (*Bādarāyaṇa*) and the commentator (*Śaṅkarācārya*) in the fourth chapter of the *Brahmasūtras* and their commentaries that without *ahaṅgraha* meditation (identifying the Self with *Brahman*), *Brahmaloka* is not reached by other forms of meditation.
नार्मदबाणानां शिवरूपेण, सालग्रामशिलानां विष्णुरूपेण च ध्यानं तु प्रतीकध्यानमेव ।
Meditation on the stones from the Narmadā as Śiva, and on the *Śālagrāma* stones as Viṣṇu, is merely symbolic meditation (*pratīka-dhyāna*).
नाहङ्ग्रहध्यानम् ।
It is not *ahaṅgraha* meditation.
एवमेव मनो ब्रह्मेत्युपासीत (छा. ३.१८.१) आदित्यो ब्रह्मेत्यादेशः (छा. ३.१९.१) इत्यादिश्रुत्युक्तोपासनमपि प्रतीकध्यानमेव ।
Similarly, the meditations taught in the *Śrutis* such as 'One should meditate on the mind as Brahman' (Chā. 3.18.1) and 'The instruction is that the sun is Brahman' (Chā. 3.19.1) are also purely symbolic meditations (*pratīka-dhyāna*).
नाहङ्ग्रहध्यानम् ।
They are not *ahaṅgraha* meditations.
तेषां तत्तत्प्रकरणे पृथक् फलश्रवणात्तैर्न ब्रह्मलोकोऽवाप्यते ।
Because distinct fruits are declared for them in their respective scriptural contexts, *Brahmaloka* is not attained by them.
सगुणस्याथवा निर्गुणस्य ब्रह्मणः स्वात्माभेदेन चिन्तनमहङ्ग्रहध्यानमित्युच्यते ।
Contemplation of *Brahman*, whether qualified (*saguṇa*) or unconditioned (*nirguṇa*), as non-different from one's own Self, is called *ahaṅgraha* meditation.
तेनैव ध्यानेन ब्रह्मलोकोऽवाप्येत ।
By that meditation alone can *Brahmaloka* be attained.
313 · उत्तरायणमार्गेण ब्रह्मलोकं गतानां पुनः संसाराप्राप्तिः; ज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षप्राप्तिश्च
पूर्वोक्तो मार्ग उत्तरायणमार्गो देवयानमार्गोऽर्चिरादिमार्ग इति चोच्यते ।
The previously described path is also called the northern path (uttarāyaṇa-mārga), the path of the gods (devayāna-mārga), and the path beginning with light (arcirādi-mārga).
तेन देवमार्गेण ब्रह्मलोकं गत उपासकः पुनः संसारं न प्रतिपद्यते, किन्तु तत्रैव ज्ञानोत्पत्त्या स विदेहमुक्तिमाप्नोति ।
The meditator who has gone to Brahmaloka by that divine path does not return to worldly existence, but rather attains *videhamukti* right there through the dawn of knowledge.
तत्र ज्ञानसाधनीभूतगुरूपदेशाद्यपेक्षा नास्ति ।
There, there is no dependence on means of knowledge such as the guru's instruction.
ब्रह्मलोके गुरूपदेशादिसाधनं विनैव ज्ञानोत्पत्तिर्भवति ।
In Brahmaloka, knowledge arises even without external means such as the guru's instruction.
तत्र च कारणं ब्रह्मलोके रजस्तमोगुणयोर्लेशतोऽप्यभावः ।
And the reason for that is the complete absence, even in the slightest degree, of the qualities of *rajas* and *tamas* in Brahmaloka.
तस्य लोकस्य केवल1
Of that realm, purely...
टिप्पणी
1.
राज्ञः प्रजानां राज्य इव ईश्वरलोके वासमात्रं सालोक्यमुक्तिः ।
Just like subjects residing in a king's kingdom, mere residence in the realm of the Lord is *sālokya-mukti*.
ततोऽपि श्रेष्ठा राजसेवकवदीश्वरसमीपे वासरूपा सामीप्यमुक्तिः ।
Higher even than that is *sāmīpya-mukti*, which consists of dwelling in proximity to the Lord, like a king's attendant.
ततोऽप्युत्कृष्टा राजानुजवदीश्वरसमानरूपप्राप्तिः सारूप्यमुक्तिः ।
Superior even to that is *sārūpya-mukti*, which is attaining a form identical to the Lord, like the king's younger brother.
ततोऽप्यतिशयिता राज्ञो ज्येष्ठपुत्रयुवराजवदीश्वरसमानसत्यसङ्कल्पाद्यैश्वर्यप्राप्तिः सार्ष्ट्यमुक्तिरित्थमुत्तरोत्तरमुत्कृष्टा चतुर्विधा मुक्तिः शास्त्रेषु कथिता ।
Exceeding even that is *sārṣṭi-mukti*, which is attaining lordly powers such as infallible will equal to the Lord, like the king's eldest son, the crown prince; thus four progressively higher types of liberation are declared in the scriptures.
तत्र चतुर्थी सार्ष्ट्यमुक्तिः श्रेष्ठा ।
Among those, the fourth, *sārṣṭi-mukti*, is the highest.
सार्ष्ट्यमुक्तिरेव सायुज्यमुक्तिरीत्युच्यते ।
*Sārṣṭi-mukti* itself is called *sāyujya-mukti*.
सत्त्वगुणप्रधानता च ।
And there is the predominance of the *sattva-guṇa*.
तमोगुणाभावात् जडत्वालस्यादिकं नास्ति ।
Because of the absence of *tamo-guṇa*, dullness, lethargy, and the like do not exist.
रजोगुणाभावात् तत्कार्यभूतकामक्रोधादिरूपविक्षेपोऽपि नास्ति ।
Because of the absence of *rajo-guṇa*, there is also no distraction in the form of desire, anger, and so forth which are its effects.
एवं तमोरजसोरभावादावरणविक्षेपयोरभावे केवलसत्त्वगुणप्रधाने ब्रह्मलोके सत्त्वगुणकार्यज्ञानरूपप्रकाशस्तत्र लोके मुख्यः ।
Thus, due to the absence of *tamas* and *rajas*, and consequently the absence of veiling (*āvaraṇa*) and projection (*vikṣepa*), in Brahmaloka where pure *sattva-guṇa* is predominant, the light in the form of knowledge, which is the effect of *sattva-guṇa*, is pre-eminent in that world.
एतेन प्रतिपद्यमाना इमं मानवमावर्तं नावर्तन्ते (छा. ४.१५.५) न च पुनरावर्तते (छा. ८.१५.१) तेषां न पुनरावृत्तिः (बृ. ६.२.१५) ज्ञानमुत्पद्यते पुंसां क्षयात्पापस्य कर्मणः सत्त्वात् सञ्जायते ज्ञानम् (भ. गी. १४.१७) इत्यादिश्रुतिस्मृतिभ्यः ।
[This is proven] from *śruti* and *smṛti* passages such as: 'Those who go by this do not return to this human cycle' (Chā. 4.15.5), 'And he does not return again' (Chā. 8.15.1), 'For them there is no return' (Bṛ. 6.2.15), 'Knowledge arises in men upon the destruction of sinful karma', and 'From sattva arises knowledge' (Bh. Gī. 14.17).
314
पूर्वमोङ्कारस्य ब्रह्मरूपतयोपासनकाले ओङ्कारमात्राणामर्थो वक्ष्यमाणरीत्या चिन्तितः - स्थूलोपाधिविशिष्टविराडात्मकविश्वचैतन्यमकाररूपप्रथममात्राया वाच्यार्थः ।
Earlier, at the time of meditating on Om as Brahman, the meaning of the morae of Om was contemplated in the following manner: the Viśva consciousness identical with Virāṭ qualified by the gross upādhi is the literal meaning of the first mora in the form of 'A'.
सूक्ष्मोपाधिविशिष्टहिरण्यगर्भात्मकतैजसचैतन्यमुकाररूपद्वितीयमात्राया वाच्यार्थः ।
The Taijasa consciousness identical with Hiraṇyagarbha qualified by the subtle upādhi is the literal meaning of the second mora in the form of 'U'.
कारणोपाधिविशिष्टेश्वरात्मकप्राज्ञचैतन्यं मकाररूपतृतीयमात्राया वाच्यार्थः ।
The Prājña consciousness identical with Īśvara qualified by the causal upādhi is the literal meaning of the third mora in the form of 'M'.
एवं प्राक्चिन्तितार्थानुस्मरणमुपासकस्य ब्रह्मलोके जायते ।
Thus, the recollection of the meaning contemplated earlier arises for the meditator in the realm of Brahmā.
सत्त्वगुणप्रभावाच्च वक्ष्यमाणप्रकारेण विवेकपूर्वकं विचारयति चोपासकः - (१) स्थूलोपाधिदृष्ट्या खलु शुद्धे चैतन्ये विराट्त्वविश्वत्वप्रतीतिरभूत् ।
And due to the power of the sattva-guṇa, the meditator discriminatively inquires in the following manner: '(1) Indeed, from the viewpoint of the gross upādhi, the appearance of Virāṭ-hood and Viśva-hood occurred in pure consciousness.
तत्र समष्टिस्थूलदृष्ट्या विराट्त्वम्, व्यष्टिस्थूलदृष्ट्या विश्वत्वं चाभात् ।
There, from the perspective of the cosmic gross, Virāṭ-hood appeared, and from the perspective of the individual gross, Viśva-hood appeared.
समष्टिव्यष्ट्यात्मकस्थूलदृष्टिविरहे विराट्त्वविश्वत्वे न प्रतीयेयाताम् ।
In the absence of the gross viewpoint of the cosmic and the individual, Virāṭ-hood and Viśva-hood would not be perceived.
किन्तु शुद्धं चैतन्यमात्रं भासेत ।
Rather, pure consciousness alone would shine.
तस्मात्स्थूलोपाधिसहितविराडात्मकविश्वोऽकारवाच्यार्थः ।
Therefore, Viśva, who is identical with Virāṭ together with the gross upādhi, is the literal meaning of 'A'.
तथैव सूक्ष्मोपाधिसहितहिरण्यगर्भात्मकतैजस उकारवाच्यार्थः ।
(2) In the exact same way, Taijasa identical with Hiraṇyagarbha accompanied by the subtle upādhi is the literal meaning of 'U'.
समष्टिसूक्ष्मोपाधिदृष्ट्या शुद्धचैतन्ये हिरण्यगर्भत्वम्, व्यष्टिसूक्ष्मोपाधिदृष्ट्या तैजसत्वं चाभात् ।
From the perspective of the cosmic subtle upādhi, Hiraṇyagarbha-hood appeared in pure consciousness, and from the perspective of the individual subtle upādhi, Taijasa-hood appeared.
सूक्ष्मोपाधिदृष्टिविरहे तु हिरण्यगर्भत्वं तैजसत्वं वा न भायात् ।
However, in the absence of the subtle upādhi perspective, neither Hiraṇyagarbha-hood nor Taijasa-hood would shine.
किन्तु शुद्धं चैतन्यमात्रं भासेत ।
Rather, pure consciousness alone would shine.
तथैव कारणोपाधिसहितेश्वरात्मा प्राज्ञो मकारवाच्यार्थः ।
(3) In the same manner, Prājña, identical with Īśvara accompanied by the causal upādhi, is the literal meaning of 'M'.
समष्ट्यज्ञानोपाधिदृष्ट्या शुद्धचैतन्ये ईश्वरत्वमभात्, व्यष्ट्यज्ञानोपाधिदृष्ट्या प्राज्ञत्वमभात् ।
From the perspective of the cosmic nescience-upādhi, Īśvara-hood appeared in pure consciousness, and from the perspective of the individual nescience-upādhi, Prājña-hood appeared.
अज्ञानोपाधिदृष्टिविरहे तु ईश्वरत्वं प्राज्ञत्वं वा न भासेत ।
However, in the absence of the nescience-upādhi perspective, neither Īśvara-hood nor Prājña-hood would shine.
किन्तु केवलचैतन्यमात्रं प्रतीयेत ।
Rather, mere absolute consciousness alone would be perceived.
किञ्च यत्र यद्वस्त्वन्यदृष्ट्या प्रतीयते तत्र तद्वस्तु परमार्थतो नास्ति ।
Moreover, wherever an entity is perceived due to an extrinsic perspective, there that entity does not exist in absolute reality.
यस्य वस्तुनो यद्रूपमन्यदृष्टिं विना स्वत एव प्रतीयते तदेव तस्य पारमार्थिकं स्वरूपम् ।
Whichever form of an entity is perceived by itself without any extrinsic perspective, that alone is its ultimate, real nature.
यथा कस्मिंश्चित्पुरुषे पितृदृष्ट्या पुत्रत्वम्, पितामहदृष्ट्या पौत्रत्वं च प्रतीयमानं न तस्य परमार्थधर्मः, किन्तु पुरुषत्वमेव तस्य परमार्थधर्मः ।
Just as in a person, being a son perceived from the perspective of the father, and being a grandson perceived from the perspective of the grandfather, is not his real attribute, but his very personhood alone is his real attribute;
तथा स्थूलसूक्ष्मकारणोपाधिदृष्ट्या भासमानविश्वत्वतैजसत्वप्राज्ञत्वादयो न परमार्थधर्माः, परन्तु मिथ्यैव ते ।
so too, the appearing Viśva-hood, Taijasa-hood, Prājña-hood, etc., from the perspective of the gross, subtle, and causal upādhis, are not real attributes, but rather they are entirely illusory.
चैतन्यमात्रं परमार्थसत्यम् ।
Consciousness alone is the absolute truth.
तच्च चैतन्यं समस्तभेदशून्यम् ।
And that consciousness is devoid of all distinctions.
विराजो विश्वस्य च भेद औपाधिक एव ।
The distinction between Virāṭ and Viśva is only due to the upādhi.
तयोरुभयोः स्थूलोपाधिकत्वेऽपि समष्ट्युपाधिको विराट् ।
Even though both of them possess the gross upādhi, Virāṭ has the cosmic upādhi.
विश्वस्तु व्यष्ट्युपाधिकः ।
Whereas Viśva has the individual upādhi.
समष्टिव्यष्ट्युपाधिप्रयुक्तभेदवत्त्वेऽपि विराड्विश्वयोः स्वरूपतो नास्ति भेदः ।
Despite having a difference occasioned by the cosmic and individual upādhis, between Virāṭ and Viśva there is fundamentally no distinction in essential nature.
तथैव हिरण्यगर्भतैजसयोः समष्टिव्यष्ट्युपाधिप्रयुक्तभेदवत्त्वेऽपि स्वरूपतो न भेदोऽस्ति ।
Just so, between Hiraṇyagarbha and Taijasa, despite having a difference occasioned by the cosmic and individual upādhis, there is fundamentally no distinction in essential nature.
एवमेवेश्वरप्राज्ञयोः समष्टिव्यष्ट्युपाधिनिबन्धन एव भेदो न स्वरूपतः ।
In the same manner, between Īśvara and Prājña, the distinction is solely grounded on cosmic and individual upādhis, not in their essential nature.
इत्थं च प्राज्ञेनेश्वरस्य, तैजसेन हिरण्यगर्भस्य, विश्वेन विराजश्चाभेदः सिद्धः ।
And thus, the non-difference of Īśvara with Prājña, of Hiraṇyagarbha with Taijasa, and of Virāṭ with Viśva is established.
एवमेव स्थूलोपाधिकस्य सूक्ष्मोपाधिकेन वा कारणोपाधिकेन वा न भेदगन्धोऽप्यस्ति ।
Likewise, between that which has the gross upādhi and that which has the subtle upādhi or the causal upādhi, there is not even a trace of difference.
यतः स्थूलसूक्ष्मकारणरूपोपाधिदृष्टिपरित्यागे चैतन्यस्वरूपे न कोऽपि भेदोऽस्ति ।
Because upon renouncing the perspective of the upādhis in the forms of gross, subtle, and causal, there exists no difference whatsoever in the essential nature of consciousness.
किञ्चानात्मनः सकाशादपि चैतन्यस्य नास्ति भेदः ।
Moreover, there is no difference of Consciousness even from the non-Self.
यतोऽनात्मभूतदेहादिप्रपञ्चोऽविद्यादशायामेव भाति ।
Because the universe consisting of body and so forth, which is non-Self, appears only in the state of avidyā.
न परमार्थतः ।
Not from the ultimate standpoint.
तस्मादनात्मप्रपञ्चस्यापि चैतन्येन सह भेदोऽसङ्गत एव ।
Therefore, even the difference of the non-Self universe from Consciousness is indeed untenable.
इत्थं सर्वभेदशून्यासङ्गनिर्विकारनित्यमुक्तपरब्रह्मस्वरूपः प्रत्यगात्मा ओङ्कारलक्ष्यार्थत्वेन स्वयम्प्रकाशतया ब्रह्मलोके उपासकस्य भासते ।
Thus the inner ātman, whose true nature is the supreme Brahman devoid of all differences, unattached, changeless, and eternally liberated, shines forth by its self-luminosity as the implied meaning of *Oṅkāra* to the meditator in the world of Brahmā.
तस्माद्धिरण्यगर्भलोके वसत उपासकस्य न पुनः संसारगतिः ।
Therefore, for the meditator dwelling in the world of Hiraṇyagarbha, there is no return to saṃsāra.
किन्तु स ज्ञानेन विदेहकैवल्यमेवाप्नोति कार्यब्रह्मणोऽवसानसमये ।
Rather, he attains disembodied liberation (*videha-kaivalya*) indeed through knowledge at the time of the dissolution of kārya-Brahman.
315 · ओङ्कारस्य महावाक्यानां चार्थैकत्वम्
यद्यपि महावाक्यविवेकमन्तरा ज्ञानं न सिद्ध्यतीति सिद्धान्तस्तथापि ओङ्कारविवेकस्य महावाक्यविवेकरूपत्वादोङ्कारविवेकेनापि ज्ञानमुदियादेव ।
Although the established conclusion is that knowledge cannot be attained without inquiry into the *mahāvākya*s, nonetheless, because the inquiry into *Oṁkāra* is identical in nature to the inquiry into the *mahāvākya*s, knowledge will certainly arise through the inquiry into *Oṁkāra* as well.
तथा हि, स्थूलोपाधिसहितचेतनोऽकारवाच्यार्थः; स्थूलोपाधिरहितकेवलचेतनोऽकारलक्ष्यार्थः ।
To explain: Consciousness associated with the gross *upādhi* is the expressed meaning (*vācyārtha*) of the letter 'A'; pure Consciousness devoid of the gross *upādhi* is the indicated meaning (*lakṣyārtha*) of the letter 'A'.
सूक्ष्मोपाधिसहितचेतन उकारवाच्यार्थः ।
Consciousness associated with the subtle *upādhi* is the expressed meaning of the letter 'U'.
सूक्ष्मोपाधिरहितचेतन उकारलक्ष्यार्थः ।
Consciousness devoid of the subtle *upādhi* is the indicated meaning of the letter 'U'.
कारणोपाधिसहितचेतनो मकारवाच्यार्थः ।
Consciousness associated with the causal *upādhi* is the expressed meaning of the letter 'M'.
कारणोपाधिरहितचेतनो मकारलक्ष्यार्थः ।
Consciousness devoid of the causal *upādhi* is the indicated meaning of the letter 'M'.
इत्थमुपाधिसहिता विश्वादयोऽकारादिमात्राणां वाच्यार्थाः ।
Thus, Viśva, Taijasa, and Prājña, endowed with their respective *upādhi*s, are the expressed meanings of the letters 'A' and the rest.
उपाधिरहितः केवलं चेतनः सकलमात्राणां लक्ष्यार्थः ।
Pure Consciousness devoid of adjuncts is the indicated meaning of all the syllables.
तथैव नामरूपात्मकाखिलोपाधिसहितचेतन ओङ्कारवाच्यार्थः ।
In the same way, Consciousness endowed with all adjuncts consisting of name and form is the expressed meaning of *Oṁkāra*.
नामरूपात्मकसकलोपाधिरहितकेवलचेतन ओङ्कारलक्ष्यार्थः ।
Pure Consciousness devoid of all adjuncts consisting of name and form is the indicated meaning of *Oṁkāra*.
इत्थमोङ्कारस्य महावाक्यानां चार्थ एक एव भवति ।
Thus, the meaning of *Oṁkāra* and that of the *mahāvākya*s is precisely one and the same.
तस्मादोङ्कारविवेकेनैवाद्वैतात्मज्ञानं जायते ।
Therefore, non-dual Self-knowledge arises through inquiry into *Oṁkāra* alone.
इत्थमदृष्टिराचार्यवाक्यं श्रुत्वा उपासनायां प्रवृत्तो ज्ञानद्वारा परमपुरुषार्थमोक्षमलभत ।
Hearing the preceptor's teaching in this manner, Adṛṣṭi engaged in meditation and, through knowledge, attained *mokṣa*, the supreme goal of human life.
316 · निर्गुणोपासनानधिकारिणा कर्तव्यम्
यो निर्गुणोपासनेऽनधिकारी स सगुणमीश्वरं 2सदा मनसि धारयेत् ।
He who is unqualified for the meditation on the attributeless (*nirguṇa*) Brahman should constantly hold in his mind the Lord with attributes (*saguṇa-īśvara*).
सगुणोपासनेऽशक्तः निष्कामतया 3नित्यनैमित्तिकानि कर्माण्यनुतिष्ठन्नीश्वरे समर्पयेत् ।
One who is unable to practice *saguṇa* meditation should perform the obligatory daily and occasional actions without desire and dedicate them to the Lord.
कर्मविरामकाले ईश्वरमपि भजेत ।
During the intervals between duties, he should also worship the Lord.
निष्कामकर्म कर्तुमप्यशक्तः सकामः शास्त्रोक्तशुभकर्माण्यनुतिष्ठेत् ।
One who is unable even to perform desireless action should, with desire, perform the auspicious actions prescribed in the scriptures.
तत्राप्यशक्तो यः स शठः पुनः पुनर्जन्ममरणप्रवाहे पतति ।
He who is incapable even of that is a perverse fool and falls again and again into the continuous stream of birth and death.
ओङ्कारार्थविचारेण कृतार्थोऽभूददृष्टिकः ।
By inquiring into the meaning of *oṅkāra*, Adṛṣṭika became fulfilled in purpose.
एतत्तरङ्गपठनात् सुदृष्टिं कुरुते गुरुः ॥1
Through the study of this *taraṅga*, the Guru turns him into one of keen vision (*Sudṛṣṭi*).
टिप्पणी
1.
वेदान्तश्रवणमननरूपविचारे प्रवृत्तो जिज्ञासुस्तं विहाय नान्यत् साधनमनुतिष्ठेत् ।
A seeker who has engaged in the inquiry consisting of hearing and reflecting upon Vedānta should not abandon it to pursue another practice.
वेदान्तविचारशीलः पुरुषो यदि विचारं परित्यज्यान्यत्र प्रसज्यते स आरूढपतितो भवति ।
If a person habituated to Vedāntic inquiry abandons inquiry and engages elsewhere, he becomes one who has fallen after having mounted high (*ārūḍha-patita*).
अथवा करस्थं मधु सन्त्यज्य कूर्परं लेढि मूढधीः इति न्यायस्य विषयो भवति ।
Or rather, he becomes the subject of the maxim: Abandoning the honey present in his hand, the fool licks his elbow.
यः करस्थं मधु प्रमादात्परिस्राव्य मधुना लिप्तं कूर्परं लेढि पश्चात्, तस्य तुल्यो भवति वेदान्तविचारं परित्यज्यान्यत्र प्रसक्तः पुरुषः ।
Just as someone, having carelessly spilled the honey in his hand, later licks his elbow smeared with honey, equal to him is the person who abandons Vedāntic inquiry and engages elsewhere.
तस्माद्वेदान्तविचारशीलः पुरुषः सुदृढबोधोदयपर्यन्तं विचारमेव कुर्यात् ।
Therefore, a person inclined toward Vedāntic inquiry should carry on inquiry alone until firm realization arises.
यस्य विचारे न प्रवृत्तिर्भवति स निर्गुणोपासनं कुर्यात् ।
He who has no inclination toward inquiry should practice meditation on the attributeless (*nirguṇa-upāsanā*).
तत्राप्यशक्तेन उपवासात् वरा भिक्षा इति न्यायेन सगुणोपासनादिकं कर्तव्यं भवेत् ।
If unable even in that, then by the maxim Begging alms is better than starving, *saguṇa* meditation and the like ought to be performed.
2.
मायाविशिष्टचैतन्यरूपं कारणं ब्रह्म सगुणेश्वर इत्युच्यते ।
Causal Brahman, of the nature of Pure Consciousness qualified by *māyā*, is called *saguṇa-īśvara*.
अथवा कारणब्रह्मोपलक्षणभूता हिरण्यगर्भवैश्वानरहरिहरगौरीगणेशार्कादयः कार्यब्रह्मरूपा अपि सगुणेश्वरत्वेन ध्येयाः ।
Or, forms of effect-Brahman (*kārya-brahman*) such as Hiraṇyagarbha, Vaiśvānara, Hari, Hara, Gaurī, Gaṇeśa, Sūrya, and others, which serve as pointers to the causal Brahman, may also be meditated upon as *saguṇa-īśvara*.
अथवा तेषां हरिहरादीनां प्रतीकभूतसालग्रामादयः, तेषां प्रतिमाविशेषाश्च सगुणेश्वरत्वेनोपास्याः ।
Or, their symbols such as the Śālagrāma and their specific icons are to be worshipped as *saguṇa-īśvara*.
पूर्वोक्तेषूपास्येषूत्तरोत्तरापेक्षया पूर्वपूर्वस्योपासनं प्रशस्तं भवति ।
Among the aforementioned objects of worship, the meditation on each preceding one is superior to each succeeding one.
उत्तरत्र सप्तमतरङ्गे वक्ष्यमाणक्रमेण मायाविशिष्टचैतन्यरूपं कारणं ब्रह्मैवेश्वरशब्दस्य मुख्यार्थः ।
Later, according to the order to be explained in the seventh wave, causal Brahman, of the nature of Consciousness qualified by *māyā*, is alone the primary meaning of the word 'Īśvara'.
तदेवोपास्यम् ।
That alone is the principal object of worship.
तथापि मायां तु प्रकृतिं विद्यान्मायिनं तु महेश्वरम् (श्वे. १०) इति श्रुत्या मायाविशिष्टचैतन्यादन्यस्य वस्तुनोऽभावात् श्रीविद्यारण्यस्वामिनः सर्वमताविरोधेन चित्रदीपे ईश्वरस्वरूपमवर्णयन् ।
Even so, because of the absence of any entity apart from Consciousness qualified by *māyā* per the Śruti: Know māyā to be prakṛti, and the wielder of māyā to be the Great Lord (श्वे. १०), Śrī Vidyāraṇya Svāmin in the *Citradīpa* described the nature of the Lord without conflicting with any philosophical system.
तदनुसारेण हिरण्यगर्भादिसर्वमुपास्यवस्तु ईश्वर एवेत्यभिप्रायः ।
In accordance with that, the purport is that every object of meditation, starting from Hiraṇyagarbha, is indeed Īśvara.
3.
फलाभिसन्धिमन्तरा स्वस्ववर्णाश्रमोचितानि कर्माणि केवलमीश्वरार्पणबुद्ध्या कुर्यात् ।
Without desiring results, one should perform the duties appropriate to one's own caste and life-stage purely with the mindset of offering them to the Lord.
कर्मोपरमकाले नामोच्चारणादिरूपमीश्वरभजनं च कुर्यात् ।
And during the cessation of duties, one should worship the Lord in the form of chanting His divine names and so forth.
फलेच्छां विनानुष्ठितमीश्वरे समर्पितं च विहितं कर्मेश्वरप्रसादहेतुर्भवति ।
Prescribed action performed without yearning for fruits and surrendered to the Lord becomes the cause of the Lord's grace.
अतो निष्कामकर्मानुष्ठानमीश्वरभजनरूपमेव भवति ।
Therefore, the practice of desireless action is itself truly a form of worshipping the Lord.
